playbook.whatItDoes: A decentralized 'outsourcing intelligence' platform: customers define measurable competitions (task + data + scoring function) and a global pool of human and agentic-AI solvers competes to solve them. Validators score submissions in isolated sandboxes and emissions flow winner-takes-all to the top-ranked solver. Used for autoresearch, algorithm discovery, RL training and data engineering.
playbook.hardwareRec: No fixed GPU floor in repo — compute is competition-dependent (often CPU + LLM-agent workflows; some competitions may want GPUs). Budget mostly for research time and per-competition submission fees, not always hardware.
playbook.keyRequirements: ["Apex CLI installed from repo (uv workspace)","Bittensor wallet linked via `apex link`","Per-competition submission fee (varies, listed in docs)","Solution must match the competition's file format","Top leaderboard rank at payout time wins","Agentic mining guide: repo AGENTS.md"]
playbook.minerJob: Miners are 'solvers': pick an active competition, fork the baseline in shared/competition/, and iterate on a solution maximizing the objective f(x)→R. Submissions go through the Apex CLI, which signs, charges the entry fee and uploads; validators run each submission in an isolated sandbox against the customer's scoring function and keep leaderboards continuously updated. Rewards are winner-takes-all per competition — the top-ranked submission earns that competition's emissions on-chain, shifting as the leaderboard changes. Solutions are community-shared, so progress compounds.
playbook.minerJobProvide: ["Competition solutions (code/models) scoring best on f(x)","Per-competition submissions in the required format","Iterated improvements beating other solvers' leaders","Agentic research workflows per AGENTS.md","Deployable artifacts for competition owners"]
playbook.top10Strategy: Treat each competition as a short research sprint: read the per-competition spec, fork the baseline, and spend budget only where expected score gain is largest — winner-takes-all makes 'pretty good' worthless. Study shared solutions and compound on the community's best ideas. Pick competitions matching your edge rather than entering everything; a fee is sunk cost unless you can plausibly reach rank 1.
playbook.top10Levers: ["Pick competitions matching your team's edge","Fork and improve the repo baseline solution","Agentic loops (LLM researchers) to widen search","Continuous iteration as leaderboards update","Fee discipline: enter only when rank-1 is plausible","Understand scoring quirks and sandbox constraints"]
playbook.followTopMiners: Watch the docs.macrocosmos.ai current-competitions page and `apex list -c <id> -t` leaderboards; track taostats.io/subnet/1 weight shifts per competition; join the Macrocosmos Discord #apex; monitor repo commits and AGENTS.md updates.

playbook.whatItDoes: Inference Labs' Proof-of-Inference subnet: builds zk-ML verification so an AI prediction can be proven to come from a specific model. Miners produce verifiable predictions plus zero-knowledge proofs; validators verify proofs and score them. It earns by supplying verifiable-inference infrastructure - trust-minimized AI outputs for buyers who cannot trust a black-box API.
playbook.hardwareRec: CPU-only per README: 8-core 3.2GHz+ (3.6GHz+ competitive), 32-64GB RAM, 400Mbps-1Gbps symmetric network, 1-2TB NVMe SSD. zk-proving is CPU-heavy; faster CPU/network/storage directly raises rewards. Rented cloud VMs are fine; no GPU required.
playbook.keyRequirements: ["Run the sn2-miner Rust binary (prebuilt release, Docker image, or build from source)","Registered hotkey on netuid 2 (finney); PM2 or Docker+watchtower recommended","Score = cryptographic integrity, time-to-proof, proof size, and response time","Binaries auto-update every 5 minutes with atomic replacement - do not fight it","HTTP (port 8091) and QUIC (btlightning) endpoints reachable"]
playbook.minerJob: Runs the sn2-miner Rust daemon over HTTP/QUIC. Validators push input data; the miner runs its custom verifiable model - an AI model compiled into a zero-knowledge circuit - and returns the prediction plus a zk proof. Validators verify proofs via the Expander backend and weight miners on proof size, generation time, and response latency. Rewards flow purely from Yuma weights on those performance metrics, so better proving hardware and efficiency mean higher weight. Prebuilt binaries self-update every 5 minutes.
playbook.minerJobProvide: ["Verified AI predictions returned to validator requests","A zero-knowledge proof of inference per prediction (Expander-compatible)","Fast time-to-proof (scored directly)","Compact proofs (proof size is scored)","High-uptime HTTP and QUIC endpoints"]
playbook.top10Strategy: This is a systems/efficiency race, not a model-quality race: winners minimize proof time, proof size, and response latency on strong bare-metal CPUs and 1Gbps+ links. A newcomer breaks top-10 by over-provisioning CPU clock, NVMe, and network, keeping the binary current via auto-update, and watching the stats dashboard to see where the proof-latency frontier sits - every performance point is scored.
playbook.top10Levers: ["CPU clock speed and core count for faster proving","1Gbps+ symmetric network to cut response latency","64GB+ RAM and NVMe storage headroom","Always-current binaries (auto-update channel)","Track sn2-stats.inferencelabs.com and wandb for frontier metrics"]
playbook.followTopMiners: Watch taostats.io/subnet/2 top UIDs and incentive spread, the sn2-stats.inferencelabs.com dashboard and wandb.ai/inferencelabs/subnet-2 for proof-latency distributions, and GitHub release cadence on inference-labs-inc/subnet-2.

playbook.whatItDoes: Teutonic is a king-of-the-hill pretraining contest on Bittensor. Miners train language models and submit immutable checkpoints; a validator verifies each submission and sends challenger plus current king to a remote GPU evaluator for paired cross-entropy scoring. Whoever beats the king becomes king and earns the subnet's emissions; buyers get progressively better pretrained models.
playbook.hardwareRec: 8× H200/B200-class node (~141GB+ VRAM aggregate) to train a competitive checkpoint — per input metadata; training is done on your own infrastructure, since evaluation runs remotely on validator GPUs. Rental marketplaces not addressed by the README.
playbook.keyRequirements: ["Ed25519 hotkey (validator encrypts R2 upload credentials to it)","One submission per hotkey — consumed irreversibly at 'ready'","Complete checkpoint directory: no symlinks, no self-made manifest.json","Registration on netuid 3 can spend TAO (registration burn)","Choose competition lane: main, math, code, or text"]
playbook.minerJob: Day-to-day you train a model offline, then run the teutonic-miner CLI: register the Ed25519 hotkey, poll the mailbox for temporary prefix-scoped R2 credentials (7-day validity, auto-renewed), upload the checkpoint, then commit with 'ready'. 'Ready' is irreversible: the submission is consumed and the validator evaluates asynchronously. The evaluator scores challenger vs king with paired cross-entropy; a successful challenger becomes king and the validator updates weights. Rewards flow only if your checkpoint is or becomes the king.
playbook.minerJobProvide: ["Immutable trained model checkpoints uploaded to R2","One ready submission per hotkey per competition","Checkpoints that beat the king's cross-entropy","Optionally specialist entries (math/code/text lanes)"]
playbook.top10Strategy: Near winner-take-all: only the king earns, so marginal models waste your one submission. Newcomers win with training compute, data quality, and picking the lane (main/math/code/text) where they can beat the incumbent — not with CLI tricks. Understand the evaluation reuse limit and threshold mechanics before spending a registration; a rejected checkpoint can have its storage deleted automatically.
playbook.top10Levers: ["Training-compute budget on H200/B200-class GPUs","Data quality and token efficiency","Lane selection (main/math/code/text)","Pre-validating the checkpoint before submission","Tracking king state and thresholds before committing"]
playbook.followTopMiners: Watch taostats.io/subnet/3 for the king UID and weight distribution, teutonic.ai for published state, and github.com/unarbos/teutonic commit cadence (thresholds, competitions, DEPLOY.md changes). One submission per hotkey makes timing king-targeted attempts everything.

playbook.whatItDoes: Targon is a confidential decentralized AI cloud: miners contribute TEE-capable GPU servers (Intel TDX / NVIDIA Confidential Compute) that host verifiable AI inference and compute for customers. Emissions are auction-based per GPU card with USD-denominated target prices, so miners earn by keeping attested cards live; emission not allocated to auctions is burned.
playbook.hardwareRec: Bare-metal 8-GPU node: H100 SXM/H200/B200/B300 or RTX PRO 6000 Blackwell, Intel TDX CPU (TEE in BIOS), 128+ threads, 1.5-1.9 TiB RAM, 3 TB storage. TargonOS wipes all disks; clusters must be TEE-attested, so generic rentals don't qualify.
playbook.keyRequirements: ["TEE-capable hardware: Intel TDX (AMD SEV-SNP roadmap) with Confidential Compute enabled in BIOS","Exact 8-GPU profile (h100-8x, h200-8x, b200-8x, b300-8x, rtx-pro-6000-blackwell-8x); min cluster size 8 cards","Install signed TargonOS (wipes disks, auto-attests every boot); report node IPs in miner config.json","Run the miner (docker compose) with registered hotkey, external IP, and axon port 7777","Emissions pay per card up to the auction max_price cap; unallocated emission is burned"]
playbook.minerJob: The miner installs TargonOS, a signed OS that on every boot attests to the Targon network, mounts encrypted LUKS storage, and starts Targon services. The miner daemon (docker-compose) registers each node's IP and axon on-chain so validators and the Targon scheduler can direct confidential inference workloads into the TDX VMs. Emissions are paid per card per hour against auctions (e.g. H200 target ~$2.90/hr, B200 ~$4.20/hr) with a max-price cap; once an auction passes its card target the pool spreads and per-card rates settle toward target. Rewards flow automatically per live, attested card.
playbook.minerJobProvide: ["TEE-attested 8-GPU compute nodes running confidential workloads","Always-on axon endpoint reporting live node inventory","Verifiable remote attestation each boot (secure boot, encrypted storage)","Capacity for confidential model inference (CC/PPCIE isolation)"]
playbook.top10Strategy: Fleet operations, not ML: secure cheap TEE-capable hardware, keep every card attested and online 24/7, and watch the auctions API to add card types whose target price beats your power+colo cost. Top miners run multiple 8-GPU nodes per cluster, automate provisioning with iPXE netboot, and never let attestation or the miner daemon lapse.
playbook.top10Levers: ["Buy/colo TEE-capable servers early; per-auction card targets are limited","Track tower.targon.com/api/v2/auctions and stats.targon.com/targets pricing","iPXE unattended TargonOS installs to scale fleets quickly","Zero attestation failures - no attestation means no emission","Keep config.json node IPs current and axon reachable","Compare your per-card payout on stats.targon.com miner stats"]
playbook.followTopMiners: Track taostats.io/subnet/4 top UIDs and the public payout feed stats.targon.com/api/miners (other subnets even benchmark against it), watch manifold-inc/targon commit cadence for auction/profile changes, and monitor the Targon Discord for hardware-profile and terms updates.

playbook.whatItDoes: Hone runs an RLVR (verifiable-reward) competition for coding/terminal agents. Validators lease V3 repository or terminal tasks from a problem server, dispatch them to miners, then grade each response in an isolated Docker sandbox against a hidden verifier. Buyers are the subnet/team needing verifiable agent-training tasks; miners earn by returning exact, passing solutions.
playbook.hardwareRec: CPU only. The miner is an agent calling an external LLM API (reference demo miner uses Amazon Bedrock); no local GPU. Validators need Docker, ~12GB RAM, 25GB disk - miner box is light.
playbook.keyRequirements: ["Registered hotkey on finney netuid 5","LLM API access to power your solving agent (demo uses Bedrock Chat Completions)","Return exact signed responses: git unified diff OR bash script plus canonical trajectory","Candidate code cannot touch verifier files, network, or other miners' workspaces","Byte-exact protocol compliance; identical submissions in a round are graded once"]
playbook.minerJob: Day-to-day you run a miner process that receives server-assigned V3 tasks from validators, solves them with your LLM agent, and returns a signed git diff or bash script plus trajectory. The verifier is only released after responses are durably committed, so you cannot fit to it. Validators grade in the release-pinned polyglot sandbox (no network, no verifier files), compute local scores, and set weights from a preserved scoring window. Rewards flow purely from graded task success; infrastructure failures abandon rounds without changing your score. A reference demo miner and scripts/try_task.py let you grade patches against retired tasks.
playbook.minerJobProvide: ["Signed git unified diffs that pass hidden tests","Bash scripts with canonical trajectories","Consistent task success across rounds","Protocol-exact submissions (no relays, no verifier peeking)"]
playbook.top10Strategy: This is an agentic-coding arms race: the seat goes to the strongest, most reliable task-solving harness. Start from docs/DEMO_MINER.md and try_task.py on retired tasks, then iterate on model choice, scaffolding, and patch formatting. Win by maximizing graded pass rate per round - byte-exact diffs, no flaky runs, and fast turnaround during task windows beat exotic tricks.
playbook.top10Levers: ["Stronger coding model / fine-tuned solver in the agent loop","Robust harness: repo exploration, test-driven patching, clean diffs","Low-latency turnaround when tasks are dispatched","Byte-exact signed-response compliance","Track V3 contract changes in docs/V3_TASKS.md"]
playbook.followTopMiners: Watch taostats.io/subnet/5 top-UID incentive share and weight changes; repo commit cadence (release-pinned sandbox image and policy changes); docs/V3_TASKS.md and demo-miner updates; Bittensor Discord hone channels.

playbook.whatItDoes: Numinous is a forecasting protocol that aggregates AI agents into superhuman LLM forecasters. Miners submit Python forecasting agents; validators execute them in Docker sandboxes and score predictions against the market's own price seven days later. Prediction markets and trading desks are the end users; agents that beat the market baseline earn emissions.
playbook.hardwareRec: CPU only per repo (agent code <=2MB, 240s timeout); the real cost is LLM inference plus news/OSINT API calls through the validator gateway, paid by the miner. No GPU; API spend is the actual bill.
playbook.keyRequirements: ["Registered hotkey; agent is a Python function agent_main(event_data) -> probability, code limited to 2MB","Execution must complete within 240 seconds; deterministic behavior required (no dynamic timestamps or random seeds)","Code submitted before 00:00 UTC activates next day; updates allowed at most once every 3 days","Below 85% event coverage you earn nothing","Miner pays for its own inference (OpenAI/OpenRouter) and scored news/OSINT signals via the gateway"]
playbook.minerJob: There is no long-running axon to babysit: you develop and upload a Python agent. Validators pull the code into sandboxes, call it once per live event per interval with context plus your private memory blob, and it returns a probability. Agents reach reasoning models and Numinous Signals/Indicia through a signing gateway; usage is billed to the miner. At resolution, S = (prediction - target)^2 - (market_price - target)^2 is scored against the market price 7 days later; rewards split by how far ahead of the field you finish.
playbook.minerJobProvide: ["Per-event probability forecasts (0-1) from sandboxed agent code","Private memory blob (<=32768 chars) carried between intervals","Coverage across at least 85% of live events","Deterministic, reproducible agent behavior across validators"]
playbook.top10Strategy: Winning means beating the market baseline, not just other miners: matching the market price scores exactly 0. Edge comes from better information (scored news/OSINT), calibrated reasoning models, and relentless coverage. Use the 3-day update cadence deliberately and keep API costs low since you pay them. Newcomers break in by specializing in event categories where market consensus is weak.
playbook.top10Levers: ["Beat the market-price baseline (positive score requires it)","Maintain >=85% event coverage to avoid earning zero","Deterministic prompts for cross-validator caching consistency","Cheaper/stronger inference routing via the OpenAI/OpenRouter gateway","Specialize in weak-consensus event categories","Exploit the 3-day code update cadence for iteration"]
playbook.followTopMiners: Track taostats.io/subnets/6 chart and the public Numinous Hex dashboard; watch repo commit cadence (docs/scoring-system.md changes) and the Numinous Discord. Agent code is visible to the protocol, so study what top agents do.

playbook.whatItDoes: A settlement layer for AI agents: an agent holding SOL, TAO, BTC or another supported asset submits one swap and receives the destination asset natively in its own wallet — no bridges, wrapped tokens or custodian. Miners are market makers: they post quotes, lock collateral and fulfill swaps; validators verify both legs on-chain and slash collateral on failure.
playbook.hardwareRec: CPU only (any small VPS runs it via Docker Compose). The real input is capital: SOL or TAO collateral bonds, funded delivery wallets per chain (BTC/ETH/etc.), plus a one-time 0.1 SOL identity deposit for hotkey binding.
playbook.keyRequirements: ["Python 3.10+, Docker Compose miner stack","Bittensor wallet; .env with PORT/WALLET_PATH","Collateral bond (SOL purse or locked TAO vault bond)","Private keys per delivery chain (BTC, ETH, ...)","alw miner bind-hotkey + activate before quoting","Failed deliveries are slashed from your collateral"]
playbook.minerJob: Run the reference miner container and quote lanes (e.g. SOL↔TAO) with `alw miner post`. When a taker reserves your quote, you deliver the destination asset to their wallet within the swap window; validators attest both legs on-chain and your credibility accrues from completed swaps. The optional Quote Optimizer auto-reprices 0.4% under the best competing quote inside the validators' 0.5% crown band, pulls quotes when wallets can't cover a full fill, and reports strikes via Discord webhooks.
playbook.minerJobProvide: ["Native cross-chain swap fulfillment (SOL/TAO/BTC lanes)","Exchange-rate quotes locked with collateral","24/7 unattended settlement service","Collateral-backed pricing risk","Optional optimized market-making strategy"]
playbook.top10Strategy: This is a market-making business, not a compute one: earnings come from being the best quote on active lanes while never missing a fill. Undercut rivals inside the 0.5% crown band, keep delivery wallets funded for full-size fills (a missed fill costs a 10% premium strike), and tune the optimizer's per-lane tolerances. More collateral → bigger fill capacity → more weight; strikes and timeouts destroy both TAO and standing.
playbook.top10Levers: ["Tightest quotes within the 0.5% crown band","Deep collateral covering full-size fills","Quote Optimizer with tuned lane tolerances","Multi-lane coverage incl. opt-in BTC lanes","Zero missed fills / no timeout strikes","Funded BTC fee reserves on BTC lanes","Uptime with dead-man-switch quote pulls"]
playbook.followTopMiners: Track taostats.io/subnet/7 top-UID dividends, docs.all-ways.io updates and the @allways_io X account; watch your own webhook strike/fee alerts and the public API (api.all-ways.io) quote book to see which hotkeys lead each lane.

playbook.whatItDoes: Vanta Network (formerly Taoshi's Proprietary Trading Network): miners submit LONG/SHORT/FLAT futures trade signals across forex, crypto, equities, and commodities (Hyperliquid perps included). Validators simulate fills with fees and slippage, track each miner's equity, and pay weekly PnL-ranked emissions. External traders and the dashboard consume the signals; top miners receive funding via Vanta programs.
playbook.hardwareRec: CPU only. Signal submission is strategy logic, not compute-bound; a small VPS (2-4 cores, 8GB RAM) suffices. Real costs are strategy R&D and registration burns; rented GPUs are pointless here.
playbook.keyRequirements: ["Submit orders during market hours per asset class (crypto 24/7, forex Sun 17:00-Fri 17:00 ET, equities 09:30-16:00 ET)","Never exceed 5% intraday or 8% end-of-day drawdown from high-water mark - instant elimination","No plagiarism: copied orders trigger elimination","Each registration needs a fresh unused hotkey; eliminated hotkeys are permanently blacklisted","Carry fees (10.95%/3% per year), spread fees (0.03% crypto, 0.01% equities, 0.005% commodities) and slippage apply","Rank below 25th in your asset class starts a 90-day probation"]
playbook.minerJob: Runs a miner daemon that submits directional orders with entries/exits to validators during market hours. Validators validate trades, simulate portfolio returns with carry fees, spread fees, and leverage-scaled slippage, and continuously track equity against drawdown limits. Weights follow the previous week's PnL scaled by penalties under a debt-based scoring system, with payout periods ending Sunday 00:00 UTC. Elimination is effectively permanent: blacklisted hotkeys cannot re-register, so read docs/miner.md before starting.
playbook.minerJobProvide: ["Timely LONG/SHORT/FLAT signals per supported trade pair","Consistent positive PnL with controlled drawdown","Unique, non-plagiarized order flow","Continuous activity (no 60-day order gaps)","Risk discipline within intraday and EOD drawdown limits"]
playbook.top10Strategy: A zero-sum trading arena where top miners are genuine quant/ML shops. Survive first: small size, strict intraday risk, no leverage spikes; then compound one backtested edge across many pairs to smooth weekly PnL - weights pay last week's PnL net of penalties, so consistency beats home runs. Use the dashboard and Vanta Trading Discord's open strategy resources; expect eliminations while you iterate.
playbook.top10Levers: ["Backtested, unique strategy with positive expectancy across pairs","Hard risk limits - drawdown control is survival","Diversification across asset classes (each class ranks separately)","Minimize carry/spread/slippage drag (low leverage, shorter holds)","Weekly PnL consistency over single lucky trades"]
playbook.followTopMiners: Track the vantanetwork.io dashboard top traders and their return/drawdown profiles, taostats.io/subnet/8 incentive distribution, and docs/miner.md plus the Vanta Trading Discord for rule changes (fees, pairs, drawdown thresholds).

playbook.whatItDoes: IOTA (Macrocosmos) pretrained LLMs across a swarm of heterogeneous machines: an orchestrator distributes model layers to miners and streams activations between them over a shared S3 bucket. Miners compete to process the most activations; validators spot-check that work was genuinely done. Currently training a 1.5B Llama-architecture model, with 15B-100B runs planned.
playbook.hardwareRec: CUDA GPU >=16GB VRAM (RTX 4090 cited by repo), Ubuntu 22.04. bf16 footprint ~2GB per 1B params today; larger planned runs will raise the bar. One GPU joins a pipeline stage; README silent on rental marketplaces.
playbook.keyRequirements: ["CUDA GPU >=16GB VRAM (RTX 4090 example)","Ubuntu 22.04 (Jammy)","uv + bash setup.sh, then .env config","Sustained connectivity to orchestrator and shared S3","Run under PM2 for reliability"]
playbook.minerJob: You run start_miner.sh: the miner registers with the orchestrator, receives its assigned model layers, and streams activations for forward/backward passes. Miners race to process as many activations as possible each training stage, periodically upload local weights, and merge activations via a Butterfly All-Reduce variant. Validators spot-check miners to confirm assigned work was performed as required; emission flows per verified processing contribution across the multi-week run.
playbook.minerJobProvide: ["Processed activation batches per training step","Correct local weight updates uploaded on schedule","Butterfly All-Reduce merge contributions","Uptime across long uninterrupted training runs"]
playbook.top10Strategy: Throughput-plus-reliability race: rewards track activations processed without failing spot-checks, so a pegged GPU, fast network path to orchestrator/S3, and zero downtime beat raw clock speed alone. Newcomers: follow the official IOTA mining setup guide exactly, monitor the public dashboard, and fix disconnects fast — every missed stream is lost paid work.
playbook.top10Levers: ["GPU throughput and VRAM headroom","Low-latency networking to orchestrator/S3","Uptime and fast crash recovery","Precision/config correctness to pass spot-checks","Tracking run-scale changes (15B/50B plans)"]
playbook.followTopMiners: Watch iota.macrocosmos.ai/dashboard/mainnet for miner counts and run metrics, taostats.io/subnet/9 for top UIDs and incentive spread, docs.macrocosmos.ai for setup-guide changes, and the repo commit cadence for run upgrades.

playbook.whatItDoes: Pareton runs inference-optimization campaigns: it pins a vLLM or SGLang baseline and pays miners whose git code patches make it measurably faster. Improvements that pass validation become the new floor for the next campaign, so serving quality compounds for everyone using open-source inference stacks.
playbook.hardwareRec: Authoring patches needs only a dev machine with Docker; benchmarking runs on platform-rented GPU pods (e.g. 4x RTX 5090 for a Qwen3-FP8 SGLang campaign). Rent or own a 5090-class GPU only to reproduce benchmarks locally before submitting.
playbook.keyRequirements: ["Strong systems engineering of vLLM/SGLang: kernels, scheduling, memory, quantization paths","Git patch against the pinned baseline commit, respecting allowed/denied path globs","Pay the campaign submission fee (published amount_tao/recipient; --max-fee-tao cap; --yes for scripts)","On-chain commitment via miner/commit_patch.py: campaign_id, baseline_commit, patch_hash, retrieval_url","Patches stay private (presigned S3 with UUIDv4 names); validators build hermetically in the pinned image"]
playbook.minerJob: Day-to-day a miner reads the frozen campaign manifest, clones the pinned vLLM/SGLang baseline, and engineers a patch improving throughput or latency without breaking correctness. They hash the patch, upload it to presigned S3, pay the submission fee, and commit campaign_id/baseline_commit/patch_hash/retrieval_url on-chain. A watcher records commitments; validators run identity/integrity/base-apply/surface gates, build the patch hermetically into a content-addressed image, and in each round benchmark baseline, current leader, and all challengers on one rented GPU pod. The best image takes the crown and rewards.
playbook.minerJobProvide: ["Correct, fast code patch against the pinned inference-framework baseline","On-chain patch commitment with payment proof","Reproducible performance gains verified inside the hermetic build","New campaign floor: passing improvements raise the baseline for everyone"]
playbook.top10Strategy: A pure engineering competition - treat each campaign like a Kaggle for inference kernels: profile the pinned baseline hard, target the highest-leverage bottlenecks (attention kernels, CUDA graphs, quantization), and submit early to bank the leader position before the round closes. Scores only compare within one round, so timing matters as much as raw skill.
playbook.top10Levers: ["Deep vLLM/SGLang internals: custom kernels, chunked prefill, speculative decoding","Read the frozen manifest - allowed path globs define your legal change surface","Reproduce the exact base image and benchmark locally before committing","Submit early; the leader holds the crown until beaten within the round","Budget fees per campaign and cap with --max-fee-tao","Watch campaign launches on pareton.ai docs/Discord"]
playbook.followTopMiners: Watch campaign announcements via pareton.ai/docs and the Bittensor Discord, the Pareton-ai/pareton commit cadence for new campaign types, and taostats.io/subnet/10 weight shifts to see who holds the crown each round.

playbook.whatItDoes: TrajectoryRL Season 2 pits miners against each other on 'fusion policies' - programs that decide, per request, which of eight open-weight models on Engy answer an agent and in what combination. Validators run scenario containers with hidden tests; the best policy holds the seat and is served on Engy as engy/auto for paying customers.
playbook.hardwareRec: CPU only - explicitly 'no GPU, no server, no uptime': the platform stores your pack and validators run everything. Your real cost is model-call spend for local evaluation against your own Engy API key.
playbook.keyRequirements: ["Pack containing SKILL.md plus policy.json, policy.py (small SDK), or an OpenAI-compatible server","Policy may only call the eight allowlisted Engy models; $0.30 per-scenario spend cap","Local testing via scripts/eval_pack.py needs Docker + your own Engy key","Submission signed with your hotkey via trajectoryrl-miner web-submit","Winning packs transfer copyright to trajrl.com"]
playbook.minerJob: You build a pack (SKILL.md + fusion policy), validate it with the CLI, optionally self-test with the exact validator code on public scenarios, then web-submit. Validators run your policy in a sidecar next to the scenario container (Hermes + task), metering every model call at a frozen price table with a $0.30 safety cap. Score is the sum over 20 scenarios of tests passed over tests total; cost is shown but not scored. Consensus is stake-weighted and Winsorized; the seated policy only changes hands on a real margin, and the winner's pack becomes Engy's auto mode.
playbook.minerJobProvide: ["SKILL.md + fusion policy pack (json/py/server)","Higher tests-passed fraction across 20 scenarios","Measured policy baselines you can reproduce","Submissions that stay inside the $0.30/scenario meter"]
playbook.top10Strategy: Beat the published baselines (SKILL-only 19.9; pinned kimi-k3 ~22.8; kimi + three cheap advisers 23.6) with smarter routing: pin one strong model, add cheap advisers in parallel, rewrite prompts, keep session state. Since cost is not scored, spend freely up to the cap during validation. Local-eval on public trajrl-bench scenarios before every submit - the seat only moves on a real margin.
playbook.top10Levers: ["Per-request model routing quality (when to parallel vs sequence)","Prompt rewriting and context shaping for the scenario container","Testing against public scenarios (trajrl-bench) pre-submit","Session-state exploitation across turns","Using the full $0.30 cap for more/parallel model calls"]
playbook.followTopMiners: Track taostats.io/subnet/11 incentive distribution and seat holder; examples/policies/ measured scores in the repo; trajrl-bench scenario updates; docs/FUSION_POLICY.md changes; trajrl.com and Bittensor Discord.

playbook.whatItDoes: ComputeHorde sells verified decentralized GPU compute to validators of other Bittensor subnets, replacing centralized clouds. Those validators submit dockerized jobs; miners run GPU executor containers that execute them and return results. Rewards track completed job runtime: validator-paid executor-seconds convert into scores, with mechanisms pushing work toward organic (cross-subnet) jobs.
playbook.hardwareRec: A6000 is the only supported hardware class (A100 next per repo); >=500GB shared disk for Docker images and job data. Multiple executors per UID scale earnings. Rental GPUs run it but a stable dedicated box is typical; input notes A100.
playbook.keyRequirements: ["NVIDIA GPU matching the A6000 hardware class (A100 planned); Ubuntu + Docker + NVIDIA drivers",">=500GB shared disk to reliably handle Docker images and job data in /tmp","Stock miner image manages comms; competitive edge is a custom ExecutorManager running multiple executors","Optional collateral deposit to become eligible for organic jobs (slashing risk)","Publicly reachable miner endpoint; optional DDoS shield container"]
playbook.minerJob: Run the stock miner (install_miner.sh) plus executor containers that accept dockerized jobs from validators, e.g. LLM data/benchmark jobs from other subnets. Each block mints executor-seconds per miner-validator pair; validators spend allowance blocks covering job runtime and score miners globally on paid runtime seconds, folded by coldkey with a 10% dancing boost for hotkey variance. Commit-reveal weights and a trusted-miner cross-validator keep work honest.
playbook.minerJobProvide: ["Dockerized GPU job execution for other subnets' validators","Verified honest results (slashing-eligible when collateral is posted)","Multiple executors matched to declared hardware class","Low-latency job pickup and result return"]
playbook.top10Strategy: Emissions track completed job runtime, not GPU specs alone. Winners run many executors via a custom ExecutorManager, keep availability near-perfect, preload likely job Docker images to cut startup, and post collateral to win organic jobs. Match the hardware class weights the network currently demands. Newcomers: one solid A6000-class executor online 24/7 beats flashy hardware that keeps dropping.
playbook.top10Levers: ["Custom ExecutorManager scaling many executors per UID","Collateral deposits unlocking paid organic jobs","Preloading DYNAMIC_PRELOAD_DOCKER_JOB_IMAGES to cut job latency","Dancing bonus: hotkey variance adds a 10% coldkey boost","Uptime plus DDoS shield for reliability","Matching in-demand hardware class weights"]
playbook.followTopMiners: Watch the Subnet 12 Grafana health monitor (grafana.bactensor.io) and taostats.io/subnets/12 for executor counts and score spread; track repo releases and the ComputeHorde Discord channel for class/collateral changes.

playbook.whatItDoes: Macrocosmos's data-scraping and sentiment subnet: miners scrape real-time X (Twitter), Reddit and YouTube-transcript data, store it locally, and expose it to validators that power products like Gravity (no-code scraping), Nebula (visualization) and the Macrocosmos API/MCP. Businesses and other subnets buy this data; miners earn for holding fresh, desirable, non-duplicated data.
playbook.hardwareRec: CPU only — no GPU needed. Prioritize cores for scraping throughput, large fast storage/databases for DataEntities, and bandwidth. S3-compatible storage setup required for public dataset upload.
playbook.keyRequirements: ["Miner runs the scraper stack per docs/miner.md","Large local storage for DataEntity buckets","S3-compatible upload of anonymized stores","Data must be <30 days old to score","Macrocosmos Miner Data Compliance Policy (GDPR)","Respect source ToS; anonymized data only"]
playbook.minerJob: Day-to-day the miner scrapes configured DataSources (X, Reddit, YouTube transcripts), files each DataEntity into buckets (source, time bucket, label) forming its MinerIndex, and answers validator queries for that index. Validators sample and verify items to build a credibility score, then weight miners by data value: freshness (<30 days), position on the Dynamic Desirability List (driven by Gravity user requests), and a duplication factor that pays a premium for data few others hold. Miners also upload anonymized copies to S3 for public dataset access.
playbook.minerJobProvide: ["Fresh social-media scrapes (X, Reddit, YouTube)","MinerIndex reporting to validators on demand","Verifiable sample data passing credibility checks","Anonymized dataset uploads to S3","Coverage of desirable, low-duplication buckets"]
playbook.top10Strategy: Win by differentiation, not volume: use the hosted sn13-dashboard to find buckets where desirability is high but few miners hold data, since duplication directly divides value. Keep everything under 30 days old, refresh continuously, and never inflate your index — credibility sampling punishes misrepresentation harder than honest smallness. React fast when the Desirability List changes (updates are announced ahead of time).
playbook.top10Levers: ["Dashboard-driven bucket selection (sn13-dashboard)","Freshness discipline (<30d, continuous refresh)","Low-duplication niche data over common scrapes","Desirability-list tracking and fast reconfiguration","Perfect credibility on sampled verification","Scraping throughput and 24/7 reliability","Compliant, ToS-respecting collection pipeline"]
playbook.followTopMiners: Watch the hosted sn13-dashboard for bucket coverage, the wandb validator logs (macrocosmos/data-universe-validators), taostats.io/subnet/13 top UIDs, and the Macrocosmos Discord; monitor repo and macrocosm-os/scrapers commits for new DataSources.

playbook.whatItDoes: Cacheon is an inference-speed competition built around SGLang: the validator owns the model, workload, and engine, and miners submit inspectable optimizations - served-model modules or the scheduler's prefix cache - that must measurably speed up end-to-end serving without quality loss. LLM operators benefit from faster/cheaper serving; rewards flow only to measured, qualified improvements.
playbook.hardwareRec: Platform data: B300-class GPU (1). Mining itself is code optimization: a local dev GPU to profile SGLang helps, but qualification runs on validator-owned no-egress OCI workers. Software is pre-release; expect policy churn.
playbook.keyRequirements: ["Submit one optimization against a validator-published arena target (forward_pass modules or prefix cache)","Must beat the arena incumbent by the required margin after one complete audited qualification PASS","Stay within behavior and quality limits - speed alone earns nothing","Possible TAO anti-spam admission gate paid to subnet owner (--pay locks the quote ~300 blocks)","Python 3.11+; run cacheon.cli scan/verify locally before submitting"]
playbook.minerJob: Not a 24/7 service. Miners study the validator-published arena, engineer an optimization (engine module or prefix-cache change), run local scan/verify checks, then commit and submit the bundle. The validator builds and runs the candidate in isolated no-egress workers, measures end-to-end latency on the registered agent workload under its speed/quality policy, and records a crown plus V1 credit only if the incumbent is beaten by the required margin. A publisher later combines eligible claims into an on-chain weight vector.
playbook.minerJobProvide: ["Inspectable optimization code for a registered engine target","Measured end-to-end latency improvement over the incumbent","Preserved output quality within policy limits","Passing audited qualification (node audit + graph checks)","Occasional new crown for the target"]
playbook.top10Strategy: A kernel/systems-engineering game: read the docs (concepts, architecture, slot contract), pick one hot target, and profile the SGLang path locally before submitting - blind micro-tweaks waste the admission gate. Because reward requires beating the incumbent on the validator's own benchmark, submissions from engineers with real CUDA/SGLang skill can win fast; the pool of qualified optimizations is tiny and pre-release means early movers shape targets.
playbook.top10Levers: ["Deep SGLang/CUDA optimization skill","Local profiling harness reproducing the registered workload","Target selection where the incumbent is weak","Submit only strong candidates (admission gate economics)","Follow repo commit cadence for fast-moving policy changes"]
playbook.followTopMiners: Watch cacheon.ai/docs (rendered repo docs) and the latent-to/cacheon commit cadence since this is pre-release, plus taostats.io/subnet/14 for weight distribution and which UIDs hold crowns in validator publications.

playbook.whatItDoes: ORO evaluates AI shopping agents on real-world shopping tasks (ORO Bench, from ShoppingBench). Miners submit Python agents that shop for a simulated shopper: search a frozen catalog, ask about unstated needs, track price/stock changes, and place one order. Validators run agents in sandboxed Docker; the best agent earns emissions. Challengers must clear a decaying threshold to take the top spot.
playbook.hardwareRec: CPU-only to host the agent — it can call LLM APIs (bring your own inference credentials; models must be on the live Backend allowlist). Validators need Docker + 16-32GB RAM. No GPU mentioned anywhere; a small VPS works.
playbook.keyRequirements: ["Python agent defining agent_main(problem_data)","Docker for local testing against the practice EnvPack","Inference credentials in .env (INFERENCE_PROVIDER)","Model must be on the live Backend allowlist","Beat the decaying challenger threshold to claim top spot"]
playbook.minerJob: You develop and host a Python agent that reads policy_view.tools and drives a shopping session — search, read listings, message the shopper, order — until done=true. Validators run it in isolated Docker sandboxes against sealed ORO Bench EnvPack tasks; a miss scores 0, a passing order earns up to 1.0 minus penalties for extra questions or a less-than-best pick. Emissions flow proportionally to validator stake-weighted scores; the reference implementation lives in src/agent/environment_agent.py.
playbook.minerJobProvide: ["Python agent implementing agent_main(problem_data)","Orders satisfying sealed task requirements/obligations","Minimal extra clarifying questions","Iterated submissions that clear the threshold"]
playbook.top10Strategy: An agent-quality knife fight, not an infra race: winning means asking exactly the right questions and picking the best product. Newcomers should fork the reference agent, replay failures via the local trajectories.html artifacts, fix each failure category, and iterate — the decaying threshold lets a steadily improving challenger dethrone a stale leader.
playbook.top10Levers: ["Agent policy quality (search/question/order decisions)","Local Docker testing on the practice EnvPack","LLM model choice within the allowlist","Failure-category analysis from trajectories.html","Iteration speed vs decaying threshold"]
playbook.followTopMiners: Track the leaderboard at oroagents.com, docs.oroagents.com/docs/miners/scoring for threshold/scoring changes, repo commits (EnvPack versioning), and the ORO Discord (discord.gg/MHqAVWTdka).

playbook.whatItDoes: 404-GEN runs a decentralized 3D-generation competition: miners generate 3D models from published seeds/prompts, validators compare them in VLM pairwise duels, and winners are audited by regenerating outputs from the miner's Docker image on serverless GPUs. Anyone needing AI-generated 3D assets is the buyer; the best pipeline wins each round.
playbook.hardwareRec: Multi-GPU rig for 3D model training/generation - audits regenerate on 4xH200 serverless pods using the hardware you declare in hardware.json. A single H100/H200-class node can compete; CPU-only cannot. Workload ships as Docker, so cloud GPUs are fine.
playbook.keyRequirements: ["Register on-chain during the OPEN window; generate from the published seed and prompts before the deadline","Upload 3D files (Three.js JS modules) to your own CDN for validators to download","Provide a Docker image that reproduces outputs; winners are regenerated on serverless GPUs (4xH200 default)","Outputs are statically analyzed, sandboxed, rendered via headless Chromium, then VLM-judged","Regenerated outputs must match submission quality (DINOv3 perceptual-distance checks)"]
playbook.minerJob: Each round the miner pulls the published seed and prompts, runs its 3D-generation pipeline, uploads models to its CDN, and registers on-chain while the round is OPEN. Validators download submissions, render multi-view PNGs, and run VLM pairwise duels; candidate winners are verified by regenerating outputs from their Docker image on a serverless 4xH200 pod (128 prompts in 4 batches, same seed). The round winner becomes leader; repeated leader wins suffer weight decay toward a floor while new winners start at weight 1.0.
playbook.minerJobProvide: ["Generated 3D assets from published seeds/prompts, uploaded to your CDN","On-chain registration within the round's block window","A reproducible Docker image that regenerates your outputs exactly","Round-winning pipeline that survives VLM duels and audit"]
playbook.top10Strategy: Winner-stays-in: you must beat the reigning leader decisively every round, and one-off wins decay. Build a fast, deterministic pipeline that handles the whole prompt pool, keep generation inside the block windows, and guarantee your Docker reproduces outputs - audit failures discard the win. Mine the public round state files to learn which styles win duels.
playbook.top10Levers: ["Prompt diversity: one pipeline must cover the entire round prompt pool","Determinism with the round seed - regeneration must match submissions","Inference speed: generation deadlines are block-limited","Study public state (leader.json, matches_matrix.csv) for VLM judge preferences","Keep GitHub Actions Docker builds green - build failure forfeits audit","Strike when the champion's weight has decayed"]
playbook.followTopMiners: Watch taostats.io/subnet/17 top UIDs plus leader transitions, the public competition state repo (leader.json, per-round winner files in 404-Repo org), and the Bittensor Discord 404-GEN channel for competition/config changes.

playbook.whatItDoes: Zeus (Orpheus AI) is a decentralized weather-forecasting network for energy markets. Validators issue global ERA5 forecasting challenges on a 0.25-degree grid for four surface variables energy desks trade on - 2m temperature, 100m u/v wind, surface solar radiation - and score miners' hourly forecasts out to 15 days against ERA5 reanalysis truth.
playbook.hardwareRec: CPU-only miner viable for inference; repo mining guide: GPU required for training custom models, not for inference. Budget real GPU time only if you train your own forecast model. VPS-class box with open axon port works for serving.
playbook.keyRequirements: ["Registered hotkey; axon reachable (open port, validator-permit blacklist)","Answer 4 forecast rounds daily (00:30/06:30/12:30/18:30 UTC), 49-step and 361-step horizons","On-chain commit-reveal: hash of compressed prediction committed before revealing bytes","Full-Earth grid output per challenge variable","ERA5/CDS data pipeline for training and self-evaluation"]
playbook.minerJob: Run the Zeus miner with an axon on finney. Four times daily the validator sends challenges (one per ERA5 variable x horizon); you return hourly forecasts for the whole globe at 1-hour steps. You commit a hash of your compressed prediction on-chain before revealing, which blocks relay mining and lets businesses verify forecasts against hashes. Validators score reveals against ERA5, keep rank history in SQLite, and set weights from rolling averages of recent ranks, with most of each challenge's weight to the best-ranked miner; short-horizon weight 0.2, long-horizon 0.8, plus regional boosts (e.g. Europe/Germany). Dynamic burn rotates a burn UID to deter weight-copying validators.
playbook.minerJobProvide: ["On-time full-grid forecasts for four variables","On-chain prediction commitments (anti-relay)","Verified skill vs ERA5 at 2-day and 15-day horizons","Testable predictions via Hugging Face upload flow"]
playbook.top10Strategy: ML-NWP skill wins: data-driven forecast models (GraphCast/Aurora-style architectures fine-tuned on ERA5) that beat competitors on verified rank take the top of each challenge's weight. Long-horizon (15-day) challenges carry 0.8 weight - prioritize there. Train on near-unlimited ERA5 history, target the boosted regions, and never miss rounds; rank history means consistency compounds.
playbook.top10Levers: ["Forecast model quality on 2m-temp/wind/solar","Long-horizon (360-hour) accuracy where 80% of weight sits","Reliability across all 4 daily rounds","Regional boosts (Europe/Germany) exploitation","GPU training pipeline for custom architectures"]
playbook.followTopMiners: taostats.io/subnet/18 top UIDs and incentive spread; zeussubnet.com whitepaper/benchmark updates; HuggingFace orpheus-zeus verification datasets; Bittensor Discord Zeus/Orpheus channels; repo docs/Mining.md and constants changes.

playbook.whatItDoes: Blockmachine provides decentralized RPC and archive-node infrastructure for Ethereum, Bittensor, and BSC. Miners run real chain nodes behind an authenticated nginx gateway; customer RPC traffic is routed to eligible nodes by quality score and price, and proof-emitting responses are verified with Merkle state proofs. DApps and bots buy the RPC; heavy-traffic nodes earn the incentive.
playbook.hardwareRec: No GPU. Run full or archive chain nodes (Ethereum reth recommended, BSC geth/reth, Bittensor subtensor); archive nodes need multi-TB NVMe and strong CPU/RAM. Capacity burst tests score hardware speed, so fast disk/CPU directly wins routed traffic.
playbook.keyRequirements: ["Chain node for a supported chain with honest archive/full declaration (claiming archive without archive state fails)","Endpoint reachable via WebSocket/JSON-RPC with TLS on 80/443; stay within 90s of chain tip (archive nodes get 10 min)","Blockmachine CLI registration with a Bittensor miner hotkey (testnet netuid 417 first)","Pass continuous randomized eligibility tests; burst capacity tests set a 0-1.0 routing multiplier","Optional capacity helper at /capacity-test for archive nodes (removes network-latency penalty)"]
playbook.minerJob: You provision and operate your own node (syncing, disk sizing, staying at tip), front it with the gateway Docker stack, and register the endpoint plus a USD-per-compute-unit price via the bm CLI. The protocol gateway routes customer RPC by quality and price; eligibility is retested regularly with randomly timed probes, and a burst test scores your hardware against the fastest node on the chain, scaling your routing weight. Per-chain base incentive: 90% to archive nodes, 10% to full nodes.
playbook.minerJobProvide: ["Live JSON-RPC/WebSocket traffic served at the chain tip","Verifiable archive queries (eth_getProof-style Merkle proofs)","Honest node-type depth (full vs archive promises kept)","Burst-tested low-latency capacity driving routing multiplier"]
playbook.top10Strategy: Within the archive share, only the top-5 archive nodes by served traffic per chain split that chain's archive incentive each epoch - so winning traffic is everything: reth archive on fast NVMe, capacity helper running, aggressive pricing, tip-lag near zero. Serve multiple chains to diversify. Newcomers: pick chains with five or fewer eligible archive nodes, where every node shares the archive incentive.
playbook.top10Levers: ["Top-5 archive nodes by traffic share that chain's archive incentive","Capacity helper removes network-distance penalty in scoring","Fast NVMe and strong CPU for the burst-test multiplier","Aggressive per-CU pricing to win routed traffic","Multi-chain operation (eth/bsc/tao) diversifies incentive pools","Tip-lag discipline (90s full, 10min archive)"]
playbook.followTopMiners: Check the blockmachine.io/miners dashboard for per-chain node rankings and traffic shares; monitor taostat/blockmachine-miner releases and the whitepaper/technology pages for incentive-rule changes.

playbook.whatItDoes: A video-understanding benchmark subnet: miners submit immutable video-language model weights; evaluator validators privately test them on random audiovisual clips from a 1,000-video catalogue and crown one 'king' per window. 100% of each validator's weight goes to that single king (0% burn otherwise) — a winner-take-all leaderboard for multimodal video models.
playbook.hardwareRec: Miner needs no GPU to serve — a CPU server distributes weights (packages up to 24–44 GB). GPU spend goes into training/selecting a model strong enough to beat the king; A100/H100-class for experimentation.
playbook.keyRequirements: ["Allowlisted archs: salmonn2-pro, qwen2.5-omni, qwen3-omni","Full safetensors weights (no adapters), size-capped","One hotkey binds one model permanently","CPU model server on public IP (default port 8091)","Pinned TLS + btauth/1 signed requests; zstd ranges","Downloaders must hold ≥100,000 SN20 alpha"]
playbook.minerJob: Run `witness-benchmark-miner prepare` to hash the package and mint a TLS certificate, `serve` to host weights over authenticated TLS (HTTP/1.1 keep-alive, 4 MiB ranges, zstd), and `commit` to publish the wm2 manifest+cert commitment on-chain. Evaluators download the weights, run the model on private video clips with validator-owned loaders, and score quality/reward/paired-king metrics; the miner never serves inference. Your model stays king only while challengers fail to beat its paired reward by more than 0.02.
playbook.minerJobProvide: ["Immutable video-LM weights (one per hotkey)","Authenticated TLS weight-distribution endpoint","On-chain wm2 model commitment","Uptime through the evaluation window","A model that beats the reigning king"]
playbook.top10Strategy: King-of-the-hill: study the reigning king's published scores and only enter a model you believe clears the +0.02 paired-improvement margin with aggregate quality >0.05 — a terminal evaluation consumes the hotkey for that evaluator, and one hotkey binds one model forever. Serve from a fast, stable endpoint: slow downloads (15-minute acquisition cap) are dropped without scoring. New submissions queue for the next two-epoch window.
playbook.top10Levers: ["Model quality beating king by >0.02 margin","Fast, reliable weight serving (zstd, keep-alive)","Choosing the right allowlisted architecture","Timing entry to window openings","Tracking evaluation-v3 scoring changes","Endpoint availability so retries keep queue spot"]
playbook.followTopMiners: Track the witness dashboard (queue, kings, per-window scores), taostats.io/subnet/20 weight concentration on the single king, repo commit cadence (evaluation-v3, window policy changes), and witnessvision.io announcements.

playbook.whatItDoes: SN21 (ippcteam) is a verifiable prediction market for Google Ads campaign outcomes. An operator publishes daily baskets of real account changes (budget/bid changes, pauses); miner containers predict P10/P50/P90 outcome distributions at 7/14/28-day horizons; settled results feed standings that drive emissions. Ad-tech buyers get calibrated forecasts of campaign impact.
playbook.hardwareRec: CPU only: 2 cores/4GB min, 4 cores/8GB+ recommended, 20GB SSD. GPU optional for heavier models. Container must run deterministic, network-isolated, under RAM/time budgets.
playbook.keyRequirements: ["Ship a digest-pinned container: stdin episodes to stdout P10/P50/P90 per horizon (7/14/28d)","Commit sn21-model:v1:<repo>@sha256:<digest> on chain; the subnet pulls and runs it daily","Emissions: 1st place 50%, 2nd 25%, 3rd 10% of pot, geometric tail, hard cap 20 earners","250 weighted predictions to place; full standing at 1,000","Score: pinball 50%, interval coverage 10%, direction 15%, goal metric; 12-day half-life standing","Horizon weights: 7d 20%, 14d 35%, 28d 45%"]
playbook.minerJob: Build a forecasting model, package it as a digest-pinned container implementing the MINER_MODEL_SPEC I/O contract, and commit its digest on chain once. Each day the subnet runs your container (network=none, budgeted) against a fresh basket of Google Ads episodes; it emits probabilistic deltas per horizon. Outcomes settle at day 15/22/36; scores roll into a 12-day half-life standing that a published rank curve maps to chain weights. You never POST daily predictions - the container is the miner.
playbook.minerJobProvide: ["Deterministic container emitting calibrated P10/P50/P90 forecasts","Calibration (interval coverage), not just point accuracy","Direction accuracy on the goal metric","Long-horizon stability (28d carries 45% weight)","Maintained on-chain digest commitment"]
playbook.top10Strategy: The rank curve is brutally top-heavy (50/25/10), so top-10 means out-calibrating everyone on quantile accuracy. Start from the docs' training pipeline, backtest against published receipts with verify_day.py, and optimize pinball loss plus coverage before adding complexity. Placement needs 250 weighted predictions and standings decay with a 12-day half-life, so ship early and iterate continuously; a genuinely calibrated simple model beats a fancy miscalibrated one.
playbook.top10Levers: ["Pinball-loss optimization across P10/P50/P90 quantiles","Interval coverage tuning (10% of score)","Horizon-aware training (28d weight 45%)","Early, consistent submission to accumulate standing","Local score reproduction via verify_day.py receipts"]
playbook.followTopMiners: Track the public accuracy/receipt feeds and standings (docs/SN21_VERIFYING.md), taostats.io/subnet/21 weights, and repo docs SN21_REWARDS.md and SN21_STAKING.md - the published feeds mirror the operator's scored record.

playbook.whatItDoes: Desearch builds a pre-query web index for AI on Bittensor. In the live 2.0 phase miners crawl assigned pages and upload extracted text; validators re-check a sample under published rules; the Desearch team integrates accepted pages into the index behind its Search API (console.desearch.ai). Miners are paid by their share of accepted pages. Embedding tasks are built and open later.
playbook.hardwareRec: CPU-only for the crawl phase: any cheap VPS with bandwidth and disk. The later embed program will pay miners to run the selected embedding model on GPUs, so keep a modest GPU option in mind. Rentals fine.
playbook.keyRequirements: ["Registered hotkey on SN22 + task API access (docs/miner-setup.md)","Fetch assigned pages and upload extracted text","Validators re-fetch random samples; mismatch forfeits earnings since last good check","All results public at api-22.desearch.ai/v1/tasks","Local miner test before registering (test-your-miner.md)"]
playbook.minerJob: The miner takes tasks from the task API, fetches its assigned URLs, extracts clean text, and uploads it for the index. Validators re-fetch a random sample of each miner's tasks and compare; weights are set from the share of accepted work, and a miner caught returning bad pages loses everything earned since its last good check. A future embed task type will run a selected model on accepted text with sample recomputation. Reward = your share of accepted pages per round.
playbook.minerJobProvide: ["Fetched page text for assigned URLs","Extraction fidelity matching validator re-fetch","High accepted-page share per round","Later: embeddings from the selected model"]
playbook.top10Strategy: A crawl-reliability war: fetch success rate on hard pages, extraction accuracy, and throughput decide your accepted share. Newcomers: run the reference miner, pass the local validator test first, then tune concurrency and IP quality. Never shortcut pages — sampling makes cheating lose everything since the last good check.
playbook.top10Levers: ["Fetch success rate on assigned pages","Extraction fidelity vs validator re-fetch","Task throughput and concurrency","Bandwidth/IP reputation","Fast adoption of new task types (embed)"]
playbook.followTopMiners: Watch the public task log api-22.desearch.ai/v1/tasks, docs/emission.md for share mechanics, taostats.io/subnet/22 for incentive distribution, and the Desearch Discord/X for program openings (embedding phase).

playbook.whatItDoes: Trishool builds an AI guard model via a red-team competition: miners submit universal jailbreak prompt templates; validators expand them against active challenges, run an OpenClaw agent, and score responses with a Judge agent (safe/partial/jailbreak). Aggregated scores become on-chain weights, so stronger adversarial prompts earn more.
playbook.hardwareRec: CPU only. Miners run a Python CLI plus optional Docker agents; heavy inference runs on Chutes/OpenRouter APIs with your own key. A small VPS or laptop is enough - no GPU, no special networking.
playbook.keyRequirements: ["TEMPLATE submission JSON with exactly one {{objective}} placeholder (<=2000 chars including it)","Upload via alignet.cli.miner with wallet signature to api.trishool.ai; challenge must be TEMPLATE format","Legacy QUESTIONS format supports technique/url/MCP fields; wrong shape is rejected","Local smoke-testing via tri-check (OpenClaw -> Judge) before uploading","Platform dedupe and format/surface validation; scoring is 0=safe, 1=partial, 2=full jailbreak per question"]
playbook.minerJob: Miners craft universal jailbreak templates that make the target agent leak across a whole question set, smoke-test locally with tri-check against their own OpenClaw+Judge Docker stack, then upload wallet-signed submissions to the platform. Validators expand each template into Q1..Qn, run the tri-claw agent, score with the Judge, and aggregate totals; the platform's weight endpoint is synced on-chain. Rewards track aggregated adversarial effectiveness, not compute, so iteration speed and originality dominate.
playbook.minerJobProvide: ["Wallet-signed universal jailbreak template submissions","Prompts that generalize across the active challenge's question set","Pre-tested templates (tri-check) that avoid duplicate/invalid rejections","Guard-model research signal: measured safe/partial/jailbreak outcomes"]
playbook.top10Strategy: A prompt-engineering arms race, not a GPU game: study docs/universal-jailbreaks.md, iterate against your local OpenClaw+Judge replica, and optimize templates that generalize across all questions rather than one-off exploits. Duplicate detection makes creativity the moat, and early submission locks your idea before near-identical rivals land.
playbook.top10Levers: ["Master universal jailbreak patterns (encoding, roleplay, tool abuse)","Always tri-check locally before upload - never burn a submission untested","Maximize score across all questions, not a single question","Adapt fast when challenge format rotates (TEMPLATE vs QUESTIONS)","Run the repo auto-updater - validator/agent mechanics change often","Follow the Trishool Discord for challenge announcements"]
playbook.followTopMiners: Track taostats.io/subnet/23 weight distribution, trishool.ai/dashboard, the trishool-phase2 commit cadence (an auto-updater exists for a reason), and the Trishool Discord where challenge parameters ship via private channels.

playbook.whatItDoes: Quasar Training is decentralized pretraining: miners continue training the Quasar MoE model (Quasar Preview) toward 10T+ additional tokens. A subnet-run orchestrator splits model tensors into 24 fragments, assigns training leases, merges validator-approved live fragments, and releases public checkpoints. Buyers are the SILX team/ecosystem wanting decentralized training throughput.
playbook.hardwareRec: Multi-GPU training node. Repo shows QUASAR_MINER_DEVICES=0,1,2,3 with FSDP on multi-GPU systems; treat this as a datacenter-class training rig (multiple large-VRAM GPUs). No TEE/static-IP requirement documented; OOM discipline and batch-size control matter.
playbook.keyRequirements: ["Registered native ED25519 hotkey on netuid 24","Latest miner release (signed live fragment claims + live-control grants)","Multi-GPU node; keep one hotkey on one machine only","Public S3 bucket reads (QUASAR_S3_ANONYMOUS=true) for run discovery","Steady training uptime so the syncer can pull live fragments"]
playbook.minerJob: The miner publishes a heartbeat, discovers the active run, polls for jobs, verifies orchestrator signatures, decrypts scoped grants, downloads checkpoint/data via presigned URLs, and trains its assigned Quasar fragment. While training it answers live fragment pull requests (fragment_id = global_step % 24) with signed live claims and applies synced fragments the orchestrator pushes back. Validators verify claims against the frozen previous fragment state, evaluate quality, and approve merges; weights come only from accepted live merge events with decay - self-reported TPS, loss, and GPU names are telemetry only. Not winner-take-all: every accepted merge counts.
playbook.minerJobProvide: ["Validator-approved live fragment merges (the reward path)","Signed training artifacts and receipts for audit","Continuous fragment availability during training","Checkpoint-coverage contributions across the 24 fragments"]
playbook.top10Strategy: Rewards follow accepted live-merge events, so the win condition is raw verified GPU-hours: stay online 24/7 on the latest release, keep FSDP/batch settings from OOMing, and respond to fragment pulls fast. Invalid, stale, replayed, or unsigned claims score zero. Newcomers should join via the published checkpoint manifest and target consistently high accepted-merge rates rather than one big run.
playbook.top10Levers: ["GPU-hours online and training throughput","Fast live-fragment claim responses to syncer pulls","Zero invalid/stale/replayed claims","Staying current with miner releases (protocol changes)","Multi-GPU scaling (QUASAR_MINER_DEVICES, FSDP)"]
playbook.followTopMiners: taostats.io/subnet/24 weights and rewarded miners; orchestrator current-run metadata and merge ledger via the public bucket; repo releases for protocol bumps; HuggingFace silx-ai/Quasar-Preview checkpoint cadence.

playbook.whatItDoes: UR is a decentralized privacy network: network operators sell VPN/proxy traffic carried by independent providers. Validators walk server-assigned provider routes measuring liveness and latency; Yuma consensus turns those measurements into emission. Demand is revenue-backed - operators deposit alpha sized to real usage, which funds pool payouts to providers via Merkle claims.
playbook.hardwareRec: CPU only; this is a bandwidth play. Providers run the UR client on residential/VPS hosts carrying ingress/egress traffic with stable connections and routable IPs. Fleets holding many distinct routable /29 (IPv4) or /48 (IPv6) prefixes can reach the head tier.
playbook.keyRequirements: ["Register as a provider via a network operator (ur.xyz); pool tier needs no UID or burn","Run provider software carrying ingress/egress traffic under a registered client_id","Survive validator probes: Wilson-score liveness interval and latency p95/p99 (EMA-smoothed)","Head tier requires burn-registered UID, manifest commitment, dual-signed client bindings; 200-fleet cap","7-day settlement epochs; pool payouts claimed with Merkle proofs from the vault"]
playbook.minerJob: Run the provider miner pointed at an operator's API; it carries VPN ingress/egress for that privacy network's customers. Each tempo validators measure your hops' liveness and latency; pools are weighted implied_usage x quality (clamped 0.75-1.0) and paid through Merkle claims, while top fleets ranked by routable-IP breadth get native Yuma payments straight to their hotkey. A client earns in exactly one tier at a time.
playbook.minerJobProvide: ["Real VPN/proxy ingress and egress bandwidth for privacy customers","Verified liveness (Wilson interval) and low p95/p99 latency on probed hops","Distinct routable egress prefixes for head-tier fleet breadth","Correct client_id attribution for Merkle pool claims"]
playbook.top10Strategy: The pool tier is the on-ramp: quality is clamped so pools differ at most 1.33x, meaning uptime and latency dominate - join a strong operator and run stable bandwidth. The head pays natively but needs broad routable IP breadth, effectively for operators with many distinct /29s. Note the mainnet bootstrap weights 90% to owner hotkeys initially, so positioning with operators matters more than solo residential lines today.
playbook.top10Levers: ["Provider liveness/latency quality (Q clamp 0.75-1.0)","Routable-IP breadth (distinct /29 or /48 prefix hashes) for head fleets","Choosing high-deposit operators (implied_usage weights pools)","Early burn-registered head fleet UID (limited head slots)","Multi-operator mining via provider provide --all-operators","Avoiding tier conflicts (client earns in exactly one tier)"]
playbook.followTopMiners: Watch ur.xyz/operators.yml and each epoch's public payout artifacts; track taostats.io/subnets/25 weights, mainnet/MAINNET.md bootstrap updates in-repo, and WHITEPAPER/VALIDATOR.md protocol changes.

playbook.whatItDoes: A decentralized adversarial-robustness network. Validators publish an ImageNet-1k image every two minutes; miners must find an imperceptible perturbation that flips EfficientNetV2-L's prediction. Outputs feed a growing adversarial-training dataset and on-chain robustness certificates (relevant to EU AI Act conformity) for enterprise and safety customers.
playbook.hardwareRec: Miner: 8 vCPU / 32 GB RAM with any 8+ GB NVIDIA GPU (12–24 GB comfortable); attack search speed matters more than VRAM. Optional model track (fine-tuning EfficientNetV2-L) wants a bigger GPU. No axon exposure needed; rentals fine.
playbook.keyRequirements: ["Python 3.10+, Node 18+/PM2, scripts/run_miner.sh","Miner env: WALLET_NAME/HOTKEY, NETUID, NETWORK","Registered hotkey; no axon exposure required","Submissions: image URL + sha256 pixel hash","Hard gates: L∞ bounds, SSIM, PSNR, label flip","Model track: on-chain commitment sha256(model||hotkey)"]
playbook.minerJob: Poll the task API for the current ImageNet-1k image, run your attack (baseline is PGD) to find a perturbation within L∞/SSIM/PSNR limits that flips the classifier, then upload the image and submit its URL plus pixel hash. Validators recompute hashes and score: smaller, subtler perturbations score higher ((1−ratio)² terms plus small margin/novelty bonuses). Scanning emissions split 75/20/5 across the top three ranks; separately, a daily adversarially-trained EfficientNetV2-L contest pays 20% of miner emissions to the day's winner. Weights come from stake-weighted cross-validator leaderboard ranks.
playbook.minerJobProvide: ["Verified adversarial examples per ~2-minute task","Compliant perturbations passing all hard gates","Leaderboard-topping attack scores (75/20/5)","Optional fine-tuned adversarially-trained EfficientNetV2-L","Stable image URLs with matching pixel hashes"]
playbook.top10Strategy: Emissions are brutally top-heavy — rank 1 takes 75% of the 80% scanning pot — so optimize attack quality: minimize L∞/RMSE ratios while staying under epsilon and above SSIM/PSNR floors, and poll fast enough to never miss a task. Beating the baseline PGD (better initialization, momentum, adaptive steps) is the core lever. Note avgScore needs a ~50-record history before it counts. The daily model track is a separate lottery — enter only with a genuinely strong fine-tune.
playbook.top10Levers: ["Stronger attack optimizer than baseline PGD","Minimize L∞/RMSE ratios under gates","Low-latency task polling and submission","Consistency: top-3 on every validator's leaderboard","Optional daily model-track fine-tune wins","Build the 50-record scoring history fast","Uptime across all validators' windows"]
playbook.followTopMiners: Watch the public leaderboard reports (per-validator avgScore), taostats.io/subnet/26 for the 75/20/5 weight pattern, repo commits for scoring-constant changes (PERTURB_* envs), and the perturbai.io whitepaper/Discord.

playbook.whatItDoes: Orion (SILX Labs) is a data-mining subnet: campaigns (currently coding, math, technical, and general-knowledge data for the Quasar model) define what a model needs; miners turn assigned source batches into model-ready datasets and upload signed snapshots. Validators replay a hidden sample to verify, and pay only valid, useful, non-duplicate work. Quasar is the first consumer.
playbook.hardwareRec: One modest GPU to run the campaign-pinned Quasar-Preview model locally (--devices 0), plus CPU/RAM for data processing. Needs a Chutes API key and Python 3.11-3.13 with uv. Rented cloud GPUs work.
playbook.keyRequirements: ["Python 3.11-3.13 + uv; install locked deps with uv run --frozen","Chutes API key for the campaign-pinned hosted judge","Process assigned real batches (not individual records) into model-ready datasets","Upload one signed dataset snapshot per assignment to the S3 bucket/prefix","Rewards = verified quality x useful token volume x signed availability history","Invalid, duplicated, stale, or unverifiable work scores zero"]
playbook.minerJob: Run the Orion miner CLI: it picks up signed campaigns and assignments, downloads assigned source data, processes it into model-ready dataset batches, compares the hosted judge against the locally-run Quasar-Preview revision (auto-downloaded from Hugging Face and cached), and uploads one signed snapshot. Validators independently replay a hidden sample, score verified quality and useful token volume, multiply by your signed availability history, and set weights. Availability is a direct reward multiplier, so uptime compounds.
playbook.minerJobProvide: ["Model-ready dataset snapshots per campaign assignment","Signed uploads that survive hidden-sample replay","Local Quasar-Preview runs matching the pinned revision","Sustained signed availability history","Zero duplication or staleness in submissions"]
playbook.top10Strategy: Rewards are quality x volume x availability, so top-10 means high throughput of verified-good data with near-perfect uptime. Automate the whole loop (assignment pickup, processing, judge comparison, signed upload), invest in processing quality over raw volume, and never let the miner go offline - availability multiplies everything. Deduplicate aggressively: stale or duplicate work pays zero and can poison your record.
playbook.top10Levers: ["Uptime and availability history (direct multiplier)","Dataset quality that survives hidden-sample replay","Processing throughput on real assigned batches","Clean dedup and freshness discipline","Right-sized GPU so Quasar-Preview inference stays fast"]
playbook.followTopMiners: Watch taostats.io/subnet/27 weight distribution and per-UID earnings, SILX-LABS/Orion commit cadence (campaign mechanics evolve), and Hugging Face silx-ai Quasar releases since your local model must match the pinned revision.

playbook.whatItDoes: gm is an LLM API gateway: buyers point existing OpenAI/Anthropic/Gemini SDKs at the gm gateway and get identical behavior. Miners supply upstream provider API capacity inside an Intel TDX TEE (neither operators nor hosts see buyer content or miner keys) and earn the spread between buyer price and upstream cost.
playbook.hardwareRec: No GPU, no bare metal: the miner is a pinned TEE container deployed to Phala Cloud (bring a funded Phala account). Hardware here means upstream API keys plus TDX attestation. Rentals irrelevant; Phala is the supported target.
playbook.keyRequirements: ["Funded Phala Cloud account; deploy via gmcli (dstack compose)","Your own provider API keys: Anthropic, OpenAI, Google, Chutes, Z.ai, Moonshot, DeepInfra, KubeTEE, Engy, Moonmath, NEAR","Taostats OAuth login (device code)","Registered Bittensor hotkey recorded with gmcli","Intel TDX TEE attestation must stay green"]
playbook.minerJob: You deploy the gm-miner image to Phala Cloud with gmcli deploy; at startup it mints an RA-TLS data-plane certificate, runs the attestation server, optional NEAR/Chutes/KubeTEE verifiers, and the Envoy data plane inside TDX. Buyer requests route to your verified key slots (up to 8 keys per direct route); you declare products and prices via gmcli and earn the spread on served traffic. Keys stay encrypted inside the TEE; testnet is netuid 482.
playbook.minerJobProvide: ["Upstream LLM API capacity inside the TEE container","Valid TDX attestation for the data plane","Declared products at competitive prices","Reliable multi-key slot capacity per route"]
playbook.top10Strategy: This is a margins-and-reliability business, not a benchmark race: price spreads per model, multi-provider route coverage, and uptime decide earnings. Newcomers: rehearse fully on testnet first, source cheap upstreams (DeepInfra/Engy/Moonmath sourcing routes) for popular models, and use multi-key slots to survive rate limits.
playbook.top10Levers: ["Price spread vs upstream cost per model","Uptime and clean TEE attestation","Provider-route breadth (11 routes)","Multi-key slot capacity (8 per route)","Testnet rehearsal before mainnet deploy"]
playbook.followTopMiners: Track taostats.io/subnet/28 for earning hotkeys, saygm.com and the repo docs/ for product/route changes, and release cadence of gm-miner (run gmcli update; the image is pinned to digest).

playbook.whatItDoes: An open winner-take-most arena for production LLM inference optimization: miners submit containerized inference servers, validators benchmark them against a pinned vLLM baseline on identical 8-GPU pods, and the fastest correct server earns most emission. V1 arena serves Qwen2.5-72B-Instruct with TP=8. Note: the repo README is branded Cacheon/SN14 while bittensor.ai lists SN29 as hotfloat, LLM inference optimization - same arena mechanics, rebranded.
playbook.hardwareRec: Miners need no resident GPUs - publish a Docker image (<=20 GB; weights mounted at runtime) and validators benchmark it on NVLink/SXM 8xH200/B200/B300 pods (8xH100 Tier B). Budget the submission fee; rent 8-GPU pods only to tune your server locally.
playbook.keyRequirements: ["Containerized server exposing /v1/chat/completions with streaming and logprobs","Public container registry plus image digest; image <=20 GB (weights mounted, not baked in)","On-chain commit via miner/commit.py with submission fee and payment proof","Greedy-decoding correctness gate - failing it zeroes your score","Challengers must beat the reigning winner's fresh score by a fixed 1% margin"]
playbook.minerJob: The miner builds and maintains a Dockerized LLM serving stack that beats pinned vLLM on end-to-end response time for the arena model. After pushing the image, they commit its reference, digest, and fee payment on-chain; validators pull it, mount model weights at /models, and score median speed improvement over baseline per round. Correctness is checked first - fail and score is zero. The winner earns 80% of the competition pool, runner-up 20%; scores compare only within a round and the crown persists until beaten by >1%.
playbook.minerJobProvide: ["Docker image of a production-grade serving stack for the arena model","On-chain commitment with image digest and fee payment","Measured e2e latency wins over the pinned vLLM baseline","Correctness-clean output (greedy decoding must match exactly)"]
playbook.top10Strategy: Systems engineering wins: custom kernels, better scheduling, quantization-aware serving, CUDA graph and overlap tuning for H200/B200-class pods. Benchmark locally against the exact pinned model/hardware before paying the fee, and remember the winner's score is the floor challengers must exceed by 1% - ship often, but never submit a correctness-risky change.
playbook.top10Levers: ["Squeeze e2e latency: continuous batching, speculative decoding, custom attention kernels","Replicate the validator eval locally; greedy-decode outputs must match","Respect the 20 GB image budget - lean runtime, external weights","Verify variance before submitting; the 1% margin filters noise","Track the current winner's fresh scores each round","Account for fees - every commit costs TAO"]
playbook.followTopMiners: Watch taostats.io/subnet/29 (and legacy /14 branding) weight changes per round, cacheon.ai docs/scoring updates, coldint/hotfloat commit cadence, and the Bittensor Discord for arena model or hardware-tier changes.
