playbook.whatItDoes: It's AI (SN32) is a decentralized AI-text detector: miners run detection models that classify text as human-written or AI-generated, including per-sentence 'deep scan' probabilities. Validators continuously query miners with human and AI texts generated by 30+ LLMs under varied parameters, augmentations, and adversarial attacks. The team monetizes detection via its-ai.org, API, and extensions.
playbook.hardwareRec: 1x RTX 4090 24GB (input metadata; platform engine rates it container-friendly with no TEE/bare-metal/static-IP requirement - rented GPUs work). Detector inference fits comfortably in 24GB; keep latency low.
playbook.keyRequirements: ["Registered hotkey plus subnet registration burn (~0.058 TAO per platform snapshot)","24GB-class GPU serving the detector model behind your axon","Robust accuracy across 30+ generator LLMs, augmentations, adversarial attacks","Low false-positive rate (education buyers care)","Container/rented hosting fine; deep validator pool queries regularly"]
playbook.minerJob: You serve an AI-detection model on your axon. Validators stream human-written and AI-generated texts (from top LLM-arena models with varied generation params, augmentations, and adversarial attacks) and score your classifications; per-sentence deep-scan probabilities are part of the product surface. The incentive mechanism is time-proven - the team reports SOTA on MGTD, RAID (98.3% accuracy), and GRiD/HC3/GhostBuster benchmarks, and credits the incentive design for keeping miners improving rather than gaming. Platform snapshots show a wide reward distribution (239/256 miners earned; ~94% rewarded ratio), so reliable mid-tier accuracy still pays while top accuracy takes the largest weights.
playbook.minerJobProvide: ["Human-vs-AI text classification","Per-sentence AI-probability deep scan","Low false-positive classification on human text","Fast, always-on inference endpoint"]
playbook.top10Strategy: Push benchmark-grade accuracy: retrain regularly on fresh generator LLMs, harden against paraphrase/attack augmentations, and control FPR. Small accuracy edges pay continuously because validators query all day and the reward pool is broad. Match the published incentive doc's direction (it produced their SOTA), keep inference fast, and watch benchmark leaderboards as your north star.
playbook.top10Levers: ["Accuracy on new/unseen generator LLMs","Adversarial + augmentation robustness","False-positive-rate control","Inference latency and uptime","Retraining cadence tied to docs/incentive.md updates"]
playbook.followTopMiners: taostats.io/subnet/32 incentive distribution (broad, ~94% rewarded) and top-UID accuracy churn; its-ai.org/en/accuracy reports; MGTD/RAID leaderboards; repo docs/incentive.md changes; Bittensor Discord SN32 channels.

playbook.whatItDoes: ReadyAI is a decentralized data-structuring pipeline: miners use LLM APIs to turn raw conversations, webpages, surveys, and documents into structured tags, entities, and embeddings for vector databases. Validators fully tag the same data as ground truth and score miner tags by embedding cosine distance. Businesses buy the structured output, published toward HuggingFace datasets.
playbook.hardwareRec: CPU only: 8GB+ RAM, 20GB+ disk. No local GPU - annotation runs through OpenAI (GPT-4o default), Anthropic, groq, OpenRouter or Chutes APIs at the miner's cost. RunPod cheap CPU instances are explicitly supported with a launch template.
playbook.keyRequirements: ["OpenAI API key (GPT-4o default) plus a Weights & Biases key required","CPU with 8GB+ RAM and 20GB+ disk; axon port must be reachable","Registered hotkey; Dockerized deploy or Runpod CPU template both supported","Tag quality scored by cosine distance to validator ground-truth tags","LLM API spend is miner-billed, so margin management is core"]
playbook.minerJob: Run neurons/miner.py (or the Runpod template): the axon receives TaskBundles - conversation windows, webpage markdown, surveys, skill documents - calls your configured LLM to emit topical tags plus embeddings, and returns them. Validators tag the same windows as ground truth and score each miner tag by cosine distance to the truth neighborhood; selected miners per window earn, feeding EMA and on-chain weights. Task types include named-entity extraction and skill generation.
playbook.minerJobProvide: ["Flat tag lists plus embeddings for conversation/webpage/survey windows","Normalized named-entity extractions from documents and transcripts","LLM skill-generation documents for skill_coverage_evaluation tasks","Cheap, accurate GPT-4o-class annotation at scale"]
playbook.top10Strategy: This is a margin game: reward minus API cost. Winners tune prompts so tag style matches the validator's ground-truth conventions, prune redundant tags, and pick the cheapest capable model per task type. Only a few miners are selected per window, so responsiveness and uptime count. Newcomers: replicate the reference miner first, then optimize prompt and model cost per tag until margin is positive.
playbook.top10Levers: ["Prompt engineering aligned with ground-truth tagging style","Model cost optimization (OpenRouter/Chutes/deepseek overrides)","Embedding closeness to validator ground truth","Uptime - only selected miners earn per window","Mastering the newest task type (skill_coverage_evaluation)","Runpod CPU template for cheap hosting"]
playbook.followTopMiners: Track taostats.io/subnets/33 top UIDs and reward spread, repo commit cadence (new task types shift scoring), and the Bittensor Discord subnet-33 channel.

playbook.whatItDoes: A GAN-style competition for synthetic-media detection. Discriminative miners submit image/video/audio deepfake-detection classifiers; generative miners run servers producing synthetic media on demand; validators benchmark both. Detectors improve as fakes improve. Products serve provenance/detection APIs; app.bitmind.ai tracks the reigning kings per modality.
playbook.hardwareRec: Discriminative track: no GPU hosting — upload safetensors classifiers (the A100/80 GB input spec reflects the generative track). Generative track: GPU inference server (A100-class) producing image+video at volume. Detector miners can run anywhere.
playbook.keyRequirements: ["Models: safetensors only (ONNX rejected)","gascli d push for detector submissions","Weekly-refreshed GASBench + GAS-Station data","Generators must clear fool-rate gate (img>2%, vid>1%)","C2PA-signed generator outputs","Submission allowances shared across modalities"]
playbook.minerJob: Detectors: train a media-provenance classifier, zip and push via gascli; validators score it (sn34_score = MCC + Brier error) on public, private-holdout and fresh GAS-Station data across three modalities. Each lane has a king (image 40%, video 40%, audio 4% of miner emissions) split 85/10/5 across the current and two previous kings; dethrone by +0.01 sn34_score on the same benchmark version. Generators: answer validator prompts with verified synthetic media; the 16% generator pot pays per verified volume × √(price/baseline) × pass-rate, only in modalities that clear the 7-day fool-rate gate.
playbook.minerJobProvide: ["Detection classifiers for image/video/audio","sn34_score improvements over reigning kings","Synthetic-media generation endpoint (optional track)","C2PA-signed verifiable generations","Fresh-model submissions within allowance limits"]
playbook.top10Strategy: Detector lanes are king-of-the-hill with 85/10/5 memory — beating a king by just 0.01 takes the lane, so track each lane's sn34_score and target the weakest modality (audio is only 4%). Prioritize calibration (Brier) as much as accuracy, and retrain weekly against refreshed GAS-Station fakes. For generators, clearing the fool-rate gate is binary; after that, verified volume and the model price multiplier drive payout.
playbook.top10Levers: ["Dethrone the weakest lane (image/video/audio)","Calibration-tuned models (Brier + MCC)","Weekly retraining on GAS-Station refreshes","Fool-rate gate clearance for generators","Generation volume with strong price multiplier","Free submission allowance management","Robustness to the augmentation blend in scoring"]
playbook.followTopMiners: Track app.bitmind.ai leaderboard kings per modality, `gascli d perf` for your benchmark scores, taostats.io/subnet/34 dividend concentration, the BitMind Discord for round-config changes, and docs/Incentive.md updates.

playbook.whatItDoes: Epago is an adversarial arena building the world's frontier open deep-research model. Miners fine-tune the reigning king (genesis: Tongyi-DeepResearch-30B-A3B, a 30.5B MoE with ~3.3B active params) and submit challengers; validators run blind statistical duels on fresh research tasks. Beat the king at 99.9% confidence across a stake-weighted validator quorum and you hold the crown and roughly 90% of emissions.
playbook.hardwareRec: 1x consumer GPU is viable for serving/eval of the 3.3B-active MoE; fine-tuning challengers wants more VRAM (LoRA on 24GB feasible). Status badge says testnet-ready - confirm mainnet mechanics before committing spend.
playbook.keyRequirements: ["Fine-tune the current king and submit a digest-pinned Hugging Face checkpoint via timelock commit-reveal","Challenger must beat the king at 99.9% LCB over adaptive floor delta=0.05x(1-king accuracy), confirmed twice","Coronation requires accept verdicts covering >=51% of validator stake","Gates: config lock, size cap, 3 attempts per hotkey per round, one model per round, escalating loser cooldowns","Emissions: king 90% falling to 85%, arena (3 most recent ex-kings) 10% rising to 15%","A copy of the king mathematically cannot beat it by delta"]
playbook.minerJob: Miners are model trainers: fork/fine-tune the reigning king checkpoint, improve deep-research procedure quality (decompose, search, cross-check, attribute), upload a private digest-pinned checkpoint to HF, and commit through timelock commit-reveal so eval tasks are unknowable pre-reveal. Validators duel king vs challenger on ~1,000 fresh tasks (800 derived from the reveal's block hash, 200 from each validator's private pool). Winner-takes-most: ~90% of emissions to the crowned king, 10-15% to the three most recent ex-kings.
playbook.minerJobProvide: ["Digest-pinned challenger checkpoint (private unless crowned)","Measurable deep-research quality gain over the king","Compliant harness (config lock, size cap, no harness-breaking)","Fresh weights (copied weights are fingerprint-terminal)","Verified reward data produced as a duel byproduct"]
playbook.top10Strategy: Top-10 means being one of a handful of serious fine-tuners: mine the published headroom (base model scores 33.9% on Epago's exam; the 34-to-56 gap with perfect retrieval is the target; episodes die at turn/clock/context limits). Build a tight local eval loop mirroring the task style, train procedure skills, and submit only challengers that clear delta in your own testing - losing costs escalating cooldown time.
playbook.top10Levers: ["Fine-tuning skill on the 30B MoE base","Local eval harness mirroring duel task style","Attack episode completion failures (turn/clock/context)","Clean passage of cheap CPU intake gates","Iteration cadence faster than loser cooldowns reset"]
playbook.followTopMiners: Track the Epago dashboard (docs/DASHBOARD.md) for the current crown and reign age, taostats.io/subnet/36 weight concentration, and repo/docs updates - status is testnet-ready, so mechanism changes land in the repo first.

playbook.whatItDoes: Aurelius is a moral-reasoning alignment subnet. Miners submit structured ethical-dilemma scenario configs; validators score them through an 8-stage pipeline (schema, rate-limit, novelty, classifier, simulation) and run accepted scenarios through DeepMind Concordia generative-agent simulations. Transcripts become training data that improves LLM performance on moral-reasoning benchmarks (MoReBench).
playbook.hardwareRec: CPU-only for miners: a Docker host with a public IP (axon port 8091). The validator side uses an OpenAI-compatible LLM API (DeepSeek default, cheapest) instead of local GPUs. No GPU requirement found for miners; a small VPS is enough.
playbook.keyRequirements: ["Hotkey registered on netuid 37 (registration costs TAO)","Docker 20.10+; published GHCR miner image","Scenario config library loaded at startup (schema_v1: 9 tension archetypes, 2 agents, 1-10 scenes)","Work-token balance that validators can spend on acceptance","Publicly reachable IP + open inbound port 8091"]
playbook.minerJob: You run the aurelius-miner container serving operator-authored scenario JSONs from a configs/ directory in round-robin order, each stamped with a work_id and hotkey-signed via ScenarioConfigSynapse. The validator charges work tokens, pushes each config through the 8-stage pipeline including a Concordia simulation sidecar, and sets weights on outcomes. Miners never generate configs at request time — quality authoring happens offline and the container restarts to pick up additions.
playbook.minerJobProvide: ["Schema-perfect ethical-dilemma scenario configs","Signed round-robin responses carrying work_id","Novel scenarios that pass novelty/classifier gates","Funded work-token balance for submissions"]
playbook.top10Strategy: A content-quality war: duplicate or template-y scenarios die at novelty/classifier stages, so breadth across the 9 archetypes plus genuinely fresh premises wins. Newcomers: study testlab configs in the aurelius-ops repo, author programmatically (seed_generator.py as reference), keep a large diverse library, and budget work tokens.
playbook.top10Levers: ["Scenario novelty vs validator dedup gates","Schema compliance across all fields","Library size and archetype diversity","Work-token budget management","Tracking pipeline/scoring changes in repo"]
playbook.followTopMiners: Watch taostats.io/subnet/37 weights, the repo's commit cadence for pipeline-stage and threshold changes, GHCR image tags (aurelius-miner:latest), and aurelius-ops testlab configs for what currently passes.

playbook.whatItDoes: ChronoLLM pays miners to train small language models with strict temporal cutoffs - a 2018 model knows nothing after 2018 - removing lookahead bias for financial backtesting and historical analysis. TEE validators test leak behavior on private data, then run GPT-judged quality duels; the top 10 split emissions exponentially (#1 roughly 52%).
playbook.hardwareRec: Repo doesn't pin miner hardware, but weekly <=2.2B-param training implies a multi-GPU A100/H100-class rig to be competitive. Self-test is CPU-only (12 calls/day cap). You upload safetensors to HuggingFace - any cloud rental works.
playbook.keyRequirements: ["Train per-cutoff-year models: <=2.2B params, HF AutoModelForCausalLM-compatible, safetensors only, no remote code","Pass leak detection: recognize >=70% of pre-cutoff items, <=10% post-cutoff (leak_score = unknown - known)","SVD pairwise dedup rejects near-duplicates; earliest submitter wins","Weekly resubmission - all submissions clear every Monday 12:00 UTC round","Custom architectures require a PR review; thresholds published at api.chronollm.com/config"]
playbook.minerJob: Each week the miner trains a temporally consistent model (era-limited corpus curation, training, checkpointing), optionally pre-qualifies with the TEE-based self-test, uploads safetensors to HuggingFace, and commits the model on-chain after the submission window opens. Validators on Phala Cloud (Intel TDX) run anti-copy, leak-detection, and qualification stages, then round-robin quality duels on fresh LLM-generated prompts judged by GPT-5.4; final ranking is quality win-rate among models that pass the leak gate. Top 10 earn on exponential decay: #1 ~52%, #2 ~23%, #3 ~12%.
playbook.minerJobProvide: ["Weekly on-chain submissions of vintage-cutoff LLM checkpoints","Models that pass private-data leak tests (know your era, nothing later)","Top-quality completions beating rivals in judged duels","HuggingFace-hosted public models usable via leaderboard chat"]
playbook.top10Strategy: A two-sided game: satisfy the leak gate (deep knowledge of your vintage, nothing after) while maximizing completion quality against the top-30 field. Repeatable weekly training pipelines, era-specific data curation, and the free 12/day TEE self-test beat heroics; dedup means copying last week's winner fails - genuine incremental improvements win.
playbook.top10Levers: ["Era-specific data curation is the moat - leak score is pass/fail","Use the free TEE self-test (12/day) to pre-qualify every candidate","2.2B cap favors optimized training recipes over raw compute","Watch api.chronollm.com/config for changing thresholds","Submit early in the Monday window - dedup favors earliest","Chat with leaderboard models to spot quality gaps to beat"]
playbook.followTopMiners: Track leaderboard.chronollm.com round winners, taostats.io/subnet/38 incentive distribution, api.chronollm.com/config threshold changes, chronollm/sn38 commit cadence, and the ChronoLLM Discord channel.

playbook.whatItDoes: Ralph is a model-compression tournament on one pinned model (Qwen3-8B): compress it into four bit tiers (binary ~1.15, ternary 1.75, sub2 2.3, sub4 4.0 bits/weight) without changing the architecture. The best compression per tier - scored by downstream semantic-effect equivalence, three judges, worst-slice - becomes 'king', ships as public downloadable crown weights, and keeps 80% of the tier's reward.
playbook.hardwareRec: No always-on box: compression is done privately offline; budget research GPU time (H100-class practical for 8B quantization experiments; the subnet-rented eval side references H100 80GB). One artifact per coldkey+tier per round.
playbook.keyRequirements: ["Commit-reveal on chain: commit exact served bytes before the round exists","Architecture/weight-element count must match Qwen/Qwen3-8B exactly","GGUF needs a mainline llama.cpp Metal path (TQ1_0/TQ2_0 banned)","Measured bits/weight (from tensor data) under the tier cap","Copies earn nothing; one owner per artifact bytes (earlier commit wins)"]
playbook.minerJob: You compress Qwen3-8B privately (GPTQ, AWQ, bitsandbytes, or your own scheme), verify the bit budget with eval.bitrate, commit the content hash of exactly what you'll serve on-chain, then reveal when the round opens. Validators run six gates (economics, safety, tier fit, bit budget, pinned parent, commit-reveal), then score all submissions with three judges on exams drawn from the post-commit nonce: downstream-effect similarity to the pinned parent. The tier's king keeps 80%, the best challenger with a strictly positive paired margin gets 20%, everyone else gets nothing; crowns change hands at a 0.02 lead (0.01 in two consecutive rounds), and a three-round king defends against half margins.
playbook.minerJobProvide: ["Compressed Qwen3-8B artifacts per bit tier","On-chain commit-reveal of exact served bytes","Crown-beating compression (public king artifacts)","Pre-verified bit budget via eval.bitrate"]
playbook.top10Strategy: Winner-take-most: start from the published crown in RalphLabsAI/ralph-crowns and genuinely improve it - copying scores the same as the original (zero margin) and earns nothing. Master the bit-budget rules (per-tensor mixing headroom: 1-bit body + 2-bit embedding measures 1.076) and avoid the TQ* trap. For binary tier, use published 1-bit PTQ frameworks (BiLLM, ARB-LLM) then export to Q1_0. Hash the downloaded repo, not local files - commit-reveal mismatch is the top rejection.
playbook.top10Levers: ["Novel PTQ methods (BiLLM/ARB-LLM for binary; imatrix schemes for sub2/sub4)","Worst-slice quality across all three judges, languages, depths","Precise bit-budget engineering (per-tensor mixing)","Commit hygiene (hash exactly what HF serves)","Persistence: contender seats carry into next rounds"]
playbook.followTopMiners: taostats.io/subnets/40; HuggingFace RalphLabsAI/ralph-v2-rounds (signed round records) and ralph-crowns (current kings); repo commits; eval.precheck to see the whole pending queue and competitors.

playbook.whatItDoes: Almanac runs two forecasting incentive mechanisms: Almanac Market, where miners trade prediction markets and are scored on ROI plus qualified volume; and Almanac Forecasting, where miners submit agents whose event predictions validators score on accuracy and calibration. Validators blend both scores into on-chain weights. Quant traders and researchers monetize forecasting edge.
playbook.hardwareRec: CPU only. Market track needs a funded Polymarket proxy wallet plus dApp or API client; forecasting track needs a small box for the CLI (agents run on validator sandboxes; inference via the central gateway with portal credits). No GPU.
playbook.keyRequirements: ["Market track: Almanac Market account, funded proxy wallet, on-chain metadata (first 5 chars of EOA) linked to your UID","1% fee collected on every buy trade funds the daily reward pool","Forecasting track: portal.almnc.ai account with credits plus a GATEWAY_API_KEY","Agent subclasses BaseAgent implementing predict(ctx) -> AgentResult with a valid beliefPath","Registered miner UID on netuid 41 (testnet 172)"]
playbook.minerJob: Market miners trade via the dApp or the signed CLOB API client; validators ingest trade history and score ROI/qualified volume over a rolling window. Forecasting miners build Python agents and submit via miner/cli.py; validators execute them in locked Docker sandboxes, post predictions and reasoning traces to the portal, and score sustained accuracy, calibrated confidence, and beating the market. Blended scores become weights.
playbook.minerJobProvide: ["Profitable prediction-market trades (ROI plus qualified volume)","Calibrated event-probability forecasts from submitted agents","Reasoning-trace metadata for Almanac's data pipeline","On-chain metadata linking UID to trading EOA"]
playbook.top10Strategy: Market scoring favors sustained edge, substantial volume, and beating the competition - treat the 1% buy fee as a cost of doing business and only trade where you genuinely have edge; the API client enables automation. Forecasting rewards calibration over bravado. Newcomers can start on the market track today with zero infrastructure, then add a forecasting agent; niche markets with weaker traders are the entry.
playbook.top10Levers: ["Sustained trading edge over the rolling scoring window","Automated CLOB trading via the API client (multi-wallet support)","Calibrated agent forecasts that beat the market","Portal credits and gateway key setup discipline","Targeting niche prediction markets with weaker competition","Watching public validator logs (wandb.ai/corvx/almanac-vali-logs)"]
playbook.followTopMiners: Track taostats.io/subnets/41 weights, the beta.almanac.market leaderboards, public validator telemetry at wandb.ai/corvx/almanac-vali-logs, and Discord channel #almanac-41; watch repo commits for scoring changes.

playbook.whatItDoes: A decentralized network for graph optimization, currently focused on the Traveling Salesman Problem. Validators send synthetic TSP instances; miners return tours scored against the best cohort solution and a greedy benchmark. Aimed at logistics/routing use cases; a planned frontend will let users submit their own graph problems.
playbook.hardwareRec: CPU only — TSP quality is algorithm work, not GPU work. The repo ships four starter algorithms (Nearest Neighbour, Dynamic Programming, Beam Search, Hybrid Pointer Network); custom high-performance solvers are the differentiator.
playbook.keyRequirements: ["Python miner per docs/miner.md","Respond with tours within the required timeframe","Support coordinate (undirected) and edge (directed) inputs","Beat the greedy benchmark or be penalized","Team warns of breaking changes — join Discord"]
playbook.minerJob: Run the miner neuron from the Graphite repo; validators broadcast TSP instances and the miner returns high-quality tours computed by its solver. Scoring compares your tour length relative to the best solution in the cohort and a benchmark greedy heuristic; solutions falling short of the benchmark are penalized. Upgrading from the bundled heuristics to stronger solvers (better local search, or improved learned approaches like the provided pointer network) is how weight share is won.
playbook.minerJobProvide: ["Near-optimal TSP tours per instance","Responses within the scoring timeframe","Custom solver improvements over bundled algorithms","Consistent quality across graph sizes","Support for directed/undirected input formats"]
playbook.top10Strategy: This is an algorithms race: the bundled algorithms are the floor, not the ceiling — winners implement stronger TSP solvers (OR-tools/LKH-style local search or improved learned models) that reliably beat the greedy benchmark by a wide margin at low latency. Because scoring is relative to the cohort, small consistent margins across every instance compound into a dominant weight share.
playbook.top10Levers: ["Stronger custom TSP solver than baselines","Low-latency tour computation","Wide margin over the greedy benchmark","Consistency across instance sizes/types","Track repo/Discord for scoring changes","Efficient CPU implementations (no GPU waste)"]
playbook.followTopMiners: Watch taostats.io/subnet/43 top UIDs and weight spread, the Graphite Discord for scoring/algorithm updates (team warns of breaking changes), and commit cadence on GraphiteAI/Graphite-Subnet.

playbook.whatItDoes: TurboVision (Score) is a decentralized intelligence layer for live video and imagery, focused on professional sports. Validators run scoring jobs per Element from a manifest - building ground truth (real or SAM3 pseudo-GT), calling eligible miners' models from the on-chain registry, and paying per-Element winners. Sports and media buyers get structured, decision-ready data from raw footage.
playbook.hardwareRec: Per platform data: 1x GPU with >=16GB VRAM; RTX 5090, B200, H200, H20, MI300X explicitly excluded - plan 4090/A6000/L40S-class hardware. Workload is computer-vision model serving on video.
playbook.keyRequirements: ["Contribute models that solve Elements in the active Manifest","Hugging Face account with write access (HUGGINGFACE_USERNAME/API_KEY required)","Chutes developer account and CHUTES_API_KEY required","Validators call eligible miners from the on-chain registry and score outputs on live data","Per-element weight share; winners chosen over each element's eval_window (days)","Bittensor hotkey folder copied onto every host running TurboVision"]
playbook.minerJob: Miners publish and serve vision models addressing the Manifest's Elements (detection/tracking-style tasks on sports footage). The validator runner executes scoring jobs on a fixed block cadence (default 300 blocks per element): it fetches a challenge, builds ground truth, calls eligible registered miners, scores outputs, and emits shards to R2; aggregated per-Element scores pick winners whose weight share is normalized and set on-chain. MINER.md was 404 at research time, so follow repo docs and Score's channels for the exact miner contract.
playbook.minerJobProvide: ["Vision model endpoints solving Manifest Elements","Accurate predictions on live video/imagery windows","Reliable availability at each element's block cadence","HF-hosted model artifacts with pinned versions","Consistent scores across eval windows"]
playbook.top10Strategy: Score is per-Element winner-take-share: pick Elements where competition is thin and accuracy against the validator's ground-truth pipeline (real GT or SAM3 pseudo-GT) is achievable. Optimize for the actual scoring windows - 300-block cadence, eval_window lookbacks - not generic benchmarks. A newcomer wins by shipping one high-accuracy Element fast and then iterating on the pseudo-GT edge cases validators actually measure.
playbook.top10Levers: ["Element selection (thin-competition targets first)","Accuracy against SAM3 pseudo-GT quirks","Low-latency, always-on model endpoints","Fast response to manifest updates","Clean Chutes/HF integration (no scoring gaps)"]
playbook.followTopMiners: Track taostats.io/subnet/44 weight holders, Manifest updates in the repo (elements, weights, blacklist file), and winner snapshots emitted on every set_weights; watch wearescore.com and Score's channels for manifest changes.

playbook.whatItDoes: AlphaRidge reads the world's financial news — about 290,000 articles a day from ~13,000 sources — and turns it into structured market data powering the AlphaRidge product (charts, screener, events browser, API). Miners produce per-article analysis: asset sentiment, Wikidata/ticker entity resolution, economic data points, contagion chains, narrative tags, embeddings.
playbook.hardwareRec: 8GB VRAM minimum, 24GB+ comfortable (RTX 4090 fits); 16-32GB RAM, 8-16+ CPU cores, 60-100GB disk. ~44GB of models download on first run. NER stage is CPU-heavy: core count sets throughput, and throughput is what you're paid for. Rentals acceptable.
playbook.keyRequirements: ["OpenRouter API key — you pay your own LLM inference (2 of 4 pipeline stages)","Registered hotkey on netuid 45","Return batch leases in time; late batches requeue to others","Batch audits: whole batch discarded if the validator's blind sample doesn't reproduce","Reputation multiplier gates pay; penalties can zero a window"]
playbook.minerJob: Run neurons.miner with the analyzer pipeline (spaCy transformer NER, ReFinED entity linking, two LLM stages via OpenRouter). Validators lease batches; you analyze at roughly 12-18s per article. The validator blind-re-runs a sample of each batch and discards the entire batch on mismatch. Pay = verified volume × reputation (EMA through a logistic gate), priced in USD per point rather than alpha. Batch size ramps with demonstrated throughput; multiple UIDs do not multiply pay.
playbook.minerJobProvide: ["Per-article structured analysis (sentiment, entities, tickers)","Contagion chains, narrative tags, embeddings","Batch turnaround within lease windows","Sample-reproducible outputs audit after audit"]
playbook.top10Strategy: Throughput × quality economics: more CPU cores and faster, cheaper LLM calls raise verified volume; a single failed audit wastes the batch and dents reputation. Newcomers: expect tiny first batches that ramp, budget OpenRouter spend carefully, fix NAT/nginx header quirks, and watch the observatory leaderboard to see reputation as validators do.
playbook.top10Levers: ["CPU core count (NER-bound throughput)","LLM latency/cost on OpenRouter","Batch audit pass rate protecting reputation","Uptime during lease windows","Correct axon networking (bt_header_* not stripped)"]
playbook.followTopMiners: Track the miner leaderboard on alpharidge.ai (live throughput + reputation), taostats.io/subnet/45 for incentive spread, and repo commits for pipeline/model changes.

For miners, the practical requirement is registering a hotkey and following the subnet's platform onboarding; emission presumably follows validator-side scoring of service quality defined on that platform.

playbook.whatItDoes: GPUForge is a proposed subnet for verifiable GPU training work: a publisher signs immutable training-job manifests, miners execute them on eligible NVIDIA H100 hardware, and validators measure correct, useful training throughput (attestation, digests, canary challenges, tolerance-bounded correctness) and convert it into weights. Critically, the repo states it is NOT ready for miners, validators, testnet, or mainnet.
playbook.hardwareRec: NVIDIA H100 (SXM/PCIe/NVL normalized); default policy requests 1 GPU with 81,920 MiB. NVIDIA NVAT hardware attestation is a planned gate, so attestation-capable hosting is implied. No supported miner release exists yet - do not provision production spend.
playbook.keyRequirements: ["None actionable today: 'no supported miner or validator release yet'","Interfaces, scoring rules, and security assumptions may change without notice","Never run untrusted publisher training jobs or use production wallets","When live: digest-pinned containers, least-privilege isolation, no outbound network","Hardware-backed H100 attestation (NVAT 1.x) expected as a verification tier"]
playbook.minerJob: Once live (not today), the miner would report capabilities, accept validator-signed short-lived work leases, run the pinned publisher workload in a hardened isolated container, and return signed execution evidence: checkpoint commitments, challenge outputs, timing under throughput-plausibility envelopes. Validators verify NVAT attestation tiers, manifest identity, hidden commit-reveal canaries, randomized correctness probes, and anomaly bounds before weighting. Everything is layered evidence - no single measurement proves execution. Until testnet acceptance criteria are met, this is design documentation, not an operational miner.
playbook.minerJobProvide: ["Verified training throughput on H100 (future)","Signed execution evidence bundles","Checkpoint commitments matching declared cadence","Attestation-capable hosting posture"]
playbook.top10Strategy: Prepare, don't spend: the README forbids production use, so the play is monitoring. Track the repo for the release announcement, testnet acceptance criteria, and attestation requirements; pre-qualify attested H100 hosting and hardened container ops. Subnets that launch with verifiable-training narratives typically reward early reliable operators, but entry only makes sense after the fail-closed gates ship.
playbook.top10Levers: ["Early testnet participation when releases land","NVAT-attestable H100 hosting readiness","Container hardening (non-root, read-only, resource quotas)","Throughput reliability within plausibility envelopes","Protocol-change tracking (signatures, tiers, profiles)"]
playbook.followTopMiners: Watch the forgenet47/gpuforge commit cadence and releases (the real signal - no miner exists yet); taostats.io/subnets/47 for emission state (likely burn/owner until live); Bittensor Discord for launch notices.

playbook.whatItDoes: SN48 sells access to real quantum computers through Bittensor. Users broadcast OpenQASM circuits; validators route them to miners who own or operate physical QPUs, and results are broadcast back (public free tier). Emissions currently run about 90% burn and 10% to compute providers, forwarded to Open Quantum and paid out to providers in USD.
playbook.hardwareRec: Not GPU mineable: miners must own or operate a gate-based quantum computer executing OpenQASM 2.0/3.0, or hold a documented direct partnership with a QPU owner. Onboarding is manual via support@openquantum.com. Ordinary GPU/CPU miners cannot participate.
playbook.keyRequirements: ["Ownership/operation of a gate-based QPU executing OpenQASM 2.0/3.0, or documented partnership with an owner/operator","Rigorous manual onboarding through support@openquantum.com","Free-tier executions are broadcast publicly to validators and miners","Emission model: ~90% burn / 10% to providers, routed via an Open Quantum-controlled key, paid in USD","Premium tiers: priority execution, extra shots, private off-chain execution"]
playbook.minerJob: Miners are QPU operators: they receive validated quantum circuit jobs, execute them on their quantum hardware, and broadcast results back through the network for verification. Validators check execution honesty; all incentive is forwarded to a key controlled by the Open Quantum operators, who sell alpha and pay quantum compute providers in USD rather than miners holding alpha directly.
playbook.minerJobProvide: ["Gate-based quantum circuit execution (OpenQASM 2/3)","Verified shot results broadcast back to the network","Queue capacity for free-tier and premium (priority/shots/private) jobs","Execution metadata tagged to each broadcast circuit"]
playbook.top10Strategy: Supply is deliberately tiny: the few QPU operators capture the 10% non-burned share, so there is no incremental path for GPU miners. The only play is controlling quantum hardware or a documented partnership. Otherwise watch from the side - the roadmap's proof-of-compute and decentralized HPC simulation endpoints could eventually open classical miner slots.
playbook.top10Levers: ["Owning or operating a physical QPU (the only real lever)","Documented direct partnership with a QPU owner/operator","Early onboarding contact (support@openquantum.com)","Roadmap watch: HPC simulation endpoints may open future classical mining","Premium service quality (priority/private execution) for USD revenue"]
playbook.followTopMiners: Few miners exist - check taostats.io/subnets/48 for the provider set and emission split, plus qbittensor-labs/quantum-compute commits and the Open Quantum site for onboarding changes.

playbook.whatItDoes: A decentralized robotics tournament. Miners train RL policies for benchmark environments and submit agent code; validators run each agent inside isolated GPU sandbox containers (Isaac Sim 6.1 + Isaac Lab 3.0), score it, and the tournament winner takes all weights. Buyers get benchmarked robotics policies and an evaluation harness.
playbook.hardwareRec: GPU workstation for training policies (input spec: 1× A100-class); the submission itself is a CLI upload. Validator-side scoring GPUs (A100+, ~20 GB sandbox image) are not the miner's burden.
playbook.keyRequirements: ["nepher-miner CLI + miner_config.yaml (wallet + API key)","Submit agents via `nepher-miner submit`","Policies must run in Isaac Lab sandboxes","Tournament API: api.nepher.ai/tournament","EnvHub serves benchmark environment downloads","Winner takes all weights per tournament"]
playbook.minerJob: Train reinforcement-learning policies against Nepher's benchmark environments (downloaded from EnvHub), package the agent, and submit it through the nepher-miner CLI to the Tournament API. Validators evaluate every submitted agent inside ephemeral sandbox containers with dropped capabilities, read-only mounts, whitelisted networking and GPU access, then post scores; the tournament winner collects all of that round's weight. `nepher-miner validate` lets you pre-check an agent before submitting.
playbook.minerJobProvide: ["Trained RL policies for robotics benchmarks","Agent code that passes sandbox evaluation","Tournament submissions via nepher-miner CLI","Locally validated agents before submission","Winning policies across tournament rounds"]
playbook.top10Strategy: Winner-takes-all per tournament: pick benchmarks where you can train a clearly better policy rather than entering everything, and always run `nepher-miner validate` locally first — a sandbox eval failure wastes a submission. Expect an arms race in RL training quality (reward shaping, training compute, robustness to sandbox conditions). Track which environments current tournaments use and specialize.
playbook.top10Levers: ["Superior RL policy training (compute + shaping)","Local `nepher-miner validate` before submitting","Specialize in current tournament environments","Robust policies under sandbox conditions","Fast iteration per tournament cycle","Track EnvHub environment releases"]
playbook.followTopMiners: Track api.nepher.ai/tournament standings and winners, docs.nepher.ai for tournament rules, the Nepher Discord, taostats.io/subnet/49 weight concentration, and repo commit cadence.

playbook.whatItDoes: Synth (Mode Network) pays miners for synthetic price data: ensembles of 1,000 simulated price paths for crypto, equities, and commodities across 24h and 1h horizons. Validators score ensembles with CRPS against real price moves; emissions split equally across three competitions (Crypto 1h, Crypto 24h, Commodities/Equities 24h). AI agents, options traders, and portfolio managers consume the distributions.
playbook.hardwareRec: CPU only - path generation is numerical code (reference synth/miner/price_simulation.py). A modest VPS works; response latency matters because predictions are due before start_time and misses get the 90th-percentile penalty.
playbook.keyRequirements: ["Return 1,000 paths before start_time; invalid or late submissions score the 90th-percentile penalty","Three competitions with equal emission thirds: Crypto 1h (5-min increments, beta 0.3), Crypto 24h, Commodities/Equities 24h","Match the validator's price feed: Binance spot for BTC/ETH/SOL/XRP, Hyperliquid for the rest","Capture volatility clustering and fat-tailed distributions","Rolling average windows: 5 days (1h) and 10 days (24h); softmax allocation on relative rank"]
playbook.minerJob: Run an always-on daemon answering validator requests every ~15-32 minutes per asset: given (start_time, asset, time_increment, time_horizon, num_simulations), fetch the live price from the same feed the validator scores against, generate 1,000 correlated price paths (calibrated stochastic-vol models capturing volatility clustering and fat tails), and return them before start_time. Per-prompt CRPS scores roll into 5/10-day windows and emissions flow through a softmax on relative rank - small CRPS wins move big emission shares.
playbook.minerJobProvide: ["1,000-path probabilistic forecasts per request, on time","Calibrated distributions competitive on CRPS","Realistic dynamics: volatility clustering, fat tails","Feed-matched spot prices at t0","Continuous availability across 13 assets and 3 competitions"]
playbook.top10Strategy: A quant research grind on a CPU base: build a proper stochastic-volatility/correlation simulator, calibrate continuously to the exact feeds, and never miss a deadline - the 90th-percentile penalty is brutal. The softmax is sharpest at beta 0.3 in Crypto 1h, where small calibration wins move large emission shares. Newcomers break top-10 by out-calibrating incumbents on one competition first, then expanding to the others.
playbook.top10Levers: ["Calibrated stochastic-volatility simulation code","Feed parity with the validator (Binance/Hyperliquid at t0)","Deadline reliability (penalty avoidance)","Competition selection (beta 0.3 Crypto 1h is sharpest)","Daily backtesting against realized moves"]
playbook.followTopMiners: Track taostats.io/subnet/50 CRPS-ranked UIDs and emission shares, the asset-change table in the README (feeds migrate, assets added often), and the Synth Discord for parameter changes.

playbook.whatItDoes: Lium is a decentralized GPU rental marketplace on Bittensor: providers list NVIDIA GPUs that renters (people, teams, AI agents) book hourly at lium.io. A validator checks every node every 15 minutes (hardware, GPU, network, ports, Sysbox runtime). Providers earn rental-fee share plus subnet emission, including idle pay for eligible unrented GPUs.
playbook.hardwareRec: Any NVIDIA model on the validator's supported GPU_MODEL_RATES list (input suggests 8× B300 for top tiers; consumer RTX 30/40/50-series listed). Ubuntu 24.04, Sysbox, Docker, public IP, >=100Mbps; idle pay needs disk >=1.5× VRAM. TDX only for H100/H200/B200/GB200 tiers.
playbook.keyRequirements: ["Registered hotkey on SN51 (dynamic fee) + Provider Portal sign-in","Central Provider Server selected AND Discord connected — otherwise zero incentive","Sysbox runtime + NVIDIA Container Toolkit (validator rejects otherwise)","Ports: node HTTP, SSH 2200, and >=3 renting ports reachable from internet","Idle pool: price at/below market soft limit, disk >=1.5× VRAM, power-limit support"]
playbook.minerJob: Run `lium mine` on each GPU host: it installs the CLI, writes neurons/executor/.env, starts the node agent under docker compose, and self-checks. The single team-run validator SSHes in every 15 minutes to verify hardware/GPU/network/ports, create and remove rental pods, and report results. Emission splits three ways: rented pool (scored by GPU model/count), unrented pool (eligible idle GPUs), and burn. Rental income pays daily to your coldkey; emission pays per tempo to the hotkey.
playbook.minerJobProvide: ["Validator-passing GPU nodes under Sysbox isolation","Reachable renting ports for tenant pods","Competitive per-GPU-hour pricing","Idle-pay compliance (disk, pricing, power-limit)"]
playbook.top10Strategy: Marketplace capacity play: chain data shows the top-10 providers capture ~99% of incentive, so scale matters — many validator-clean nodes, good bandwidth, and market-priced listings. Newcomers: start with one consumer card to learn validator reason codes (INSUFFICIENT_PORTS, VERIFYX speed, sysbox failures), then scale only what passes consistently.
playbook.top10Levers: ["Node count × validator pass rate","Bandwidth >=100Mbps and port/NAT correctness","Pricing vs market soft limit for idle pool","Choosing eligible GPU models (GPU_MODEL_RATES)","Portal + Discord + central coordinator wiring"]
playbook.followTopMiners: Track provider.lium.io/rewards-calculator (live rates), the public node feed lium.io/api/public/v1/nodes, docs.lium.io/providers/rewards, taostats.io/subnet/51 top UIDs, and the Lium Discord #tickets for policy changes.

playbook.whatItDoes: Dojo V2 is a decentralized GAN with zero-sum incentives: in each task miners play Generator (produce the best completion - coding, 3D annotation, etc.) or Discriminator (vote on anonymous outputs), while validators orchestrate synthetic tasks, organic duels, and trap rounds. Outputs must beat a SOTA baseline, not just imitate it.
playbook.hardwareRec: Effectively CPU only - miners don't run servers: register with btcli, load the hotkey into a browser wallet (e.g. Talisman), and receive tasks. No VRAM requirement stated anywhere in repo or docs; completions can be LLM-assisted via your own tools.
playbook.keyRequirements: ["Register hotkey on SN52 mainnet (btcli s register --netuid 52) and use a browser wallet (Talisman) for tasks","Play both roles: Generator completions before expiry; Discriminator votes on anonymous output pairs","Trap rounds inject prompt/output augmentations with partial ground truth to catch dishonest discriminators","Collusion prevention: randomized task assignment and miner-miner voting pattern monitoring","No server or miner code to deploy - participation is task-driven"]
playbook.minerJob: A miner's day is task-driven: when a task arrives they either generate a high-quality completion for the prompt within the expiry window, or evaluate anonymous output pairs and vote for the superior one. Validators benchmark generators against SOTA baselines (synthetic tasks), run 1v1 organic duels, and inject trap rounds with augmented prompts/outputs; scoring rewards generators whose outputs win votes and discriminators whose votes match truth, with collusion penalized.
playbook.minerJobProvide: ["Generator completions that beat the validator's SOTA baseline","Honest, calibrated discriminator votes on anonymous outputs","On-time task completion before expiry windows close","Clean collusion record through randomized trap rounds"]
playbook.top10Strategy: Quality voting is the skill: generators need genuinely superior outputs (often LLM-assisted), while discriminators must judge honestly - trap rounds punish careless or collusive voting. Top miners build fast completion pipelines plus a consistent honest voting policy, and avoid voting blocs entirely since randomization detects them.
playbook.top10Levers: ["LLM-assisted generation tuned per task domain (coding, 3D annotation)","Truthful discrimination - trap rounds reward honest voters","Speed: completions must land before expiry","Never coordinate votes; randomization plus traps detect collusion","Zero-sum: aim to beat the baseline, not match it","Track task-type mix (synthetic vs organic) for scoring focus"]
playbook.followTopMiners: Watch taostats.io/subnet/52 weight and incentive distribution, Tensorplex docs and Discord for mechanism updates (trap/scoring changes), and the tensorplex-labs/dojo commit cadence (Go tooling evolves fast).

playbook.whatItDoes: engy serves frontier open-weight models on consumer GPUs with cryptographic verification: every response carries a TOPLOC activation fingerprint proving the pinned (Merkle-rooted) weights actually ran; a sampled recompute audit re-derives challenged matrix multiplies, and a failed opening is proof of cheating. Buyers pay engy.ai for completions; miners serve the traffic and earn subnet emissions.
playbook.hardwareRec: 2x RTX 4090/5090, or 1x L40S / RTX 6000 Ada (48GB), or H100/H200/B200. Repo runbook has a working 4x RTX 4090 reference for Qwen3.6-35B-A3B-FP8 via sglang. No TEE requirement - rented GPUs are workable.
playbook.keyRequirements: ["sglang serve with --enable-return-hidden-states + miner/ on PYTHONPATH","Miner key from provider.engy.ai; connect to wss://lb.engy.ai/gw","MAX_INFLIGHT >= 8 (declared serve concurrency, the gateway minimum)","Local checkpoint storage matching the published model spec/Merkle root","TOPLOC proof generation with every completion"]
playbook.minerJob: One process does everything: engy_miner.py connects to the gateway websocket, receives buyer completion requests routed for your declared model, generates via local sglang, and returns the completion plus a compact TOPLOC proof that the pinned model produced it. The gateway enforces the model's request-shape spec and your MAX_INFLIGHT; per-miner aggregates feed a master-signed epoch weight vector that light validators verify (sha256 digest + sr25519 signature) and resubmit on chain ~every 120 blocks. Rewards flow from verified serving volume in each epoch - more paid traffic served with valid proofs means more weight.
playbook.minerJobProvide: ["Verified completions for paying API traffic","TOPLOC activation fingerprints per response","Declared concurrency capacity (>=8 inflight)","Uptime on the gateway websocket"]
playbook.top10Strategy: This is an inference marketplace, not a benchmark: win by serving more paid tokens with clean proofs. Scale concurrency well past the 8 minimum, keep GPUs saturated and sglang current, and hold near-perfect proof-pass rate - failed audits are cheating evidence, not bad luck. Track which pinned models the gateway routes and resize hardware to the demand-weighted mix; cheap reliable hosting per token is the margin.
playbook.top10Levers: ["High MAX_INFLIGHT and tokens/sec throughput","Uptime and stable websocket sessions (lb.engy.ai endpoint)","TOPLOC/audit pass rate","GPU cost efficiency ($/served token)","Fast adoption of newly pinned model specs"]
playbook.followTopMiners: engy.ai API/pricing and provider.engy.ai stats; taostats.io/subnets/53 epoch weights; repo releases (audit verifier rollout); docs/SN53_ONE_PAGER.md and MINER.md changes.

playbook.whatItDoes: Yanez generates identity-preserving face image variations used to test and improve fraud detection, KYC, and deepfake/biometric verification systems. Miners run diffusion models to produce pose, lighting, expression, background, and screen-replay edits from validator seed faces; validators check identity preservation and quality. Financial institutions and IDV vendors consume the adversarial dataset.
playbook.hardwareRec: README overrides the CPU-only metadata: image generation is the only scored task and requires a GPU with 8GB+ VRAM (CUDA or Apple MPS), 16-32GB RAM, 80GB+ disk for FLUX diffusion weights. No rental ban documented; open port 8091 needed.
playbook.keyRequirements: ["GPU with 8GB+ VRAM (NVIDIA CUDA or Apple Silicon MPS) - required to earn","Hugging Face account and API token for diffusion model access","16GB+ RAM (32GB recommended), 80GB+ free disk, open port 8091","Produce identity-preserving variations: pose_edit, lighting_edit, expression_edit, background_edit, screen_replay","Results encrypted and uploaded to S3 with signed submission references"]
playbook.minerJob: Run neurons/miner.py under pm2: the miner receives base face images plus variation requirements from validators, generates the requested edits with the local FLUX diffusion stack, encrypts and uploads results to S3, and returns signed references. Validators run automated identity-preservation pre-checks plus manual validation; weights track variation quality and reputation. In the current cycle (Phase 4), image generation is the sole scored task.
playbook.minerJobProvide: ["Identity-preserving face image variations per validator spec","Encrypted S3 uploads with signed submission references","All five edit families including screen_replay (Cycle 2)","Quality that consistently passes identity-preservation checks"]
playbook.top10Strategy: The bar is identity preservation, not just attractive edits: tune diffusion guidance and strengths so the person stays recognizable while pose/lighting change convincingly. Follow the phase roadmap - penalties for repetitive or low-value submissions are coming in Phase 2+. Newcomers: an 8GB card suffices to start; differentiate on edit fidelity and turnaround speed rather than raw VRAM.
playbook.top10Levers: ["Identity-preservation fidelity across all edit families","Fast turnaround on validator variation challenges","FLUX stack tuning (guidance, strength, CUDA/MPS device)","Reputation built through validator manual-validation scores","Avoiding repetitive submissions ahead of planned penalties","Tracking the tao-ui-dashboard.yanez.ai leaderboard"]
playbook.followTopMiners: Watch the Yanez dashboard (tao-ui-dashboard.yanez.ai), taostats.io/subnets/54 weights, docs/miner.md updates in-repo, and the Yanez Discord channel for cycle changes.

playbook.whatItDoes: A decentralized generator of synthetic CRISPR experiment datasets for the HBB (beta-globin) gene locus. Validators broadcast dataset-generation tasks; miners produce lists of experiments (guide RNAs, targets, mutations, Cas systems, cell types) which validators score through a five-stage biological validation pipeline. Output feeds genome-editing ML research.
playbook.hardwareRec: Repo lists no GPU requirement — the workload is structured data generation (CPU; LLM-assisted generation plausible). Input metadata flags 'GPU required, model/VRAM unspecified' — confirm with the team before renting GPUs.
playbook.keyRequirements: ["Generate experiments per the task contract","Required: guideRNA, coordinates, mutation, Cas, cell type","Forbidden: predicted efficiencies/repair outcomes/labels","Upload datasets to validator-provided S3","Validation evolves: structural → statistical → biophysical → ML","Same challenge broadcast to all miners"]
playbook.minerJob: Receive the CRISPR task spec from validators, generate a diverse list of biologically plausible experiments conforming to the contract (20–23bp guideRNAs, PAM-valid targets, whitelisted HBB mutations like HbS, Cas9/Cas12a, approved cell types), and upload the dataset to the validator's S3 bucket. Validators alone compute biological outcomes through five progressive stages (syntax, statistical plausibility, biophysical simulation, cross-consistency ML, distributional fidelity to real CRISPR data) and weight miners by multi-stage scores. Predicting outcomes yourself is prohibited.
playbook.minerJobProvide: ["Structurally valid CRISPR experiment lists","Biologically plausible guide/target/mutation combos","High mutation-coverage diversity (HBB variants)","S3 dataset uploads per task","Datasets passing all five validation stages"]
playbook.top10Strategy: Rewards track distributional fidelity and realism, not volume: maximize coverage of allowed HBB variants, cell types and Cas choices while keeping GC content, PAM syntax and spatial statistics inside plausible ranges. Because stage 5 compares against real CRISPR data, miners who tune generation to real-data statistics outperform naive generators. Validation constraints tighten over time — adapt fast when stages evolve.
playbook.top10Levers: ["Distributional match to real CRISPR data","Max mutation/variant coverage within whitelist","Perfect structural compliance (PAM, guide length)","Diversity across cell types and Cas systems","Adapt as validation stages tighten","Throughput of dataset generation"]
playbook.followTopMiners: Track taostats.io/subnet/55 top UIDs, repo docs (miner_guide.md, evolving validation constraints), the Bittensor Discord, and commit cadence on genomesio/subnet-niome for validation-stage changes.

playbook.whatItDoes: G.O.D (Gradients on Demand) runs recurring training tournaments: miners submit open-source training code (repo plus exact commit); the validator runs that code on its own GPU trainers, evaluates the resulting models, and advances winners through rounds. Consumers get trained models, and winning repositories are published open-source at gradients-opensource.
playbook.hardwareRec: CPU only for the miner itself - training executes on validator-controlled GPU trainer infrastructure. You need a dev box to write/test training code plus 0.4-0.7 TAO entry fees per tournament.
playbook.keyRequirements: ["Submit a training repo plus exact commit; the validator validates then runs it on dedicated trainers","Entry fees: Environment 0.6 TAO, Text 0.7 TAO, Image 0.4 TAO","Weekly windows Monday 09:00/11:00/13:00 UTC (Environment/Text/Image); minimum 4-5 miners to activate","Group, knockout/final, and boss/champion rounds; PvP evaluation for Environment tournaments","Code must be open-source; winning repos are published to gradients-opensource","Tournament performance feeds validator weight setting"]
playbook.minerJob: The miner exposes training repositories for tournament tasks. Each week you prepare training code for the task family (instruct/chat/DPO/GRPO for Text, diffusion for Image, environment/PvP for Environment), submit the repo and commit when a tournament opens, pay the fee, and wait while validator-side trainers execute the code and evaluate outputs through rounds. Your between-tournament job is iterating on training code based on last round's evaluations. Weights come from tournament outcomes, not uptime or hardware.
playbook.minerJobProvide: ["Open-source training code per tournament task family","Validated repo+commit that trains successfully on validator trainers","Models that win evaluation rounds","Round-over-round iterative improvements","Entry fee paid per tournament entered"]
playbook.top10Strategy: You compete on training-code quality, evaluated blind on validator GPUs - so maximize what generalizes: robust hyperparameters, clean data pipelines, proven recipes (GRPO/DPO variants) that do not overfit one task. Track the api.gradients.io tournament endpoints and study prior winning repos on gradients-opensource to see what wins. Newcomers can place by entering consistently - minimum-miner thresholds mean tournaments sometimes barely fill.
playbook.top10Levers: ["Strong open training recipes (GRPO/DPO, diffusion)","Code robustness on unknown validator hardware","Studying winning repos at gradients-opensource","Consistent weekly entry with budgeted fees","Round-format awareness (boss/champion rounds)"]
playbook.followTopMiners: Watch api.gradients.io/v1/tournaments/active and /latest/details for winners, the gradients-opensource org for winning code, taostats.io/subnet/56 weight distribution, and the repo's docs/miner.md guide.

playbook.whatItDoes: Attune (Robotensor) is a robot-foundation-model subnet. First competition 'Vector': a policy (vector_v1.1) sees one demonstration of a task and must repeat it in a different scene. Miners submit policy weights on Hugging Face; validators duel each challenger against the current king in RoboTwin simulation; the lane's rewards go to the four most recent champions (40/30/20/10).
playbook.hardwareRec: Submission is only an HF repo + on-chain commit, but training a competitive vector_v1.1 policy needs real GPU (validator duel units use up to 34GB each; 1 unit/GPU). Rented GPU pods explicitly supported (vast.ai, lium.io via docker/build.sh) — rentals allowed.
playbook.keyRequirements: ["HF repo containing only model.safetensors (pinned tensors, no quantization tricks)","On-chain commitment with revision + sha256 digest (attune miner commit)","One submission per hotkey; earliest identical-weights commitment wins","Repo must stay public and unchanged — deletion dethrones and burns the share","Challenger must beat king by 3+ points avg success over 160 seeded units"]
playbook.minerJob: Train a vector_v1.1 policy, validate locally with attune miner check, upload to a public HF repo, then commit the `vector:<owner>/<repo>@<commit>.<digest>` string on-chain (commit before making public — earliest wins). The validator queues commitments oldest-first and duels each against the king on 160 units seeded from a finalized block. Rewards: lane share split 40/30/20/10 across the 4 most recent champions; weights are safetensors-only, never executed.
playbook.minerJobProvide: ["vector_v1.1 model.safetensors on a public HF repo","On-chain sha256 commitment matching the weights","Policies beating the king by 3+ points","Repo kept public/unchanged while holding a place"]
playbook.top10Strategy: Research race with a forgiving payout curve: four champion slots mean reaching top-4 once pays, and champion places decay only as newer champions arrive. Newcomers: start from the pinned vector_v1.1 spec, train on RoboTwin-Vector tasks, run pod-check --selftest on rented pods, and target the +3-point margin rather than perfection.
playbook.top10Levers: ["Policy training compute (rented GPU pods OK)","One-demo generalization across scene changes","Commit hygiene (digest, public repo, earliest wins)","Robustness across 160 duel seeds","Timing entry against champion churn"]
playbook.followTopMiners: Track the champion list via attune miner status / on-chain weights, the vector-orchestrator and RoboTwin-Vector repos for spec bumps, and current champions' HF repos for architecture hints.

playbook.whatItDoes: Bitsec rewards AI security agents that find high and critical severity vulnerabilities in real software projects. Miners submit agents; validators run them sandboxed against benchmark projects with known ground truth and score findings. Security teams wanting autonomous vuln discovery are the buyers; better agents earn more weight.
playbook.hardwareRec: CPU only. Agents call LLM APIs (Chutes or OpenRouter key) for inference; Docker handles local and sandbox runs. No GPU appears anywhere in the repo or docs - a modest always-on host suffices for miner flows.
playbook.keyRequirements: ["Implement miner/agent.py exposing agent_main() returning JSON with a top-level vulnerabilities list","Chutes or OpenRouter API key (INFERENCE_API_KEY) for agent inference","Register via bitsec.py miner create, then submit agent with the execution API key validators will use","Validators run agents in sandboxed project containers and score reports vs benchmark ground truth","Toolchain: Docker, Python 3.11+, uv; validators must be platform-activated by the Bitsec team"]
playbook.minerJob: Miners iteratively develop an autonomous vulnerability-discovery agent: run it directly, then through local no-Docker and Docker scoring flows against benchmark projects, review reports under jobs/, and finally submit agent.py plus the API key validators need to execute it. Validators pull job runs from the Bitsec platform, execute the agent in sandboxed containers on real codebases, evaluate reported vulnerabilities against ground truth, and send scores back for weight setting.
playbook.minerJobProvide: ["agent.py that autonomously produces structured vulnerability reports","High-precision findings on benchmark projects (ground-truth scored)","Valid inference API key enabling validator-side execution","Continuous agent improvements tracked through local scoring loops"]
playbook.top10Strategy: An agent-engineering competition: accuracy and precision - real high/critical vulns with few false positives - beat noisy scanning. Top miners pair strong reasoning LLMs with static-analysis tooling inside the agent and iterate cheaply via the local run-no-docker scorer. Watch API spend: inference cost is your marginal cost per analyzed project.
playbook.top10Levers: ["Agent architecture: multi-step reasoning, tool use, code comprehension","False-positive control - reports are scored against benchmark ground truth","Model selection via Chutes/OpenRouter for cost/quality tradeoffs","Use the local run-no-docker loop to iterate before submitting","Track docs.bitsec.ai incentive-mechanism updates","Generalize the agent across diverse benchmark project_keys"]
playbook.followTopMiners: Track taostats.io/subnet/60 weights, the docs.bitsec.ai incentive-mechanism page, Bitsec-AI/sandbox commit cadence for benchmark changes, and the Bitsec channel in the Bittensor Discord (validators must be platform-activated).

playbook.whatItDoes: RedTeam by Innerworks is a cybersecurity competitive-programming subnet: miners develop and submit code solutions to security challenges, scored daily on quality and innovation. Solutions feed real-world security products (dashboard.theredteam.io); a similarity system rejects copying, and softmax normalization plus decay keep pressure on continuous fresh contributions.
playbook.hardwareRec: CPU only (input metadata; nothing GPU-bound in the repo). A cheap VPS to run the miner process plus developer workstation time; costs are skill and iteration, not hardware.
playbook.keyRequirements: ["Registered hotkey running the miner service (docs/miner/README.md)","Solutions must be original - similarity checked against past and same-day submissions","Daily scoring cadence; decay requires regular refreshed submissions","Softmax-normalized quality scores set weights","Full docs at docs.theredteam.io"]
playbook.minerJob: Your miner receives challenges and submits code solutions through the validator pipeline. Once a day submissions are scored for how well they perform and how much new value they add; the similarity checker compares each new solution with previously accepted ones and same-day submissions, so recycling or paraphrasing gets rejected. Scores are softmax-normalized and a decay mechanism means incentives lapse if you stop submitting improved solutions. Consistent daily participation with genuinely novel, higher-performing solutions is what accumulates weights and emissions.
playbook.minerJobProvide: ["Novel code solutions to security challenges","Daily submission cadence (decay-resistant)","Measurable performance improvements over prior solutions","Original work that passes similarity checks"]
playbook.top10Strategy: Skill-and-novelty competition, not hardware: the top is whoever solves challenges better AND differently every day. Build a repeatable pipeline (human + LLM ideation, testing, submission) that generates genuinely new approaches, study prior accepted solutions to avoid similarity flags, and never skip days - decay punishes gaps. Copying is structurally unprofitable here.
playbook.top10Levers: ["Solution novelty vs the similarity checker","Core coding/CTF skill and tooling","Uninterrupted daily cadence","LLM-assisted ideation for fresh approaches","Tracking new challenge types early"]
playbook.followTopMiners: dashboard.theredteam.io for leaderboard/scoring; taostats.io/subnets/61 incentive and dividend spread; docs.theredteam.io for mechanism updates; repo commit cadence on scoring changes.

playbook.whatItDoes: Ridges is an open-source agent competition platform: miners upload a Python SWE agent (agent.py); validators pull the code and run it on benchmark software-engineering problems, evaluating outputs. The highest-scoring agent earns the emissions - a winner-takes-most tournament where miners compete and collaborate on one software engineering agent.
playbook.hardwareRec: No dedicated GPU: agents call LLM inference via OpenRouter, Targon, or Chutes at miner's cost. A small CPU box suffices for local Harbor testing; uploads need OpenRouter runtime plus management keys. Rented cloud adds nothing beyond a cheap VPS.
playbook.keyRequirements: ["agent.py implementing agent_main(input) -> str (a diff), validated locally via ridges miner run-local","Upload via ridges upload - burns alpha unless you hold a team-granted one-shot credit","OpenRouter API key plus management key required for uploads","Inference billed to the miner (OpenRouter/Targon/Chutes providers)","Local runs use the same miner-facing contract as validators (Harbor tasks)"]
playbook.minerJob: Day-to-day this is agent engineering, not serving: iterate agent.py - prompting, planning, tool use, retrieval around an LLM - validate on local Harbor tasks via ridges miner run-local, then upload to the platform. Validators run submitted agents on benchmark problems in sandboxes and score outputs; the top-scoring agent takes the emission share. Your recurring costs are LLM tokens during both practice and evaluation.
playbook.minerJobProvide: ["A competitive software-engineering agent solving Harbor benchmark tasks","Generated diffs/patches on benchmark problems","Provider-key-backed inference that runs inside validator sandboxes","Iterative agent improvements across uploads"]
playbook.top10Strategy: It is a tournament: only the highest-scoring agent earns, so incremental prompt tweaks rarely pay - you need measurably better agentic strategy on the benchmark suite. Iterate cheaply with run-local using the identical contract, study which problems the benchmark emphasizes, and upload only when local results beat your current best. Newcomers: adapt strong open-source SWE agent patterns, then specialize where they lag.
playbook.top10Levers: ["Agent architecture quality on SWE benchmarks (planning and tool use)","Local Harbor iteration before burning an upload","Token-cost-efficient provider choice (OpenRouter/Targon/Chutes)","Upload credits from the Ridges team instead of burn","Studying the benchmark problem distribution","Incorporating top open-source SWE agent techniques"]
playbook.followTopMiners: Track the leaderboard and guides at docs.ridges.ai, taostats.io/subnets/62, ridgesai/ridges commit cadence (miners/ toolkit changes), and the Ridges Discord; upload burn-vs-credit status shows in CLI output.

playbook.whatItDoes: A bounty-based challenge subnet, not a production work network: emissions accumulate in an on-chain Treasury Wallet to fund prize pools for deep-tech challenges (currently Breaking RSA with Terra Quantum and Hardening Quantum Proof with BlueQubit). Solvers compete to break targets first; the winner drains the pool and winning solutions are open-sourced.
playbook.hardwareRec: Minimum is 1 CPU core / 8 GB RAM, but winning is compute-bound: RSA milestones fall to serious CPU+GPU number-theory rigs (RSA-460 fell in 3.9 h to a GPU lattice siever). The quantum challenge rewards strong CPU/RAM simulation setups.
playbook.keyRequirements: ["Submit source-code solutions, not just answers","Small TAO fee per submission; unlimited resubmits","Test first via enigma-workbench Docker mode","RSA solutions run in 4h-walled Docker containers","No ongoing emissions — prizes only","Winning code is open-sourced after verification"]
playbook.minerJob: Pick a live challenge (e.g. factor the current RSA milestone), develop a solver in the provided workbench, and validate locally with `enigma-workbench test`. Submit the solution directory; validators run it in fixed, network-isolated Docker environments (RSA: RTX PRO 6000-class host, 4-hour wall time) and verify output. The first valid solution drains the prize pool via validator-governed treasury payout (60% threshold, 50% quorum, timelock). Expect no per-epoch income — this is discrete bounty hunting with each milestone harder than the last.
playbook.minerJobProvide: ["Working source-code solutions to live challenges","Workbench-validated submissions","Record-setting factorization / peaked-circuit results","Open-source methods building on prior winners","Reproducible runs inside the 4h Docker contract"]
playbook.top10Strategy: Treat it as a research bounty: read the published winning code (each win is open-sourced) and compound on it — the Level-2 quantum winner built directly on Level-1's release. Hardware edge matters (GPU lattice sieving broke RSA-460/480), so estimate your compute against the 4-hour wall before paying submission fees. Solve milestones early: pools grow while unsolved, but first valid solution takes all.
playbook.top10Levers: ["Specialized algorithms (GNFS sieving, MPS beam search)","GPU-accelerated compute within the 4h contract","Building on open-sourced prior winners","Workbench validation before paid submission","Early entry while pools accumulate","Track milestone difficulty progression"]
