playbook.whatItDoes: Chutes is Bittensor's serverless AI inference marketplace: miners operate GPU worker nodes that run community-deployed 'chutes' (vLLM/Python apps) and earn from real user inference traffic plus subnet emissions. It is the largest consumer-facing inference network; earnings scale with hardware size, uptime, and served demand.
playbook.hardwareRec: 8x H200-class node per platform data. Hard rules: bare metal/dedicated only (no Runpod/Vast), Intel TDX-capable CPUs with TEE via sek8s host-tools, unique static IP with 1:1 port mapping, RAM >= VRAM per GPU. Rental marketplaces banned.
playbook.keyRequirements: ["Bare metal/dedicated server only - Runpod, Vast, and shared hosting will not work","TEE-exclusive: GPU nodes run inside Intel TDX confidential VMs via sek8s host-tools (chutes/tee=true label)","Unique static IPs with 1:1 port mapping; no shared or dynamic IPs","RAM >= VRAM per GPU; TDX-capable Intel CPUs required","Miner software at rayonlabs/chutes-miner; GraVal GPU verification middleware","Legacy GraVal-only verification no longer supported - TDX enforced"]
playbook.minerJob: Operate a GPU worker node joined to the chutes Kubernetes fabric (sek8s) inside an Intel TDX confidential VM. The node pulls and serves chute images (vLLM-based model apps), handles encrypted inference traffic routed by the chutes API, and passes periodic hardware/TEE verification. Income comes from actual per-token inference revenue distributed on top of Yuma emissions - idle nodes earn little, so served demand and model coverage matter as much as raw specs.
playbook.minerJobProvide: ["TEE-attested GPU inference capacity (TDX confidential VM)","Served user inference across deployed chutes","High uptime with static-IP reachability","Authentic hardware attestation (GraVal/TEE checks)","Model coverage matching user demand"]
playbook.top10Strategy: Chutes rewards real revenue capture, not spec-sheet presence: run hardware matching high-demand chutes (8x H200-class), keep TDX/sek8s tooling current, and maximize served traffic with strong uptime. Entry cost is high - dedicated TDX-capable servers - so model break-even against per-token rates at api.chutes.ai/pricing before buying. Newcomers rarely beat established fleets on price; target underserved models or regions instead.
playbook.top10Levers: ["Served inference volume (revenue share)","TDX-capable dedicated hardware at competitive $/GPU-hour","Uptime and fast chute cold-starts","Model coverage aligned with demand","Staying current with sek8s/TEE tooling releases"]
playbook.followTopMiners: Watch taostats.io/subnet/64 top UIDs and emission concentration, api.chutes.ai/pricing for GPU rates, rayonlabs/chutes-miner and chutesai/sek8s commit cadence, and the Chutes Discord for TEE rollout changes.

playbook.whatItDoes: TPN (True Performance Network) incentivizes miners to build high-performance quantized language models. It runs recurring competitions with defined benchmarks, scoring windows and emission distributions. Miners benchmark their own GGUF models and submit the model plus benchmark run ids via a TimeLocked Commit — hidden until scoring so submissions can't be copied — and validators verify and rank verified scores.
playbook.hardwareRec: GPU for building/quantizing/testing GGUF models locally (size depends on competition); note the graded benchmarks run on the subnet's paid benchmark service, not your box, so no huge inference rig is strictly required. HF account required. Rentals fine for training/quantization.
playbook.keyRequirements: ["tpn CLI + hotkey registered on netuid 65","One .gguf per private HF repo (upload metadata saved)","BENCHMARK_API_KEY with credits — you pay for your own benchmark runs","TimeLocked Commit with run ids; auto-reveals at commit_end_block","Publish the HF repo public before the scoring phase; optional miner collateral"]
playbook.minerJob: Workflow via tpn: register, upload your .gguf to a private HF repo, run `tpn benchmark` (quotes each required benchmark against your credit, saves run ids), `tpn commit` the TimeLocked payload on chain, then `tpn publish` before scoring. Validators verify every run id benchmarked exactly the committed repo/revision/file, then check top candidates for RAM usage, file integrity and base-model provenance before distributing emissions by verified rank. Incomplete runs at scoring time score 0.
playbook.minerJobProvide: ["Quantized GGUF models matched to each competition","Paid benchmark run ids matching the commit exactly","Public HF repo before the scoring phase","Integrity- and provenance-clean submissions"]
playbook.top10Strategy: Quantization craft plus benchmark economics: maximize benchmark score per RAM-usage constraint, and cheaply re-run single weak benchmarks (--only X --rerun) to replace bad runs. Newcomers: read docs/Overview.md, start from strong provenance-clean base models, budget credits before committing, and never miss the scoring-phase deadline.
playbook.top10Levers: ["Quantization quality vs benchmark score","Base-model provenance (checked on top candidates)","Benchmark-credit budgeting and rerun strategy","Competition selection (rules/emission splits)","RAM-usage and file-integrity compliance"]
playbook.followTopMiners: Watch `tpn competitions --all` and the leader validator API (val0.trueperformancenetwork.com) for active competitions and leaderboards, docs/Miner.md changes, and taostats.io/subnet/65 for emission distribution.

playbook.whatItDoes: Conjectures.io pays for Lean 4 proofs of open mathematical conjectures drawn from DeepMind's formal-conjectures: a miner pays 0.5 TAO, submits a proof bundle, and a hardened isolated verifier checks it with the Lean kernel. The first Lean-valid proof of a target earns the locked bounty; payment buys verification and never influences the verdict.
playbook.hardwareRec: CPU only. Lean theorem proving and Mathlib builds are CPU/RAM work (builds are lengthy); no GPU anywhere in the pipeline. A strong multicore Linux box with ample RAM and disk for Mathlib/toolchain builds is the practical setup.
playbook.keyRequirements: ["0.5 TAO per proof-verification attempt (credits via treasury deposit or TMC PAY); rejected proofs cost nothing pre-submit","Use conjectures-miner CLI; pre-verify locally with verifier bundle scan/verify before any TAO moves","Submission bundle: exact task ID + digest, coldkey signature, idempotency key, payment reference","Eligible tasks come from the audited pool over google-deepmind/formal-conjectures (pinned commit)","One reward per theorem target: first Lean-valid proof holds the bounty; later proofs earn nothing"]
playbook.minerJob: A miner picks an eligible conjecture, works out the mathematics, formalizes it in Lean 4 with Mathlib, and iterates locally with the same verifier the validator runs (bundle scan/verify - free). When confident, they pay 0.5 TAO and POST the bundle to the submission API; a verification worker checks the exact proof bytes in an isolated Landlock/seccomp container with the Lean kernel. Lean-valid proofs pass to the reward pipeline; the winner receives the submission-time locked bounty, priced from treasury balance.
playbook.minerJobProvide: ["Lean 4 proof bundles for eligible committed conjecture tasks","Payment (0.5 TAO) plus coldkey-signed submission via the API","Locally pre-verified proofs so paid attempts are near-certain wins","First valid proof of a target, which claims its locked bounty"]
playbook.top10Strategy: Deep formal-math skill compounds: maintain a strong Lean/Mathlib codebase, target conjectures where you hold an edge, and always pre-verify locally so paid attempts are near-certain. Bounty pricing scales with the treasury, so hunting neglected high-value targets beats racing crowds on obvious ones.
playbook.top10Levers: ["Lean 4 + Mathlib fluency - the core moat","Free local verification before every paid submission","Task selection: bounty size vs difficulty vs competition","Watch the audited task pool and pins.lock.json updates","Track docs/MINER.md workflow and bounty/pricing changes","Budget: 0.5 TAO per attempt; post-submit failures aren't refunded"]

playbook.whatItDoes: Harnyx turns deep research into a competition: miners submit Python agent scripts, validators execute them in sandboxes against research queries with stronger reference answers, and a pairwise judge scores responses. Emission splits between a champion artifact (up to 50% max) and participants, multiplied by stage (top-50%/top-10%/main) and novelty (near_duplicate 1x to novel 10x).
playbook.hardwareRec: CPU-only runner: agents execute in validator sandboxes and the miner CLI is lightweight. Real costs are model/tool API spend inside a tight tool budget. No GPU appears anywhere in the repo.
playbook.keyRequirements: ["Python agent implementing the SDK `query` entrypoint","10 qualifying tasks, then up to 30 participants run 20 shared main tasks","Tight tool budget; ties prefer lower total tool cost","Novelty preflight classifies artifacts (near_duplicate/notable_change/novel)","Dethroning needs +10pp score, or -10% median cost, or -10% runtime (>=1000ms)"]
playbook.minerJob: You develop and submit agent scripts via the miner CLI; the platform batches each with research queries and expensive reference answers. Validators poll the work ledger, run script x task in the sandbox, score comparison_score (judge vs reference, run twice with swapped order), and submit weights. Emission: a newly selected champion artifact has a 50% maximum (first retention 25%, later 12.5% floor) scaled by champion score; participants share the remainder proportional to stage multiplier (1/2/5) times novelty multiplier (1/3/5/10); failed batches split the entire emission equally among distinct participant hotkeys; uid=0 remainder burns.
playbook.minerJobProvide: ["Python research agent scripts (decompose/retrieve/cross-check/synthesize)","Answers with citations and optional notes","Low tool-cost, low-runtime solutions","Novel (non-duplicate) artifacts each batch"]
playbook.top10Strategy: Two viable routes: chase champion (50% max, but dethroning needs a hard +10pp score or -10% cost/runtime margin) or farm participant shares as a reliable top-10% agent with novel artifacts (5x stage x 10x novelty = 50x multiplier weight). Optimize answer quality per tool-cost dollar, keep runtime tight, and never resubmit near-duplicates - novelty classification drives everything.
playbook.top10Levers: ["Agent harness quality on research tasks","Tool-cost efficiency (tie-breaker and -10% dethrone path)","Runtime speed (>=1000ms dethrone path)","Artifact novelty classification","Consistent batch participation (failed batches still pay)"]
playbook.followTopMiners: dashboard.harnyx.ai/benchmark live run detail; GET /v1/weights emission allocations per hotkey; repo data-version bumps (rules change often); taostats.io/subnets/67.

playbook.whatItDoes: NOVA does high-throughput ML-driven drug screening: miners run Boltz-2 and BoltzGen inference to score binding/affinity and generate candidate compounds across huge chemical spaces. Pharma researchers get cheap screening at a fraction of normal cost; miners with serious GPUs earn by completing validator scoring rounds reliably and on time.
playbook.hardwareRec: 2x GPUs each >48GB VRAM for parallel Boltz-2 inference - a single GPU runs sequentially and risks delayed/missing scoring rounds. CUDA 12.6, Ubuntu 24.04, Python 3.10-3.12, ample RAM. A100/H100-class or 48GB+ pro cards; rental A100/H100 viable. Tune with tools/calibrate_perf.py.
playbook.keyRequirements: ["2 GPU devices with >48GB VRAM each (parallel inference; one GPU = sequential = missed rounds)","CUDA 12.6 environment; clone with --recurse-submodules for the Boltz stack","GitHub personal access token with repo access for your submission repository","Tuned env: NOVA_BOLTZ_SHARDS, NOVA_BOLTZ_GPUS mapping, NOVA_MAX_CONCURRENT_TNP","Missing or delayed scoring rounds directly cost rewards"]
playbook.minerJob: Operate neurons/miner.py continuously: validators dispatch compound-screening batches; the miner runs Boltz-2 structure/co-folding inference (shard processes spread across 2 GPUs) plus BoltzGen generation, returns candidate scores, and commits submissions to a GitHub repo the validators read. Rewards flow from completing each scoring round within the window - throughput and round-completion rate drive weights, so GPU sharding and uptime are the job.
playbook.minerJobProvide: ["Boltz-2 binding/affinity scores for validator-sent compound batches","BoltzGen candidate generation for chemical-space exploration","GitHub-hosted submission artifacts via scoped PAT","On-time completion of every scoring round"]
playbook.top10Strategy: Throughput and reliability win: rewards hinge on finishing rounds fast, so GPU sharding via calibrate_perf.py, pinned drivers, and uptime dominate. Two 48GB+ cards are effectively mandatory - single-GPU setups run sequentially and miss rounds. Newcomers should rent A100/H100-class hardware rather than consumer cards and verify a full round completes inside the window before scaling up.
playbook.top10Levers: ["Parallel 2-GPU sharding tuned via tools/calibrate_perf.py","Round-completion rate (zero missed scoring rounds)","48GB+/A100/H100-class hardware headroom","Stable GitHub submission pipeline (PAT scopes)","CUDA 12.6 environment and auto-update discipline","NOVA_MAX_CONCURRENT_TNP throughput tuning"]
playbook.followTopMiners: Watch taostats.io/subnets/68 top UIDs and round consistency, metanova-labs/nova commit cadence (inference version changes shift performance), and open repo issues or contact the NOVA team for validator API keys.

playbook.whatItDoes: A verified media-placement subnet: PR firms and contributors publish editorial articles in real news outlets against briefs. Validators run a code-only verification oracle checking each article on the outlet's own page (signed registry, brief window, topic match, not-paid-content, text match) and weight the contributor's hotkey by verified USD value; uncovered emission burns.
playbook.hardwareRec: CPU only — in fact no miner server at all. The real 'hardware' is PR placement: you need real outlets willing to publish on-brief editorial content. Hotkey is registered through the Herald website with a wallet extension.
playbook.keyRequirements: ["Register hotkey on netuid 69 via Herald website","Google sign-in + wallet extension (Talisman/SubWallet/Polkadot.js)","Upload article text BEFORE publishing","Add live link; outlet must be in the signed registry","Article must stay live through a 30-day vesting window","Miner neuron deprecated — no server needed"]
playbook.minerJob: There is no miner service: contributors register a hotkey on the website, pick an open brief (topic, optional date window, prepaid reward pool), upload the draft before publication, then add the published link. Once per daily epoch each validator verifies signatures, coldkey-hotkey ownership, outlet-registry membership, timing, topic, text match and paid-content status. Verified articles vest value by outlet tier and search presence in daily installments over 30 days; removal or conversion to paid content forfeits the rest. Emissions flow to your hotkey pro rata to payable USD.
playbook.minerJobProvide: ["Verified editorial articles in real outlets","On-brief topic coverage","Pre-publication signed text uploads","30-day article persistence","Registered hotkey earning emission shares"]
playbook.top10Strategy: Rewards scale with outlet tier and search presence, so placement quality beats article count — one high-tier placement in a pooled brief can outweigh many low-tier posts. Choose briefs with prepaid pools and less competition, keep articles live for the full 30-day vest, and never let outlets tag them as paid. When contributor value exceeds the day's emission it's shared pro rata.
playbook.top10Levers: ["High-tier outlet placements","Briefs with prepaid reward pools","30-day persistence (vesting discipline)","Topic fidelity to brief requirements","Not-paid-content compliance","Search-visible articles (pricing input)","Disciplined upload-then-publish workflow"]

playbook.whatItDoes: Leadpoet is an AI sales-intelligence competition: miners improve an open-source sales-research agent that finds companies matching hidden ICPs with verifiable intent evidence. A daily arena evaluates submitted agents on 20 hidden ICPs; buyers get qualified B2B leads. The champion's code becomes the next public baseline and earns the largest emission share for weeks.
playbook.hardwareRec: CPU only - agents run via approved brokered APIs (OpenRouter, Scrapingdog, Deepline) inside the sandboxed gateway. Your real costs are API spend (about $4 sourcing limit per ICP) and engineering time.
playbook.keyRequirements: ["Implement harness.run_icp(icp) returning at most 5 companies as JSON with evidence","Include the verbatim Tyche AGPL-3.0 LICENSE beside harness.py (checked at upload and gateway)","No direct network access - use the broker protocol with approved operations only","$4 sourcing limit per ICP across OpenRouter/Scrapingdog/Deepline; $0.80 per qualified company for cost eligibility","Daily rounds: submit on Day 0 while 20 ICPs stay hidden; evaluation starts ~00:00 UTC Day 1","Champion must beat the daily baseline by >=0.5 points and keep API credentials funded (else -50% incentive)"]
playbook.minerJob: Mine by engineering, not serving: fork the leadpoet-sales-agent baseline (lab branch), improve the run_icp research pipeline (search, intent-signal matching, evidence verification), and submit your archive via the CLI to the gateway. Each round runs your agent on 20 hidden ICPs under frozen tool and cost limits; scorers verify fit, intent, evidence, and cost eligibility. The top eligible agent beating the baseline by the margin is promoted as the next baseline; the champion earns 30%, 24%, 18%, 12%, then 6% of emissions across successive 140-epoch reward weeks.
playbook.minerJobProvide: ["Submitted agent archive passing license and schema checks","Qualified companies with verified intent evidence per ICP","Cost-eligible sourcing within $4/ICP and $0.80/company limits","Output schema v6 compliance (intent_details paragraph)","Beat-baseline performance to claim champion weeks"]
playbook.top10Strategy: A research-agent engineering race with compounding rewards: the champion keeps earning for weeks (30% down to 6%), so one great agent pays repeatedly. Win by maximizing verified-company yield per sourcing dollar - smart provider routing, tight intent-signal filtering, bulletproof evidence URLs. Check /arena/v1/current for each round's pinned schema and policy markers; small schema mistakes zero companies. A newcomer can beat a public baseline quickly with better search discipline.
playbook.top10Levers: ["Verified-company yield per sourcing dollar","Schema and policy compliance per round markers","Provider routing efficiency (OpenRouter/Scrapingdog/Deepline)","Evidence quality that passes independent judging","Daily submission cadence (the baseline moves daily)"]
playbook.followTopMiners: Track the subnet71.com leaderboard and champion reigns, repo round publications (scores and baselines), /arena/v1/current policy markers, taostats.io/subnet/71 emission shares, and the Leadpoet Discord for round changes.

playbook.whatItDoes: NATIX StreetVision is a decentralized image-classification subnet: miners run binary classifiers that detect roadwork/construction sites in images, outputting a float 0-1 (above 0.5 = roadwork). Validators challenge miners with balanced mixes of real and synthetic media and reward accuracy. The subnet powers construction-site detection for NATIX applications.
playbook.hardwareRec: Entry-level GPU suffices: input metadata cites GTX 1660 Super 4GB; any small CUDA card runs the classifiers. Model submissions go to HuggingFace; resubmit within 90 days to keep reward factor 1. Consumer setups and rentals both fine.
playbook.keyRequirements: ["Registered hotkey; axon answering image queries with [0,1] floats","Public HuggingFace model submission required","90-day validity: reward factor 1, then decays to zero","Robustness to synthetic/generated images in validator challenge pools","Continuous retraining/re-submission culture"]
playbook.minerJob: Serve an axon that scores incoming images for roadwork presence. Validators send balanced real+synthetic batches (new datasets and generative models are continually added on the validator side, config in natix/validator/config.py) and grade accuracy; weights follow accuracy multiplied by your model's time-decay reward factor. Day-to-day: keep the axon online, retrain improved classifiers, and re-submit to HuggingFace before the 90-day decay bites.
playbook.minerJobProvide: ["Roadwork classifier responses (float 0-1)","Public HuggingFace model submissions","Re-submission within each 90-day window","Accuracy on real + generative-image mixes"]
playbook.top10Strategy: Accuracy race against an evolving synthetic challenge set: fine-tune on diverse real and generated data, calibrate the 0.5 threshold, and maintain a retraining cadence so the 90-day decay never erodes your factor. Newcomers can start on a 4GB card; the NATIX HuggingFace org and W&B logs provide baselines.
playbook.top10Levers: ["Classifier accuracy on real+synthetic mixes","Retraining cadence vs 90-day decay","Cheap consumer-GPU inference latency","Threshold/calibration tuning","Tracking new validator datasets/generators"]

playbook.whatItDoes: Gittensor pays TAO for real, merged pull requests to whitelisted open-source repositories. Validators verify GitHub account ownership via a fine-grained PAT, confirm merges, and score contributions by semantic code quality (AST/token weights), programming language, and per-repo emission shares. It monetizes genuine OSS work.
playbook.hardwareRec: CPU only - no miner neuron or GPU: register a GitHub PAT with validators via CLI; the work is actual software development on your normal machine. The input's RTX 5090 hint has no repo support; ignore it.
playbook.keyRequirements: ["Merged PRs into whitelisted repos (dynamic list; favors repos with contributing guidelines and activity)","Fine-grained GitHub PAT broadcast to validators (gitt miner post) proving account ownership","Bittensor wallet registered on SN74; no always-on miner process needed","Scoring: semantic code quality (AST token-based), language/extension weights, repo emission-share caps","Sybil resistance: merge requirement plus account verification; quality over quantity"]
playbook.minerJob: There is nothing to deploy: a miner contributes code to recognized OSS projects as usual. After PRs merge, validators authenticate the GitHub account via the stored PAT, inspect the merged diffs, and score them semantically against token/AST weights and the repo's emission share. Rewards distribute within each repository's configured share per round, so income tracks the scored value of merged contributions, not raw commit counts.
playbook.minerJobProvide: ["Real, merged pull requests to whitelisted open-source repositories","A fine-grained GitHub PAT registered with validators for ownership proof","High semantic-quality code changes (features, fixes, structure)","Ongoing maintenance of contributions as repos evolve"]
playbook.top10Strategy: Treat it as monetized OSS engineering: pick repos whose emission shares fit your expertise, land substantial high-quality merged PRs (features, fixes - not typo sprees), and follow whitelist/emission changes. Consistency compounds across scoring rounds; deep contributions to a high-share repo beat scattered small ones.
playbook.top10Levers: ["Target repos with generous emission shares (list evolves; request additions)","High-value PRs: features, bug fixes, performance - semantic scoring rewards structure","Language choice matters: extension weights affect scores","Merged status is mandatory - shepherd PRs through review","Keep the PAT valid; verify with gitt miner check","Watch docs.gittensor.io for reward-algorithm updates"]

playbook.whatItDoes: Hippius is decentralized infrastructure: distributed file storage (IPFS + S3), compute (miners act as hypervisors hosting user VMs), and blockchain management, with a reputation-based marketplace, address-linked authorization, and slashing for bad actors. Users pay to store files and run VMs; node operators earn rewards tracked per node type on-chain.
playbook.hardwareRec: Role-dependent, README gives no single GPU spec: storage miners need disk + bandwidth (IPFS nodes, dedicated storage), compute miners need virtualization-capable hosts; a GpuMiner node type exists but is unspecified here. Entry-level storage/compute roles run on CPU/VPS-class boxes.
playbook.keyRequirements: ["Run the stack for your role: IPFS node (storage) or hypervisor (compute)","Offchain workers monitoring capacity, file health, replication, metrics","Stable uptime and passing validator pin-checks/latency challenges","Reputation system compliance; blacklist/ban and slashing for bad actors","Reward state queryable via Node Metrics RPC per node type"]
playbook.minerJob: Storage miners run IPFS nodes and dedicated storage, pin approved user files, and monitor file health/replication via offchain workers; compute miners operate hypervisors fulfilling on-chain VM requests (status, VNC port, hypervisor IP all tracked). Validators verify network operations, collect performance data, run pin checks and latency challenges, and manage replication/task assignment. Rewards accumulate per account and node type (StorageMiner, StorageS3, ComputeMiner, GpuMiner) and are readable via RPC (get_total_node_rewards, pending rewards). Reliable, challenged-passing infrastructure earns; misbehavior gets blacklisted or slashed.
playbook.minerJobProvide: ["Reliable IPFS pinning and replication of approved files","S3-compatible storage availability","VM hosting uptime for compute requests","Challenge responses (pin checks, latency)","Honest offchain-worker telemetry"]
playbook.top10Strategy: Infrastructure subnets reward boring reliability: maximize uptime, bandwidth, and disk, pass every challenge, and build reputation before scaling capacity. Start with cheap storage nodes to accumulate reputation and rewards data via the RPC, then expand into compute/GPU roles where your coverage is differentiated. Avoid any blacklist/slashing events - they compound badly.
playbook.top10Levers: ["Uptime and availability across node types","Disk capacity and bandwidth headroom","Pin-check/latency challenge pass rate","Reputation accumulation over time","Multi-role coverage (storage + compute)"]
playbook.followTopMiners: Node Metrics RPC (get_miners_total_rewards by node type shows who actually earns); taostats.io/subnets/75 weights; thenervelab/thebrain commit cadence; Hippius community channels for marketplace changes.

playbook.whatItDoes: Ormas pays for accepted outcomes, not inference turns. A client describes a code change plus the acceptance test that proves it; miners offer firm or limit prices for the whole task, deliver the change, and are paid only when validators re-run the acceptance tests successfully. It is an outcome-priced decentralized coding marketplace on Bittensor.
playbook.hardwareRec: CPU box plus your own agentic coding stack (the subnet's mining logic stays private); plug in solve(), powered by LLM API spend. Verification runs in a digest-pinned OCI sandbox with no network. No GPU; cost is model tokens.
playbook.keyRequirements: ["Runner key from ormas.ai (register-only until the operator approves qualification)","Actually run draft.verify_command; receipts must be honest (no fabricated zeros, scope_ok computed from git)","Firm or limit offers with 0 < estimate_usd <= limit_usd; you bear costs above the limit","task:code cell; a qualification proof job is reserved on registration","Agentic solve pipeline is your private competitive edge (reference solver earns nothing real)"]
playbook.minerJob: Run the ormas-miner runner or MinerSkeleton with your solve(): register, bind repos, poll the gateway queue for task leases, clone the repo at the base commit, run your agentic solver to produce a commit, execute the client's verify_command in a credential-free environment, and publish an honest receipt (usage metering, git-derived scope, real verification exit code). Validators reproduce the base failure and re-run acceptance tests before payment; accepted deliveries pay your firm or settled price.
playbook.minerJobProvide: ["Accepted code changes passing client acceptance tests","Honest TaskReceipts (usage metering, git scope, verify exit code)","Firm/limit price offers per task","Completed qualification for the task:code cell"]
playbook.top10Strategy: Profitability = acceptance rate x price minus token cost. Estimate limits honestly (set the limit at your worst-case recovery chain, settle at metered cost); pick tasks where your agent demonstrably succeeds - repository familiarity beats breadth. Phase 1 accepts the first offer within the client's undisclosed spending limit, so fast, accurate offering matters. Newcomers: run the local quickstart loop, qualify, then specialize in narrow task types where verify passes reliably.

playbook.whatItDoes: A liquidity-mining subnet: SN77 token holders vote on Uniswap V3 liquidity pools; a central server computes miner weights from votes and in-range LP positions, and validators set those weights on-chain. Miners earn by providing concentrated liquidity to voted pools — emissions flow pro rata to position quality and depth.
playbook.hardwareRec: CPU only (a laptop runs the CLI). The real resource is capital in Uniswap V3 positions: weight = liquidity depth × Gaussian proximity to the current tick, so active range management matters more than any server hardware.
playbook.keyRequirements: ["Register hotkey ↔ EVM address (`just register`)","In-range Uniswap V3 positions only (strict tick check)","Weights recomputed ~every 5 min from live ticks","Fee tier sets scoring std-dev (100→10 ... 10000→500)","Bittensor wallet with stake on subnet 77","Miners need MINER_HOTKEY and ETH_KEY in .env"]
playbook.minerJob: Link your hotkey to an EVM address, then open and manage concentrated Uniswap V3 liquidity positions in pools that token holders have voted weight onto. Every ~5 minutes the server recomputes pool emissions from alpha-weighted votes, then scores each position (Gaussian of distance to range bounds, midpoint 4× weighted, scaled by liquidity/1e9) and normalizes within each pool. Your miner weight is your share of voted pool emissions — no servers run day-to-day, just active LP management monitored via `bun run pools`.
playbook.minerJobProvide: ["In-range Uniswap V3 liquidity in voted pools","Registered hotkey↔EVM linkage","Actively managed tick ranges near price","Deep liquidity (score scales with size)","Continuous position monitoring"]
playbook.top10Strategy: This is quantitative LP management: rewards favor positions tightly concentrated around the current price (Gaussian scoring, midpoint 4× weight) in pools capturing the most vote-weighted emissions. Narrow ranges earn more but churn with price — balance width against repositioning frequency and impermanent loss. Watch which pools voters favor (voting power = voter alpha share) and move liquidity there early.
playbook.top10Levers: ["Tight in-range positions near current tick","Target pools with highest vote weight","Large liquidity depth","Midpoint-centered range placement (4× weight)","Active repositioning as price moves","Low-fee-tier std-dev advantage (100→10)","Monitor /pools + /positions for shifts"]

playbook.whatItDoes: MVTRX/τaos runs an agent-based market simulation: miners host trading strategies inside a C++ limit-order-book simulator with L3 data and background agents, scored on intraday Kappa-3 (risk-adjusted) with minimum trading volume. playbook.hardwareRec: CPU-only for trading: no set requirements; base tooling ~1GB RAM per miner instance (VPS works). Optional NVIDIA 6-8GB VRAM GPU for GenTRX training; CPU-only training supported but may miss deadlines. No GPU for the main 95% pool.

playbook.minerJob: Your agent receives L3 order-book state updates from validators each tick and returns place/cancel instructions; the simulation pauses while awaiting you, and your response time determines the delay (slippage) applied to your orders. Scores use intraday Kappa-3 plus activity requirements, on a rolling window across runs that reset weekly. GenTRX opt-in trains the shared model on your assigned data slice in a background thread and uploads compressed gradients to a personal S3 bucket for validator scoring (~95/5 pool split).

playbook.whatItDoes: Reliquary runs decentralized GRPO training on Qwen3-4B-Base: miners spend their own GPU compute searching for prompts at the policy's learning frontier, generating 16-rollout groups the trainer verifies (GRAIL sketches), ranks, and trains on. Miners are paid for verified, useful rollout groups - not raw volume. Checkpoints publish to Hugging Face as the model improves.
playbook.hardwareRec: 1-2x NVIDIA GPUs with >=24GB VRAM each (docs/mining.md hardware table). Reference config runs generation and proof on separate devices; one larger device works. Two Qwen3-4B replicas plus 16 concurrent 8192-token rollouts stress VRAM. Rented GPUs fine.
playbook.keyRequirements: ["Pinned miner image + V1 profile env (qwen3-4b-base-dapo-reliquary-v1)","One miner process per hotkey/state directory; preserve HF cache","Forced-seed deterministic sampling (temp 1.0, no chat template, drand randomness)","GRAIL sketch proofs must bind completions to the exact checkpoint","Follow /state: window OPEN check, cooldown prompts, instant checkpoint reload"]
playbook.minerJob: Run the continuous poll-submit loop: GET /state for window status, checkpoint_n, cooldowns, and the drand-derived randomness; when OPEN, pick a prompt from Math (OpenMathInstruct-2, local rewards) / Code (validator-authoritative) / Logic environments, generate exactly 16 forced-seed rollouts on the current checkpoint, compute rewards, build GRAIL sketches on the proof GPU, and submit. The validator recomputes rewards (mismatch = reject), gates groups on reward variance, ranks by std(rewards) x (1-mean(rewards)), proves top-down, and picks up to 16 winners per environment; winners accumulate and train. Protocol v6 uses fill-closed windows with FIFO selection; unproven overflow burns.
playbook.minerJobProvide: ["Verified 16-rollout groups with reward variance","GRAIL sketches binding to the live checkpoint","Submission speed inside fill-closed windows","Checkpoint tracking (reload on checkpoint_n advance)"]
playbook.top10Strategy: v6 is FIFO fill with fixed payment - speed and reliability now beat auction gaming: windows close on fill, so earlier arrival keeps a residual edge. Generate high-variance, mid-difficulty prompt groups (they clear the variance gate and rank well), never mismatch seeds/profiles (WRONG_RANDOMNESS rejections), and reload new checkpoints instantly to avoid reject cycles. Multi-GPU throughput multiplies how many windows you fill.
playbook.top10Levers: ["Generation throughput (window-fill speed)","Prompt selection outside cooldown with useful variance","Exact forced-seed/GRAIL compliance","Multi-GPU setup (generation + proof split)","Instant checkpoint reloads from HF"]

playbook.whatItDoes: Noah (built by Vora) is not a compute market - it is a financial-contribution subnet around 'the Ark'. Miners are scored on two on-chain facts: their eligible spendable NOAH earnings and their qualifying contributions to the Ark - ownership transfers of staked NOAH that arrive at the official Ark coldkey, delegated to the designated Ark Validator, and labeled with the miner's identity. The Noah Validator reads finalized chain records, computes a daily score per miner, and publishes weights. There is no model to serve, no queries to answer, and no work product: the 'product' is permanent capital contribution. Contributions transfer ownership and are not withdrawable.
playbook.hardwareRec: Effectively nothing - CPU-only. No miner daemon or axon needs to be reachable and scoring is purely on-chain, so any cheap CPU VPS (1 vCPU / 1-2 GB RAM) or a laptop can run the Python deposit helper and hold keys. No GPU and no VRAM floor (platform floor: None (CPU-only)). The real cost is capital, not hardware: 10 NOAH entry contribution per hotkey, then an ongoing 50% of eligible spendable earnings contributed to the Ark.
playbook.keyRequirements: ["Register a hotkey on SN82 and make the entry contribution: 10 NOAH per miner hotkey","Contributions must arrive at the official Ark coldkey delegated to the designated Ark Validator - staking to the validator from your own wallet does NOT count","Every contribution must identify its miner (stable label) - an unnamed deposit receives no mining credit and is unrecoverable","Daily obligation: contribute 50% of eligible spendable earnings (newly spendable + earnings that unlock that day; returned registration collateral is not earnings)","Contributions transfer ownership to the Ark and are not withdrawable - treat every send as permanent","Use the deposit helper flow (preview -> send -> receipt) and verify against finalized chain records, never mempool state"]
playbook.minerJob: Run nothing 24/7 - the daily job is treasury management with the noah-miner CLI: preview the fixed deposit (deposit --preview), send the reviewed deposit with a stable label (deposit --label entry), then read its receipt (status). Keep enough liquid NOAH to cover each day's 50% obligation on time, because the streak records whether each day's requirement was met - catching up later never rebuilds a missed day's streak. Advance contributions can pre-cover future days, and surplus first repays shortfalls before becoming uncapped advance coverage. Optionally audit published scores with noah.scoring.audit_published - 'AGREES' means the published score follows from the chain inputs under the checked-in scoring code.
playbook.minerJobProvide: ["Labeled ownership transfers of staked NOAH to the Ark (delegated to the Ark Validator)","Daily coverage of 50% of eligible spendable earnings, on time","Streak hygiene: no missed days; outages marked noFault only when genuinely fault-free","Receipt verification against finalized chain records"]
playbook.top10Strategy: This is a capital-allocation game, not an engineering one - the top wallets are simply the ones that can afford to contribute the most capital permanently. On-target miners earn roughly a 1.0 contribution multiplier; surplus raises the PCI up to the 2.0 cap, which at the 50% target and harshness 2 needs a cumulative contribution ratio of about 70.71%. Score compounds credit x streak x slot x gate, and pay weight = integer_sqrt(score) x multiplier, so uninterrupted streaks and sustained surplus matter more than one big deposit. Weigh the structural risk before committing: deposits are irreversible, weights are set by a single designated scoring validator, and on-chain stake is heavily concentrated in a handful of wallets - so treat SN82 as speculation on contributed capital's token appreciation, not mining income.
playbook.top10Levers: ["Capital surplus: push the cumulative contribution ratio past ~70.7% to reach the 2.0 multiplier cap","Unbroken streaks: meet every day's 50% obligation on time - a missed day permanently breaks its streak","Advance coverage: pre-fund future days so outages never create a miss","Hold the minimum: if the holding gate closes, score is zero (mainnet profile minimum is currently 0)","Label every deposit: unnamed or misrouted transfers earn nothing and cannot be recovered"]
playbook.followTopMiners: taostats.io/subnets/82 for the weight distribution (expect heavy concentration in a few wallets); the Vora-Inc/NOAH repo is the normative spec - README, docs/SCORING.md and docs/CONTRIBUTIONS.md - and deposit notices are published there before you sign anything; run the repo's audit tool against published scores to decompose incumbents' credit/streak/multiplier; subnet announcements in Bittensor discord carry profile changes (target, harshness, cap).

playbook.whatItDoes: CliqueAI is a maximum-clique solver network. Validators sample graph problems (roughly 300, 500, and 700-vertex general graphs) from a distributed database and send them to miners, who return the largest clique found within tight time limits (6-30s). Scoring rewards optimality (beating the field) and diversity (unique solutions); a debiased EMA reputation drives weights.
playbook.hardwareRec: CPU only: high single-thread performance and fast memory help branch-and-bound/local-search clique search inside 6-30s limits. No GPU. Run start_miner.sh with your axon IP/port reachable; the real work is optimizing your own solver.
playbook.keyRequirements: ["CPU solver returning a valid maximal clique within per-problem time limits (6s to 30s)","Axon IP/port reachable by validators (start_miner.sh flags)","Equal-probability sampling per difficulty; harder problems are sampled less often","Dual-metric scoring: optimality plus diversity (identical solutions share credit)","Debiased EMA reputation (alpha=0.01, half-life about 69 samples)"]
playbook.minerJob: Run the reference miner via start_miner.sh; when a validator sends a graph problem, your solver computes a maximum clique within the time limit and returns the vertex set. The validator scores optimality (validity scaled by how many miners beat your size) plus diversity (uniqueness of your solution), aggregates them with difficulty weighting, and updates your EMA rating - that rolling reputation sets weights and future problem allocation.
playbook.minerJobProvide: ["Valid maximal-clique solutions inside 6-30s limits","Larger-than-competitor clique sizes (optimality score)","Algorithmically distinct solutions (diversity credit)","Consistent performance across difficulty tiers"]
playbook.top10Strategy: Two levers: raw solver strength - state-of-the-art clique algorithms (local search, branch-and-bound, tight coloring bounds) tuned to 6-30s budgets on 300-700 vertex graphs - and uniqueness, since identical solutions split credit. Very-hard problems have fewer eligible solvers, so excellence there pays disproportionately. Newcomers: start from open-source max-clique solvers, benchmark against all three difficulty tiers, and keep EMA consistent.
playbook.top10Levers: ["Solver speed and quality within 6-30s time limits","Unique solutions (diversity term multiplies credit)","Excelling on very-hard 700-vertex problems","Sustained EMA performance (~69-sample half-life)","Avoiding copy-paste solvers (identical solutions split credit)","Stable axon uptime for sampling eligibility"]

playbook.whatItDoes: InfiniteQuant is a signal market: miners commit encrypted directional trade calls (2-hour drand timelock), validators grade them against real market candles, and emissions go to miners with statistically proven edge — Wilson lower-bound hit-rate >=50% on enough decisive trades, scaled by hit-rate tiers. Two mechanisms: low-frequency (3 calls/day) and high-frequency (30 calls/day).
playbook.hardwareRec: CPU only: Python 3.10 venv on any small VPS. No GPU, no market-data subscription (validators handle all pricing). Feed token comes via Telegram bot; the miner is non-custodial and extremely lightweight. Rentals irrelevant.
playbook.keyRequirements: ["3 signals/day per hotkey, 1h minimum gap (LF); TP/SL symmetric 1:1 per-asset bands","Unrevealed blob = decisive LOSS; 3 bad blobs in 30d zeroes the hotkey 30 days","8-day warmup: dust weight, warmup wins never pay","Copy penalty: shadowing an existing (pair, direction) voids copied wins","HF mode: 50 submissions over 8 distinct days + per-pair direction diversity gates"]
playbook.minerJob: Pick a pair and direction, encrypt the signal with the 2-hour drand timelock, and put SHA256(signal) on-chain via set_commitment (entry price derives from the commit block). After reveal, validators verify the plaintext against the hash and grade on 1-minute candles: TP first = WON, SL first = LOST, neither = WASH. Weight ∝ trailing-7-day qualified wins (cap 20, linear decay) × shrunk-hit-rate tier (1.0×/1.2×/2.0×). HF mode sends signed WebSocket frames with countersigned receipts and Merkle-rooted windows.
playbook.minerJobProvide: ["Encrypted directional trade calls (commit + reveal)","Reveals matching the on-chain hash","Wilson-qualified hit-rate (>=50% lower bound)","Direction diversity and first-mover originality"]
playbook.top10Strategy: Real forecasting edge, not infrastructure: with 3 calls/day, selectivity and conviction matter — tiers reward 60% (1.2×) and 70% (2.0×) shrunk hit-rates, and luck cannot qualify. Newcomers: use the 8-day warmup to build a record free, respect the copy penalty by being first, and add the HF board only with genuine two-sided discipline.
playbook.top10Levers: ["True hit-rate edge (Wilson-qualified)","Signal selectivity within the 3/day cap","SHARP/WOLF tier thresholds (60%/70%)","Copy-penalty avoidance (first mover wins)","HF participation + per-pair direction diversity"]

playbook.whatItDoes: KubeTEE is the AI Factory: miners run confidential (TEE) Kubernetes clusters serving enterprise AI services - SOTA inference via a LiteLLM gateway plus batch fine-tune/eval jobs - with hardware-level attestation (Intel TDX, NVIDIA CC). Validators score infrastructure readiness and USD-competitive pricing against Targon/Lium/Chutes; demand-side paid jobs land in Phase 2.
playbook.hardwareRec: Datacenter cluster: 7+ nodes with 2-3 dedicated 8-GPU workers per type (H100/H200/B200/B300), Intel TDX BIOS-enabled, HA control plane, 100 TAO collateral deposit. Early Access onboarding is hand-reviewed; TEE-attested bare metal beats any generic rental.
playbook.keyRequirements: ["TEE attestation mandatory (Intel TDX/SGX + NVIDIA CC; Kata + CoCo runtime classes) - no attestation, no emissions","7 nodes minimum per cluster (5 combined control/etcd/worker, 3 dedicated 8-GPU workers per GPU type), one datacenter, one cluster per hotkey","Rancher inventory passing infra-readiness policy: readiness, HA topology, 8-GPU passthrough wiring, confidential runtime handler","100 TAO registration collateral on the mining hotkey (not slashable; emission stops and capital freezes on breach)","Hand-reviewed Early Access onboarding; KubeTEE binds the cluster via kubetee.ai/hotkey label + Rancher Fleet","USD price card per GPU-hour (H100 $4 / H200 $5.50 / B200 $8 / B300 $10 / RTX6000 $2.50), clamped by Targon SN4 payouts"]
playbook.minerJob: A miner operates a TEE-hardened RKE2 Kubernetes cluster enrolled via Rancher Fleet; KubeTEE applies the hotkey binding and GitOps-deploys the stack (GPU Operator, Kata/CoCo, Longhorn, NeMo, monitoring). The cluster serves confidential inference through the LiteLLM gateway and will host Armada-scheduled batch jobs. Each epoch the validator enumerates nodes via Rancher, computes a binary infrastructure-readiness verdict plus a USD-denominated compensation weight, and sets weights on-chain. Emission flows per proven, priced capacity; unearned share recycles to unissued supply, never to the owner key.
playbook.minerJobProvide: ["TEE-attested multi-node Kubernetes cluster (RKE2, Kata/CoCo, NVIDIA CC)","HA topology with 8-GPU workers and GPU passthrough, passing readiness policy","Confidential inference capacity behind the LiteLLM gateway","Armada-ready batch job execution (fine-tune, eval) as demand lands"]
playbook.top10Strategy: Enterprise-grade ops is the game: nail TDX + CC attestation, HA topology, and 8-GPU passthrough on day one, keep readiness perpetually green (the gate is binary - any gap zeroes your score), and stay priced at/below the rate card versus Targon payouts. Onboarding is demand-driven, so engage the team early and study BTLABS (UID 97), the reference production cluster.

playbook.whatItDoes: cascade builds time-series foundation models by competing on data: the model (Toto2-4M backbone) is fixed and identical for everyone, and miners write the synthetic data generators that train it. Every ~12h round, king and challengers train from the same init on the same GPU type; validators score on private real-world windows (CRPS/MASE, paired bootstrap) and crown the throne.
playbook.hardwareRec: No local GPU - miner CLI is CPU-only; your Lium key pays for the round's training pod (~5h budget) on the pinned GPU type (4090/3090/L40S/L40/A6000). Budget per funded leg, not a standing rig.
playbook.keyRequirements: ["Generator meeting the DataGenerator contract incl. determinism checks","On-chain commit; private submission to operator vault or public deploy","Funding your training leg via your Lium key (unfunded boundary runs nothing)","Same seeds/init/GPU type enforced by the trainer","Rolling intake incoming: funded legs train on funding, settled every 3h"]
playbook.minerJob: Write and iterate a synthetic time-series generator; run cascade verify (all trainer checks) and cascade score (cheap local training + scoring, --warm-start live) before committing. Submit privately (vault) or deploy publicly, then fund the leg - the trainer runs king and challengers identically (~5h budget) and validators score checkpoints on private windows with a paired bootstrap; dethrone margin is 1% vs a fresh king decaying to a 0.5% floor. King plus up to 4 prior kings share weights with geometric decay (~52/26/13/6/3%); unregistered share burns. Your generator stays private; only crowned kings publish.
playbook.minerJobProvide: ["Synthetic data generators under the interface contract","Funded training legs (Lium pod)","Crowned king generators (published on wins)","Locally-verified, deterministic submissions"]
playbook.top10Strategy: Pure research edge, cheap to iterate: your generator's synthetic distribution IS the product. Study what works (chaotic systems, regime shifts, multivariate coupling up to 32 channels) against the public GIFT-Eval/BOOM/TIME telemetry, use cascade score locally to filter ideas before funding, and submit often under rolling intake - margins are small (0.5-1%), so steady incremental edges beat moonshots.
playbook.top10Levers: ["Generator design quality (distribution coverage/realism)","Cheap local score iterations before funding","Funding cadence (more legs = more shots)","Multivariate channels (up to 32, scored jointly)","Reading duel --hotkey feedback per domain"]
playbook.followTopMiners: Public receipts/index.json and funded/round-*.json (who seated/won); the dashboard Training tab (king benchmark trajectory); taostats.io/subnets/91; DEC-CA-0043/0045 decision docs for the rolling-intake switch.

playbook.whatItDoes: Bitcast connects brands with content creators. Miners (creators) publish YouTube videos matching brand briefs; validators verify engagement via the YouTube Analytics API using OAuth tokens miners serve, score videos in USD terms, and convert scores to weights. This repo is mechanism 0 (YouTube, ~2% of emission); the X/Twitter mechanism (~98%) lives in bitcast-network/bitcast-x.
playbook.hardwareRec: CPU only - the miner serves YouTube OAuth tokens through a lightweight axon; no GPU or heavy compute. The real capital is the YouTube channel and its audience. Credentials live in ~/.bitcast/secrets (client_id, client_secret, refresh_token per channel) or via TOKEN_SOURCE=api.
playbook.keyRequirements: ["Registered YouTube channels you control (OAuth client_id/secret/refresh_token per account)","Miner axon serving AccessTokenSynapse tokens to validators","Videos must match active brand briefs (LLM-assisted brief matching)","Engagement verified through the YouTube Analytics API; scores denominated in USD","Unallocated emission is absorbed by burn UID 0 - no brief match, no pay"]
playbook.minerJob: Run neurons/miner.py: it hosts an axon serving OAuth access tokens for your channels; validators use them to pull Analytics data, match videos against active briefs, and score earned USD value with EMA smoothing into weights. Your actual day job is creating brief-compliant content with genuine engagement - the miner software itself is trivial token management. Commit-reveal validators mean on-chain last_update understates activity.
playbook.minerJobProvide: ["OAuth access tokens for owned YouTube channels (refresh-managed)","Brief-compliant YouTube videos with organic engagement","Verified Analytics access for validator scoring","Consistent EMA-scored video output across cycles"]
playbook.top10Strategy: You compete as a creator, not a sysadmin: emissions track real USD value of brief-matching videos verified via YouTube Analytics, so channel size and view quality dominate. Note this repo is only ~2% of SN93 emission - the X mechanism (bitcast-x) carries ~98%, so pick your track deliberately. Small-channel newcomers should target niche briefs with less creator competition.
playbook.top10Levers: ["Owning channels with real engaged audiences","Brief-matching precision (LLM-assisted matching favors on-brief content)","EMA consistency across reward cycles","Multiple channels per miner via secrets files","Considering bitcast-x (98% of emission) instead","Verifying liveness via AGENTS.md read-only chain commands"]
playbook.followTopMiners: Track taostats.io/subnets/93 weights, the signed Bitcast dashboard publisher output, briefs-client updates, and bitcast-network/bitcast-x commits; Loki score-audit telemetry exposes per-UID raw reward and EMA.

playbook.whatItDoes: A verifiable-compute network: operators run confidential-computing machines (Intel TDX or AMD SEV-SNP guests); validators verify fresh TEE attestation evidence bound to the live HTTPS key, reject duplicate machines, and run bounded SAT tasks — each distinct verified machine adds score to its UID. Buyers get attested, verifiable compute capacity.
playbook.hardwareRec: TEE-capable VM required: Intel TDX (with /sys/kernel/config/tsm/report) or AMD SEV-SNP (/dev/sev-guest) — plain SEV/vTPM insufficient. GPU is NOT a qualified mining path today. Cloud TDX instances are the natural rental option.
playbook.keyRequirements: ["Intel TDX VM or AMD SEV-SNP guest","Public IPv4 + inbound TCP 8081","Python 3.12, Git, Docker, nft, curl inside the guest","Bittensor CLI 11.1.0 on a separate wallet machine","Miner-owned control host for signed snapshot refresh","Duplicate hardware/endpoints score zero","Coldkeys and seeds stay off workers"]
playbook.minerJob: Provision TDX/SEV-SNP machines, run the pinned worker image per docs/MINING.md (root-owned launcher; TLS key generated inside the guest), and keep a control host refreshing signed validator-access snapshots. Validators verify fresh attestation quotes, bind evidence to your live HTTPS endpoint on :8081, reject duplicates, then run a bounded SAT task; each distinct verified machine adds to your UID's score. Registration, uptime or advertised machine counts alone earn nothing — verification is the product. No public validator-result feed exists; confirm weights on-chain.
playbook.minerJobProvide: ["Fresh TEE attestation evidence per machine","HTTPS worker endpoint on :8081","Distinct verified machines per UID","Signed snapshot refresh from control host","Passing bounded SAT work","Unique hardware (no duplicates)"]
playbook.top10Strategy: Scale = number of distinct machines that each independently pass verification — one TDX VM is a proof of concept; a fleet of attested, non-duplicate machines is the business. Rehearse three times locally before paying for anything, keep every machine's evidence fresh (stale quotes fail), and confirm finalized weight rows on-chain rather than trusting dashboards or health checks.
playbook.top10Levers: ["Fleet of distinct attested TDX/SEV-SNP machines","Fresh evidence on every validator check","Reliable :8081 endpoint uptime","Unique hardware (duplicates score zero)","Correct snapshot-refresh automation","Follow docs/MINING.md exactly (checksums, launchers)"]
playbook.followTopMiners: No public validator-result feed — confirm chain weights directly (docs/MINING.md §5), follow GitHub issues and docs updates on cathedral-sandbox, and coordinate with validator operators on AMD socket policy and admission.

playbook.whatItDoes: Verathos is the verifiable serving layer for Bittensor intelligence: model creators publish exact model identities; independent operators serve them via vLLM endpoints or GGUF mesh pools behind one OpenAI-compatible API. Validators verify execution (Gleipnir proof protocol) and run unpredictable capacity audits; rewards flow to operators by measured utility, latency, throughput, and reliability.
playbook.hardwareRec: 1x RTX 4090 (24GB) per platform data supports current qualified lanes; choose the vLLM endpoint or GGUF mesh worker path. Install via verathos.ai/install.sh; check active network policy for which models/lanes currently earn emissions.
playbook.keyRequirements: ["Serve a registered model identity with a qualified verification profile (Gleipnir protocol)","vLLM endpoint or GGUF mesh pool (coordinator + CUDA workers) lanes","Return responses with proof metadata; pass unpredictable integrity and capacity audits","Emissions gated by active network policy (eligible models/lanes change)","Rewards from measured utility, latency, throughput, reliability, and verified operation","HTTPS endpoint setup; multi-endpoint operation supported"]
playbook.minerJob: Operate inference endpoints: run the guided installer (verathos setup / verathos start), register your endpoint, and serve the currently qualified models with vLLM, or join a GGUF mesh pool as a CUDA worker behind a coordinator. Day-to-day the endpoint answers OpenAI-compatible chat completions with attached verification metadata while validators probe performance and launch surprise execution and capacity audits. Earnings track routed traffic quality - health, score evidence, and audit history decide weights.
playbook.minerJobProvide: ["OpenAI-compatible inference endpoint with verification metadata","Passing unpredictable Gleipnir execution audits","Demonstrated capacity under audit","Low-latency, high-throughput serving","Model identity served exactly as registered"]
playbook.top10Strategy: Serving economics plus audit integrity: pick the policy-eligible model your hardware serves best (4090-class for current lanes), tune vLLM for throughput and latency, and never fail an integrity audit - one failure can zero you. Watch docs/economic_model.md and network-policy announcements because lanes change. Newcomers break top-10 by being early on a newly-qualified model lane before incumbents crowd it.
playbook.top10Levers: ["Policy-lane selection (newly qualified models)","vLLM/GGUF throughput tuning","Clean audit history (integrity + capacity)","Multi-endpoint scaling","Latency and reliability on routed traffic"]
playbook.followTopMiners: Track taostats.io/subnet/96 top operators, verathos.ai/docs network-policy and economic-model updates, repo release cadence (Gleipnir proof protocol v3), and which model identities are currently emission-eligible.

playbook.whatItDoes: Distil (SN97, formerly branded Albedo) is a king-of-the-hill competitive model-distillation subnet. The teacher is moonshotai/Kimi-K2.6 (1T total / ~32B active MoE; Qwen3.5/3.6 teacher cutover went live 2026-05-02). Miners distill <=33B students, upload to HuggingFace and commit on-chain; validators score a 25+ axis composite; winner takes 100% of emissions.
playbook.hardwareRec: Student-side bf16 training of 33B-class students: 4-8× H100/H200; LoRA + checkpointing fits smaller rigs. 2× 24GB only for sub-2B sanity runs. Quantized students (GPTQ/AWQ/GGUF) rejected. Training infra is your choice; rentals allowed, evaluation runs on validator GPUs.
playbook.keyRequirements: ["Kimi-family architecture + Kimi BPE tokenizer (vocab 163,840), <=33B total params, safetensors bf16/fp16","One PERMANENT commitment per hotkey (new attempts need a new hotkey)","Unique weights: SHA256 + activation-fingerprint near-copy detection","Model stays public and unchanged on HF — edits = DQ","Ranking key: composite.final = 0.75 × worst-3-axis mean + 0.25 × weighted mean"]
playbook.minerJob: Train a distilled student, run test_miner.py (the same 15 validator checks locally), then commit the HF repo link on-chain (miner.py, dry-run first). Each commitment is scored exactly once: 11 procedurally-generated block-seeded axes (~50% — math, code, reasoning, long-context, knowledge, honesty), distillation tier (~30% incl. on-policy RKL), judge/quality and discipline axes. The king is re-evaluated every round on the same items; a challenger dethrones only at a 5% margin. Weight 1.0 to the king, 0 to everyone else.
playbook.minerJobProvide: ["Distilled <=33B Kimi-family student on a public HF repo","Permanent on-chain commitment per hotkey","High worst-3-axis composite (no weak-axis camping)","All 15 pre-submission checks passed before committing"]
playbook.top10Strategy: Winner-take-all research problem: because 75% of the score is your three WORST axes, balanced students beat specialists — fix your weakest capability, don't polish KL. Newcomers: use on-policy RKL training (community script in examples/), pre-check everything locally to save registration burns, and budget for multiple hotkey attempts since commitments can't change.
playbook.top10Levers: ["Balanced quality across all axes (worst-3 rule)","On-policy RKL distillation method","Training compute (4-8× H100/H200 class)","Anti-copy uniqueness (hash + activation fingerprints)","Robustness to procedural block-seeded axes (no overfitting)"]
playbook.followTopMiners: Watch distil.arbos.life (composite scores, king) and api.arbos.life, chat.arbos.life to query the current king, docs/MINER_FAQ.md and reports/ in the repo for axis changes, and taostats.io/subnet/97 for weight flips.

playbook.whatItDoes: Never Play Alone builds low-latency Minecraft AI companions: miners submit Node-based agents that play real missions in NPA-Bench; validators run every agent in identical sandboxed servers, score results, and set winner-take-all weights. The best agents power a commercial AI-companions product, so emission rewards exactly what sells.
playbook.hardwareRec: Agent development is Node.js plus an LLM API - CPU only; validators run the heavy Minecraft/eval infrastructure. No GPU requirement appears in repo or docs; sandbox isolation means agents reach only the Minecraft server and a spend-capped LLM proxy.
playbook.keyRequirements: ["One tar.gz agent package per round via npacli during the submission window","Fully open-source competition: winning approaches become public floors; champion margin blocks copy-paste resubmissions","Sandboxed execution: no internet except Minecraft server + validator LLM proxy (per-run spend caps, usage tracked)","Per-validator seeds derive from chain block hash - no pre-fitting; determinism enforced","Champion defense: challengers must beat the champion by the round's margin; stake-weighted validator scoring"]
playbook.minerJob: Each round the miner develops their Minecraft agent (mission planning, resource gathering, survival behaviors - LLM-driven decision loops under a spend cap), packages it as tar.gz, and submits via npacli. After freeze, validators run every entry on identical deterministic missions in network-isolated containers, upload reports plus gameplay recordings, and each validator computes the winner locally from stake-weighted scoreboards; the full weight vector lands on the winning UID. The champion re-enters automatically and retains unless beaten by more than the margin.
playbook.minerJobProvide: ["A packaged Node-based Minecraft agent submitted per round","Agents that complete deterministic missions robustly and feel alive","LLM-efficient behavior under per-run spend caps","Round-winning performance strong enough to clear the champion margin"]
playbook.top10Strategy: Winner-take-all rewards decisive wins: robust general-purpose agents that don't collapse on unseen missions outperform brittle specialists as the mission pool grows. Since every agent is open source, ship durable architectural improvements (planning, memory, error recovery) that survive the champion margin, and budget LLM spend carefully - caps punish waste.
playbook.top10Levers: ["Robustness across the expanding mission pool beats overfit specialists","LLM spend efficiency under per-run caps","Study prior winning agents (open source) for proven patterns","Practice on NPA-Bench locally; seeds derive from block hash","Submit only when clearly better than the champion","Round cadence discipline: one package, on time, every round"]
playbook.followTopMiners: Track taostats.io/subnet/98 weight concentration (winner-take-all shows one dominant UID), neverplayalone.ai and Discord for round announcements, and neverplayalone_bench repo updates for new mission types.

playbook.whatItDoes: Cortex is an agentic research subnet: the operator's Proof agent opens signed research topics (statement, metric, checklist, baseline), miners submit reproducible research artifacts and claims that get executed/scored in Docker challenge containers, and a bounty challenge pays for verified reproducible bug reports. Validators verify the master's sealed, signed epoch bundle and submit weights.
playbook.hardwareRec: Artifact submission itself is CPU/API work (tar <=5MiB, signed). Input metadata recommends B200 with RTX 5090 fallback - relevant only if a topic's challenge container demands heavy GPU inference. Budget per-topic, not per-rig.
playbook.keyRequirements: ["Hotkey-signed submissions in the frozen Cortex sr25519 context with fresh nonces","Topic must be status:open with an active epoch window","Exact-digest uncompressed tar artifact <=5MiB (no symlinks/compression)","Bounty path needs CORTEX account pairing + accepted terms","Valid bug reports only (published as valid) earn weight"]
playbook.minerJob: Discover open topics via the gateway API (status/topics endpoints), read the signed topic document, prepare your artifact tar + claim per the checklist, and submit via cortex miner proof-submit (hotkey signature, nonce, artifact digest; optional env-file for topic credentials). The master runs Proof and challenge containers, measures against baselines, signs one leaf per miner per epoch, and seals the bundle; validators verify and submit weights. The bounty challenge (CortexLM/bounty) pays share x min(N/10, 1) split by valid-report count, remainder burning to UID0. Shortfalls burn - no cross-subsidies.
playbook.minerJobProvide: ["Reproducible research artifacts per open topic","Signed claims matching topic checklists","Verified, reproducible bug reports (bounty)","Protocol-exact submissions (nonce, digest, context)"]
playbook.top10Strategy: Speed and reproducibility win: monitor for new open topics and be first with checklist-perfect, actually-executing artifacts - scoring is execution-based, so self-reported claims fail. For bounty, hunt genuinely reproducible bugs; report count saturates at 10 (min(N/10,1)), so a handful of solid reports beats spam. Keep an archive of topic documents - historical topics don't count.
playbook.top10Levers: ["Topic monitoring speed (open windows are limited)","Artifact reproducibility and checklist fit","Research quality vs the published baseline","Bounty bug count up to the N/10 cap","Correct signing context and nonce hygiene"]
playbook.followTopMiners: Gateway /challenge/proof/v1/status + topics feeds; CortexLM/bounty repo (miner guide, scoring); OpentypeAI/challenge container; taostats.io/subnets/100 epoch weights.

playbook.whatItDoes: Tag101 is a decentralized semantic tagger for X/Twitter posts: miners transform posts into concise structured tags identifying entities, topics, and events. Validators score tags by consensus alignment (embedding clusters), validity (relevance plus format tiers), and diversity (non-redundancy). Downstream systems buy the structured signals for indexing and real-time topic tracking.
playbook.hardwareRec: CPU only - the reference miner calls the OpenAI API (OPENAI_API_KEY, optional OPENAI_BASE_URL/MODEL overrides); Docker or PM2 on a small VPS. Rented GPU/cloud unnecessary; LLM spend is the cost.
playbook.keyRequirements: ["OpenAI API key (or OPENAI_BASE_URL/MODEL override) for the reference miner","Docker deployment recommended (built-in auto-update) or PM2 with a venv","Tags must be relevant, non-redundant, and well-formed (validity tiers 0/0.3/0.6/1.0)","Duplicate penalty: identical tag sets shared by many miners are sigmoid-penalized (k=0.1, c=50)","Tasks come from a whitelisted X account database (current season: AI-related accounts)"]
playbook.minerJob: Run the SN101 miner container: it receives posts from validators, calls your configured LLM to emit a small tag set per post, and returns them. Each tag scores 0.6 x consensus (cluster support x centroid proximity) + 0.4 x validity x diversity, averaged per task; validator scoreboards aggregate recent task scores into relative miner scores for weights. Reward follows semantic alignment with the network's consensus reading of each post.
playbook.minerJobProvide: ["Concise structured tags per X post (entities/topics/events)","High consensus-cluster alignment with centroid proximity","Format-valid, mutually distinct tag sets","Fast task turnaround across topic seasons"]
playbook.top10Strategy: Consensus is king: 60% of a tag's score is alignment with the dominant cluster, so tags matching how other good miners read the post win, while the diversity term punishes redundancy within your own set. Prompt for the obvious tags plus one distinctive angle, and never copy others' exact sets - the duplicate penalty is sigmoid-steep. Track whitelist account styles as topic seasons rotate.
playbook.top10Levers: ["Consensus-aligned tagging (0.6 weight on cluster support)","Distinct tags within your own set (diversity weight 0.4)","Prompt engineering for tier-1.0 format validity","Cheap model choice with semantic quality (OpenAI overrides)","Avoiding duplicate tag sets (sigmoid penalty)","Docker auto-update to track scoring changes"]
playbook.followTopMiners: Watch taostats.io/subnets/101 top UIDs, tag101-ai/tag101 commits (scoring formulas and whitelist evolve), and in-repo topic-season announcements.

playbook.whatItDoes: A decentralized MoE training network: the model is split into expert groups hosted across independent miners; validators coordinate training steps, aggregate expert contributions and score miners to drive TAO rewards. Participation means contributing trained expert weights to a shared LLM rather than serving end users.
playbook.hardwareRec: Per input spec: A100/H100 class, 40 GB+ VRAM (A6000 48 GB works). Expect sustained training-style GPU load, not inference. Datacenter-class or pro cards; consumer 24 GB cards likely insufficient.
playbook.keyRequirements: ["Host expert group(s) of the shared MoE model","Coordinate with the validator training schedule","High-bandwidth transfer of weights/activations/gradients","Sustained uptime across training rounds","Operational docs live at connito.ai/docs/miner"]
playbook.minerJob: Run the Connito miner per connito.ai/docs/miner: your machine hosts one or more expert groups of the network's MoE LLM. Validators orchestrate the training loop — routing activations to experts, collecting updated weights/gradients, aggregating — and score miners on contribution quality and reliability, setting weights each epoch. Because this is collaborative training, rewards track consistent participation and useful expert updates across rounds rather than one-shot benchmark wins.
playbook.minerJobProvide: ["Hosted MoE expert partitions","Timely expert weight/gradient updates","Reliable participation across training steps","Bandwidth for activation/gradient exchange","Contribution to a shared trained LLM"]
playbook.top10Strategy: With collaborative training, steady correct participation beats heroics: keep your experts online for every coordinated step, minimize transfer latency, and follow the official miner docs for version pins — missed rounds likely forfeit credit for that step. The 40 GB+ VRAM floor filters competition; reliable datacenter hosting and fast networking are the practical moats for breaking into the top ranks.
playbook.top10Levers: ["100% round attendance (no missed steps)","Fast interconnect for weight/gradient exchange","40 GB+ VRAM headroom for expert groups","Follow pinned versions in official docs","Stable long-running hosting (no restarts)","Watch validator coordination changes"]
playbook.followTopMiners: Track connito.ai/docs (miner/validator guides), taostats.io/subnet/102 top UIDs and emission concentration, and Connito-AI/Connito commit cadence for protocol changes.

playbook.whatItDoes: Taostatus sources working LLM API access from miners for the BT Arena Protocol's AI agent pipeline. A miner's entire job: keep one working LLM credential (e.g. GPT-4o) available and hand it over encrypted when polled. Rewards track reliability, latency, volume, and model tier. NOTE: README states netuid 501 (testnet) - verify mainnet status before registering.
playbook.hardwareRec: CPU only - no inference runs locally. The real cost is the contributed LLM API key (the protocol consumes real calls); a $2-5 VPS runs the miner. Pick high-tier models for the tier-weight multiplier.
playbook.keyRequirements: ["Configure one LLM API key for an allowed provider/model and opt in","Answer only the LLMKeySynapse request: encrypt the key client-side and return it; never contact the protocol directly","Score = 0.5 reliability + 0.25 latency + 0.25 volume, multiplied by model-tier weight","A key marked inactive scores 0.0 regardless of tier; quiet windows are skipped, not penalized","95% of emissions burn to UID 25 (BURN_PERCENTAGE 0.95) - only 5% reaches miners","README states Netuid 501 (testnet)"]
playbook.minerJob: Run neurons/miner.py with your hotkey; it listens for the single LLMKeySynapse request and replies with your client-side-encrypted API key (or declines cleanly if not opted in or the model does not match). The validator relays keys to the BT Arena protocol backend, which draws on the key operationally and reports usage (success/failure counts, latency, volume). Those reports become your score via an exponential moving average - liveness alone earns nothing; only real verified usage accumulates weight. Keep the key funded, high-tier, and heavily used.
playbook.minerJobProvide: ["One working, funded LLM API credential on an allowed model","Encrypted key delivery on every validator poll","Sustained real usage with high success rate","Fast response latency","High-tier model selection (tier multiplier)"]
playbook.top10Strategy: The 95% burn makes absolute earnings small - treat this as yield-on-an-API-key, not a mining business. Win the 5% pool by contributing a top-tier model (tier x1.0) that the protocol actually uses heavily at near-100% success. Read docs/HOW_IT_WORKS.md for the scoring formula, keep provider credit topped up (an exhausted or revoked key scores zero instantly), and confirm mainnet/netuid status before committing.

playbook.whatItDoes: Beam (SN105) is a decentralized bandwidth coordination network: it moves data at scale between clouds (AWS S3, R2, GCS, Snowflake, APIs, webhooks, MCP). Orchestrators split transfers into chunks routed across worker nodes (fan-out, aggregation, mesh); every transfer generates Proof-of-Bandwidth that validators verify and convert into emission weights. Site reports ~760 Gb/s aggregate, 1.8PB moved, ~1,150 miners.
playbook.hardwareRec: CPU only: bandwidth is the resource, not GPU. A VPS or home server with strong sustained uplink/downlink, stable uptime and open ports is what earns. No GPU requirement found; rentals irrelevant since network throughput, not compute, is scored.
playbook.keyRequirements: ["Worker/orchestrator node with verifiable bandwidth (Proof-of-Bandwidth)","Capability eligibility determines orchestrator selection and chunk allocation","Merkle-proof integrity verification on delivered chunks","Stale chunks are reassigned — laggards lose work","PRISM scoring + scheduled metrics refresh feed epoch weights"]
playbook.minerJob: Miners run orchestrators and workers that execute BeamCore transfer assignments: orchestrators select routes by latency, assign chunks by capability and bandwidth, and rebalance; workers stream chunks to destinations, report progress, verify Merkle proofs, and retry failures. Every transfer records verifiable performance data; validators refresh scheduled metrics (PRISM) and materialize epoch weights from them. Rewards scale with measured, verified bandwidth contribution — the public reference covers transfer assignment, PRISM scoring and weight materialization.
playbook.minerJobProvide: ["Worker bandwidth executing assigned transfer chunks","Merkle-proof-verified delivery","Orchestrator route selection/capability participation","Consistently measured throughput metrics each epoch"]
playbook.top10Strategy: An infrastructure-throughput contest: raw sustained bandwidth, uptime and fast chunk completion decide PRISM scores. Newcomers: run the reference node, pass capability eligibility, prove stable metrics for a few epochs, then scale with redundant uplinks and well-connected locations since scoring is performance-weighted, not stake-weighted.
playbook.top10Levers: ["Sustained verified uplink bandwidth","Uptime and chunk-retry reliability","Network proximity to transfer demand","Capability eligibility flags kept current","Adopting weight-calculation updates fast"]
playbook.followTopMiners: Track taostats.io/subnet/105 for weight/incentive distribution, b1m.ai for live network stats, the Beam X account (b1m_ai) for weight-calculation updates, and the Beam-Network org repos for PRISM/assignment code changes.
