playbook.whatItDoes: Nodexo is verified decentralized compute: GPU miners join a rental marketplace where renters launch containers over SSH, with every operation backed by cryptographic verification (ZkGEMM proofs, Sysbox-secured containers, digest-checked images). Validators verify proofs and heartbeats and authorize rentals; miners earn for provably serving verified GPU capacity.
playbook.hardwareRec: Ubuntu/Debian GPU host with supported NVIDIA GPUs (H100 80GB x1-2, A100 80GB x1-4, RTX A6000 48GB, RTX 4090 24GB per input); 100+ GB Docker storage recommended; ports 8091 + 20000-20100 open. The rental marketplace is the product; public reachability required.
playbook.keyRequirements: ["Supported NVIDIA GPU model - setup refuses to register unsupported cards; working nvidia-smi","Docker + NVIDIA Container Toolkit + Sysbox (setup refuses without sysbox-runc); 40+ GB free Docker storage","Ports open: 8091/tcp miner API and 20000-20100/tcp rental range (preflighted; strict mode refuses otherwise)","Registered hotkey with derived EVM mirror funded (small TAO) for registration and executor lease renewals","Synchronized clock (NTP enforced); alpha-stake gate may apply based on active executors per hotkey"]
playbook.minerJob: The miner daemon registers its EVM identity and executor, renews leases, reports hardware, and continuously sends ZkGEMM proofs plus heartbeats to permitted validators discovered from the ValidatorRegistry. It exposes a signed rental API (container create, SSH-key updates, termination - validator-signed) and serves rented containers in Sysbox-isolated Docker with digest-checked images. Proof/monitor traffic flows only to permitted validators, with endpoint quarantine so a dead validator never blocks liveness; rewards follow verified capacity and successful rental service.
playbook.minerJobProvide: ["Publicly reachable GPU rental endpoint (API + SSH port range)","Continuous ZkGEMM proof generation and validator heartbeats","Sysbox-isolated, digest-checked rental containers for renters","Accurate hardware reporting and renewed executor leases"]
playbook.top10Strategy: Reliability and proof hygiene win: keep ports, clock, drivers, and Docker storage healthy so preflights and proofs never fail, and hold stake above the alpha-stake gate. With hardware roughly equal, uptime, fast container provisioning, and a clean proof cadence separate top UIDs - and unsupported GPUs cannot earn at all.
playbook.top10Levers: ["Host prep: NTP, ports 8091 + 20000-20100, driver + Sysbox green on first setup","Keep the EVM mirror funded - expired leases take you offline","Monitor nodexo fleet/inventory for stake gates and executor status","Higher-end supported cards (H100/A100) attract better rental demand","Follow SUPPORTED_GPUS.md and release notes; the ZkGEMM proof stack evolves","Ensure reachability from validators AND renters - no NAT surprises"]

playbook.whatItDoes: Minos is decentralized genomic variant calling: every 72 minutes the platform generates a challenge BAM with hidden synthetic mutations (HelixForge, injected at read level). Miners run variant callers on it and submit tuned hyperparameter configurations - never outputs. Validators execute each config independently and score results with hap.py; later stages open custom algorithm competitions.
playbook.hardwareRec: CPU only per repo specs: miner >=4 cores / 8-16GB RAM (8GB BCFtools, 16GB DeepVariant), >=60GB disk (per-round BAMs ~6GB each), Docker required. Validators need 8 cores/32GB. Input metadata agrees (CPU-only, 0 VRAM).
playbook.keyRequirements: ["Docker 20.10+ (24.0+ recommended); Bittensor 10.3.1 (11.x unsupported)","72-minute cycles with lag scoring (submit cycle N while N+1 runs)","Submit configuration only - validators run it themselves","Parameter ranges enforced per tool template (GATK/DeepVariant/BCFtools; FreeBayes deprecated)","Demo mode (start-miner.sh --demo) to score without registering"]
playbook.minerJob: Run the miner loop: poll the platform, download the cycle's challenge BAM via presigned URL (Hippius SN75 / Cloudflare R2 / S3 fallback), run your chosen variant caller with tuned parameters, and submit the hyperparameter configuration through your axon. Validators download configs, execute them against the challenge genome, and score with hap.py (industry-standard precision/recall) against the hidden mutations; weights come from round scores with winner-heavy pruning dust weights. The tuning game is systematic: tools have different strengths per genome region, and the accepted parameter space is documented in templates and docs/parameter_ranges.md.
playbook.minerJobProvide: ["Tuned variant-calling configs per 72-min cycle","High hap.py F1/precision on hidden mutations","Consistent cycle participation (lag-scored)","Clean config validation within parameter ranges"]
playbook.top10Strategy: Hyperparameter-search quality wins early: automate Bayesian/Optuna-style sweeps per tool against local truth sets so your configs generalize to fresh genomes, and pick the right tool per challenge (DeepVariant vs GATK vs BCFtools trade speed for accuracy). Reliability across all cycles compounds rank history. When custom-algorithm stages open, first movers with novel pipelines take the ground.
playbook.top10Levers: ["Automated hyperparameter optimization pipeline","Per-challenge tool selection","Fast turnaround within the 72-min lag window","Disk/throughput for ~6GB BAMs","docs/tuning_guide.md mastery + template updates"]
playbook.followTopMiners: taostats.io/subnets/107 weights and rewarded miners; repo releases (tool template changes - e.g. FreeBayes deprecation); docs/tuning_guide.md updates; platform status endpoints for challenge cadence.

playbook.whatItDoes: ChipForge is a digital-design competition subnet: on-chain challenges ask for Verilog/SystemVerilog implementations of real silicon components (AI accelerators, cryptographic modules, mini-GPUs). Miners download specs, design with AI assistance, and submit solutions; validators evaluate with industry EDA tools. It is winner-takes-all per challenge, feeding designs toward manufacturable chips.
playbook.hardwareRec: CPU-heavy EDA work: synthesis/simulation/timing runs are CPU-bound (validators want 16-24 physical cores plus 32-48GB RAM); miners need a solid multicore box for local test loops. No GPU. The bare-metal note concerns state persistence in ./data, not a rental ban.
playbook.keyRequirements: ["Hotkey registered on netuid 108; repo stays on Bittensor 10.x (axon networking layer)","Miner polls the challenge server (default 300s) for spec/testbench packages; solutions are ZIPs of .v/.sv files","Winner-takes-all scoring with MIN_IMPROVEMENT_PERCENT margins; byte-identical copies refused","Winning designs are revealed to registered hotkeys after a set time (study them)","Leaderboard at chipforge.io/leaderboard shows the score to beat and every submission"]
playbook.minerJob: Run start_miner.sh (or make up ROLE=miner): the miner polls the challenge server, downloads the challenge package (spec plus testbench), you design and locally verify Verilog/SystemVerilog against the testbench with your own Verilator/Yosys loop, then submit via miner_cli.py. Validators batch-evaluate with EDA tools (Verilator, Yosys, Icarus, Openlane) and reach consensus scores; the best design per challenge takes the emission.
playbook.minerJobProvide: ["Functionally correct, high-scoring Verilog/SystemVerilog designs per challenge","ZIP submissions passing validator test benches","Improvements beating the current winner by the required margin","Design reuse via the revealed-winners program"]
playbook.top10Strategy: Winner-takes-all means only the #1 design per challenge is paid - breadth loses, depth in one challenge family (e.g. cryptographic modules) wins. Download revealed winning designs to calibrate against the evaluation bar, build a tight local EDA regression loop, and submit only when you beat the posted score-to-beat. Hardware-design skill is the moat; AI coding tools help but testbench-passing silicon thinking wins.
playbook.top10Levers: ["Deep design skill in one challenge family","Local Verilator/Yosys/Openlane regression before submit","Studying revealed winning designs (registered hotkeys only)","Monitoring the chipforge.io leaderboard score-to-beat","Planning around MIN_IMPROVEMENT_PERCENT margins","Fast response to newly announced challenges"]
playbook.followTopMiners: Watch chipforge.io/leaderboard (current winner, per-submission consensus scores), TatsuProject repo commit cadence, and the ChipForge Discord channel for validator/EDA server updates.

playbook.whatItDoes: A scientific-information-extraction subnet: miners receive paper-extraction tasks and return structured claim-evidence packets grounded in the source text (via an agent pipeline using the ARA artifact model). Validators audit grounding, claim-evidence link validity and task-scope coverage. Buyers get structured, audited scientific claims for research and tooling.
playbook.hardwareRec: CPU: 4 cores / 16 GB min (8 cores / 32 GB recommended), 50 GB disk, public Axon port. No GPU needed with hosted LLM providers — budget OpenRouter/Chutes API credits instead (Hermes agent harness).
playbook.keyRequirements: ["Python 3.12 (3.11+ min); Bittensor SDK pinned 10.5.0","agent_v1 pipeline with Hermes agent harness","LLM provider credentials (OpenRouter recommended)","Public Axon endpoint; artifacts API uploads","Docker images published (Targon rentals documented)","Coldkey only in wallet dir, never in .env"]
playbook.minerJob: Run the miner neuron with the agent_v1 pipeline: when validators send paper-extraction tasks, your agent (Hermes harness + configured LLM provider) reads the paper, extracts contribution claims with grounded evidence spans, and writes structured agent artifacts (agent_output.json plus manifests), uploaded via artifacts.claims111.ai. Validators audit each packet for source grounding, valid claim-evidence links and task coverage, and score miners accordingly. A reachable Axon is mandatory; grounding discipline and output quality drive rewards.
playbook.minerJobProvide: ["Structured claim-evidence packets per paper","Grounded evidence links to source text","Agent artifacts via signed uploads","Reachable Axon for task delivery","Low-hallucination, audit-passing extractions"]
playbook.top10Strategy: Rewards follow audit pass-rate: grounding every claim in verifiable source text beats aggressive extraction — failed grounding audits zero you out. Tune the agent stack (model choice, retries, PDF extraction method) for precision over recall, watch the dashboard for task patterns, and keep concurrency within your CPU/RAM budget (workers spawn per paper). API credit burn is the real cost — optimize tokens per paper.
playbook.top10Levers: ["Perfect source grounding (audit survival)","Strong extraction model via OpenRouter/Chutes","Token-efficient agent runs (cost control)","Concurrency tuned to hardware","Track dashboard + validator audit criteria","Stable Axon uptime","Follow agent_v1 pipeline updates"]

playbook.whatItDoes: SOMA (Dendrite) is a competition subnet for context compression: miners build algorithms and models that shrink AI-agent context (history, tool outputs, files) while preserving task success. Validators run real agent workloads with your compression enabled, scoring task quality and weighted token consumption against uncompressed baselines. Buyers: anyone running context-heavy agents.
playbook.hardwareRec: Unspecified. Algorithmic compression is CPU-only; hybrid model-based approaches may want a modest GPU. The platform/validators execute workloads (their floor: 4 cores, 16GB RAM, 500GB SSD). You need a registered hotkey on netuid 114.
playbook.keyRequirements: ["Build a compression solution compatible with the active competition rules (miner/README_prompting.md)","Upload submissions to the SOMA platform, tied to your registered hotkey","Scored on task performance plus weighted token consumption vs uncompressed baseline","Quality preservation matters - compression that breaks previously-passing tasks fails","Consistency across tasks and repeated runs is scored","Cycle: submission window -> screening/qualification -> evaluation"]
playbook.minerJob: Develop and upload compression solutions during submission windows: algorithmic (summarization, selection, structured state), model-based, or hybrids. The platform associates submissions with your hotkey, screens and qualifies them, then validators execute standardized agent workloads with your compression active - measuring whether agents still complete tasks while consuming fewer weighted tokens (input/cached/output priced differently). Aggregated rankings feed subnet weights. Between cycles you iterate on your weakest measured signal.
playbook.minerJobProvide: ["Compression solution compatible with the active competition","Token savings without task failures","Stable results across repeated runs","Platform-registered submission per hotkey","Iterative improvements across competition cycles"]
playbook.top10Strategy: The objective is maximum useful compression, not maximum ratio. Study which token categories are weighted (cached input vs fresh) and design for real economic savings while keeping task success at baseline. Ship early in each submission window, use screening feedback, and iterate - quality preservation is where most entries die. Newcomers with strong summarization/prompt engineering can beat heavier model-based approaches.
playbook.top10Levers: ["Task-success preservation at high compression ratios","Weighted-token optimization (cached vs fresh input)","Fast iteration across competition cycles","Screening/qualification pass rate","Consistency across repeated evaluations"]
playbook.followTopMiners: Track the SOMA platform dashboard and competition announcements, taostats.io/subnet/114 weight distribution, repo commit cadence (active rules in miner/README_prompting.md), and validator docs for workload changes.

playbook.whatItDoes: Everyframe routes paid media-generation jobs: a coordinator dispatches generation work (45 model contracts across video/image/audio providers like Fal, OpenRouter, MiniMax, Runway, Luma, ElevenLabs) to miners' attested cloud workers, which call the providers and return signed completion receipts. Miners bid on model offers; customers get routed generation, miners earn alpha.
playbook.hardwareRec: No GPU - the worker runs as an attested Phala Cloud workload and explicitly does not run models locally. You need a funded Phala Cloud account plus funded generation-provider API accounts; example compute ceiling $0.06/hr, storage billed separately.
playbook.keyRequirements: ["Registered SN117 hotkey verified at a finalized block (everycli register-hotkey)","Phala Cloud TEE attestation: exact pinned image + KMS transcript before keys enable","At least one funded provider of the nine supported generation providers","Staged activation: init -> deploy -> activate -> resume (with admissions)","Model offers/bids: you set discount % against the base miner reward"]
playbook.minerJob: Install everycli, save provider keys locally, and deploy the digest-pinned worker to Phala (deploy refuses if the quote exceeds your --max-hourly-usd ceiling). The coordinator sends generation jobs; your worker calls the configured providers and returns signed receipts, never seeing your hotkey private key. You publish offers on enabled models (optionally discounted to win traffic) and track earnings/balances via the CLI; coordinator accounting is separate from validator weight submission and on-chain alpha emission. Stop/start/reconcile manage the lifecycle; attestation failures or missing heartbeats block work.
playbook.minerJobProvide: ["Attested generation-job completion capacity","Signed completion receipts per job","Competitively discounted model offers","Clean attestation and heartbeat posture"]
playbook.top10Strategy: It's a price/availability market, not a compute benchmark: profit = reward minus provider cost, and you control the discount lever. Offer models where your provider rates are cheap and demand is live (check everycli offers for enabled models), maintain several providers for coverage, and keep the attested worker admitted 24/7. Watch spend - traffic is not guaranteed and provider bills don't drop when you discount.
playbook.top10Levers: ["Provider cost arbitrage (cheap rates vs base reward)","Discount % tuning to win traffic","Multi-provider coverage of enabled models","Attestation/uptime reliability","Phala hosting cost control (max-hourly ceiling)"]
playbook.followTopMiners: everycli offers/earnings/balances for live market state; coordinator accounting; taostats.io/subnets/117 weights; repo releases (worker release notes, new model contracts).

playbook.whatItDoes: Ditto incentivizes agent memory harnesses: miners submit a Docker build context implementing a public harness HTTP contract (any language); validators screen each image and run it in isolated sandboxes, scoring it on DittoBench - tool-calling and memory recall. 100% of miner emission follows the king-of-the-hill ranking; with no eligible miners, emission burns.
playbook.hardwareRec: No GPU - you submit code, validators run it. Build a Docker context implementing the HTTP contract in Rust/Python/TS/Go; a dev box plus the ditto CLI suffices. Practice offline with the starter kit and playground before submitting.
playbook.keyRequirements: ["Docker build context implementing the public harness HTTP contract (platform screening precedes scoring)","Scored on DittoBench: tool-calling and memory recall","Submit via ditto upload --path agent.tar.gz; pre-flight with ditto verify","King-of-the-hill ranking takes 100% of miner emission; zero eligible miners = burn","Wallet rotations need owner-links proof of operator identity"]
playbook.minerJob: Day-to-day you are building a memory harness: an HTTP service the validator's sandbox calls during DittoBench runs, handling tool calls and recalling context across a task. Package the tarball, run ditto verify pre-flight, upload, and poll ditto status. Validators screen, sandbox, and score each image against the deterministic DittoBench datasets; only the king-of-the-hill rank position earns emission.
playbook.minerJobProvide: ["A sandbox-safe memory-harness HTTP service","High DittoBench tool-calling and memory-recall scores","Submission tarballs that pass platform screening","A king-of-the-hill-ranked agent each cycle"]
playbook.top10Strategy: King-of-the-hill means being marginally better than the current #1 is everything - measure against the offline DittoBench practice loop (deterministic datasets in research/dittobench-datagen) before every upload. Focus on memory recall over long horizons and robust tool-calling; the starter kit is your baseline and the coding starter kit offers free shadow practice. Upload only on a verified local win.

playbook.whatItDoes: An incentive network for training-data improvement: miners generate bounded synthetic or licensed data patches (initially math and natural sciences) with record-level provenance; validators verify rights, privacy, lineage and contamination, then train a frozen baseline with each patch and reward measured capability improvements. Quality gains — not dataset size or compute — earn TAO.
playbook.hardwareRec: No GPU requirement stated in the repo. Patch generation likely leans on LLM API budgets rather than local GPUs; the train-and-evaluate comparisons run validator-side under identical conditions.
playbook.keyRequirements: ["Bounded data patches with record-level provenance","Appropriate usage rights mandatory (no unlicensed material)","No private info or real-minor data","Pass contamination/leakage/duplication checks","Patches tested against a frozen baseline","Objective subjects first: math + natural sciences"]
playbook.minerJob: Produce candidate data patches — synthetic or licensed examples with answers, reasoning steps, calculations and explanations for learning-oriented tasks — carrying provenance metadata per record. Validators run a GENERATE → VERIFY → TRAIN → EVALUATE → REWARD pipeline: they check rights, privacy, lineage, duplication and evaluation leakage, then fine-tune a frozen baseline with your patch under identical training and evaluation conditions. Rewards are proportional to measurable improvements in factual accuracy, reasoning quality, calibration, clear age-appropriate communication and safety without unnecessary refusal.
playbook.minerJobProvide: ["Synthetic/licensed training-data patches","Record-level provenance metadata","Measured capability improvements vs baseline","Rights-clean, privacy-safe content","Math/science reasoning examples"]
playbook.top10Strategy: It's an A/B-test economy: your patch must beat the frozen baseline under identical training conditions, so prioritize data that moves measurable metrics — worked examples with correct steps and units, calibration pairs, safety-without-refusal cases — over bulk. Contamination or evaluation leakage disqualifies a patch; verify uniqueness before submitting. Start with narrow, objectively-checkable domains where you can demonstrably lift accuracy.
playbook.top10Levers: ["Patches that measurably lift baseline accuracy","Rigorous provenance and rights documentation","Zero contamination/leakage (disqualifying)","High-quality step-level reasoning data","Target weak baseline areas (calibration, safety)","Narrow domains with objective scoring"]

playbook.whatItDoes: Affine (subnet 120) runs a synchronous inference-verification training loop: a checkpoint publishes, miners produce private training batches (math reasoning), artifacts freeze for public audit, verified batches score, and the next checkpoint trains. It is a verifiable training economy - miners sell correctness-attested training compute (TOPLOC-verified batches).
playbook.hardwareRec: 2x H100 80GB or 2x RTX PRO 6000 96GB (miner slots) per platform data. Current qualified inference profile: H200/SM90, FP32 eager, TF32 disabled, torch 2.14.0 + transformers 5.14.1 + toploc 0.1.6. Manifest pins are mandatory.
playbook.keyRequirements: ["Signed Ed25519 activation for your subnet-120 hotkey (no operator whitelist)","Run signed approved source only (affine.io/mining.json authority; subnet.source_bootstrap)","MATH contract: K=1/L=1, at most 3 batches per UID, at most 16 prescribed attempts per task","Upload selected-token logprobs plus TOPLOC (not full-vocabulary arrays); audits check sampler consistency","Match the pinned numerical profile exactly - other hardware/runtime profiles do not qualify","Current pilot is nonpayable (no new-mechanism chain weights) - verify payout status before scaling"]
playbook.minerJob: Run the signed-source miner: activate your Ed25519 identity, bootstrap the approved source pinned at affine.io/mining.json, and generate math training batches under the epoch protocol (checkpoint -> private batches -> freeze/public audit -> verify/score -> train). Batches carry selected-token log probabilities and TOPLOC attestations; audits recheck prescribed sampler consistency, and cheap-eligible unaudited submissions feed training independently. Payout aggregation excludes rejected records. Follow docs/MINER_QUICKSTART.md and the live manifest - the contract pins hardware, packages, and attempt ceilings.
playbook.minerJobProvide: ["Verified math training batches (TOPLOC-attested)","Selected-token logprob uploads within contract limits","Signed-source execution exactly per manifest","Sampler-consistent prescribed attempts","Epoch-to-epoch participation with valid activations"]
playbook.top10Strategy: Strict compliance is the whole game: the manifest pins exact GPU profile, package versions, and attempt limits, and audits reject anything off-spec - most entrants fail on setup, not skill. Get the signed pipeline running cleanly first, then optimize batch quality within the 16-attempt ceiling. Watch STATE.md and the evidence checks for what operators actually accept, and confirm real payouts before scaling since the pilot is nonpayable.
playbook.top10Levers: ["Exact manifest compliance (hardware/packages/numerics)","Batch quality within prescribed attempt limits","TOPLOC plus sampler consistency passing audits","Fast epoch turnaround (3 batches per UID)","Monitoring STATE.md and operator evidence channels"]
playbook.followTopMiners: Watch affine.io/llms.txt and the signed OPEN manifest, repo STATE.md plus ops.check_epoch_evidence outputs, taostats.io/subnet/120 weights, and MINER_QUICKSTART.md changes - the contract is versioned aggressively.

playbook.whatItDoes: SN121 (sundae_bar, London-listed Sundae Bar AI PLC) runs rolling AI-development contests for commercial business use. Each Challenge is a real business workflow with a public, auditable eval suite; miners submit SKILL.md files that teach a fixed agent harness the workflow; validators run every submission through the suite and emissions accrue to #1 by time-at-top (40% weight share; 100% burned between Challenges).
playbook.hardwareRec: CPU only: you author SKILL.md files and iterate via the sundae_bar Lab; all evaluation runs on validator infrastructure with per-Challenge model stacks. A laptop suffices — no GPU, no rentals.
playbook.keyRequirements: ["SKILL.md submission via sundae_bar Lab while the Challenge is open","Submission limits: daily (rolling 24h) + per-Challenge caps","Qualifying bar (currently 80%) closes the Challenge","Opaque anti-gaming gates (skill_alignment, dataset_derived) zero exploit submissions","Winner-takes-most: emissions follow time at #1, not a single payout"]
playbook.minerJob: Download the Challenge bundle (suite.yaml, dataset.jsonl, rubric.txt), author a SKILL.md teaching the base agent the procedure, and submit through the Lab. Validators load your skill into the fixed harness across multiple scenarios and score with weighted graders — skill_use 30%, scenario_quality 30%, rubric/model-judge 30%, deterministic novelty 10% — publishing per-test rationales you can download and iterate against. On-chain weights track the current #1; between Challenges, 100% of miner emissions burn.
playbook.minerJobProvide: ["SKILL.md files per open Challenge","Submissions passing the opaque anti-gaming gates","Scores clearing the 80% qualifying bar","Sustained #1 time across weight-setting cycles"]
playbook.top10Strategy: Speed-run skill engineering: the suite is public and auditable, so the winner is whoever reverse-engineers grader weights and iterates fastest within submission limits. Being early-and-good beats perfect-and-late since #1 accrues by time. Newcomers: study grader rationales obsessively, avoid template boilerplate (novelty gate), and save daily submissions for genuine improvements.
playbook.top10Levers: ["Skill-writing quality (procedures, not templates)","Fast response at Challenge open","Grader-rationale-driven iteration","Novelty/anti-gaming gate avoidance","Submission-budget discipline (daily + per-Challenge)"]
playbook.followTopMiners: Watch the sundae_bar Lab challenge pages and leaderboards, taostats validator rewards for 5EL9y2gdesAcPiPmoyFKABToiui3RkXewiKxdTMmes34ZdNf (weight extrinsics show the #1), and repo/Lab for new Challenge drops.

playbook.whatItDoes: CookingTAO (SN122) is a meta-subnet: developers submit mining code for other Bittensor subnets to the platform; users deploy that code to mine those subnets, and the SN122 validator rewards developer code by attributable user earnings (90%) and adoption (10%). Participants earn by writing miners that other people run profitably.
playbook.hardwareRec: CPU only for SN122 itself - it is a validator-only process (a small host runs it). Submitted mining code runs on target subnets with whatever hardware those require. Developers need no GPU; users deploying code need per-subnet hardware.
playbook.keyRequirements: ["Submit a GitHub repo of working miner code via prod.cookingtao.com (only supported subnets are listed)","Code review covers compatibility, reproducible install/execution, security (no embedded keys/undisclosed collection), licensing","Participant hotkey needs >1,000 alpha staked on SN122 to receive validator weight (fixed policy; UID 0 is the burn sink)","Rewards: 90% performance (attributable user earnings) + 10% adoption; anti-concentration and multi-submission penalties apply","Only five code listings per supported subnet - maintain your code or lose the slot"]
playbook.minerJob: There is no miner daemon on SN122: registered participants are developer-miners. You write or port a miner for a supported subnet, submit it through the platform, pass verification, and - if selected among the top five per subnet - it is listed for users to deploy. The validator pulls platform adoption/earnings data, reads target-subnet metagraphs, computes developer rewards, and sets weights (weight only for hotkeys with >1,000 alpha staked; filtered weight routes to UID 0 burn).
playbook.minerJobProvide: ["Working, documented miner code for supported target subnets","Security-clean submissions (no credentials, no hidden behavior)","Ongoing maintenance as target-subnet protocols change","Miners that generate attributable user earnings on the platform"]
playbook.top10Strategy: Ship the best-performing miner code for the highest-earning supported subnets - your score is users' attributable earnings, so reliable profitable miners beat clever-but-fragile ones. Grab one of five slots per subnet early, keep code updated as targets evolve, and stake >1,000 alpha so your score actually converts to weight.
playbook.top10Levers: ["Target high-emission subnets where your miner wins user earnings","Slot scarcity: five listings per subnet - approval speed and quality matter","Maintenance: track target-subnet protocol changes and update fast",">1,000 alpha stake on your SN122 hotkey - hard requirement for weight","Use the W&B validator dashboard to sanity-check reward calculations","Respect anti-concentration rules; diversify rather than spam submissions"]
playbook.followTopMiners: Watch the wandb.ai/cookingtao/CookingTAO-Subnet validator dashboard, prod.cookingtao.com listing/earnings pages, taostats.io/subnets/122, and Discord (epic.tensor) for new supported-subnet announcements.

playbook.whatItDoes: MANTIS is 'The Ultimate Signal Machine': miners publish encrypted financial-prediction payloads (ETH direction, FX binaries, volatility paths, multi-asset breakouts, cross-sectional rankings, funding rates, FLOW bracket trades). Validators sample payloads every 5 blocks, decrypt after a Drand timelock matures, and score walk-forward salience into on-chain weights.
playbook.hardwareRec: 1x RTX 4090 per input metadata, though signal generation is light (torch/scikit-learn); any reliable box producing payloads on cadence works. Real requirements are quant skill and, for FLOW challenges, posted on-chain capital.
playbook.keyRequirements: ["V2 JSON payloads on Cloudflare R2 (object key = your hotkey, <=25MB)","Dual-path encryption: owner X25519 + Drand IBE timelock (BLS12-381), binding hash AAD","Challenges weighted: MULTI-BREAKOUT 5.0, FUNDING-XSEC 4.0, ETH-LBFGS 3.5, XSEC-RANK 3.0","FLOW: post real bets on the FlowCollateralPool contract; t>=1.25 significance gate","BURN_PCT 0.35 to UID 0; uniqueness/anti-Sybil penalties on duplicates"]
playbook.minerJob: Run your signal pipeline (generate_and_encrypt.py / flow_post.py are the supported surfaces): produce predictions/embeddings per challenge, encrypt dual-path so nobody sees them pre-maturation, and upload to R2. Validators decrypt via Drand after the window, store (embedding, price) pairs in SQLite, and compute walk-forward salience - L2 logistic/ElasticNet importance, top-K selection, uniqueness penalties for >85% argmax overlap, EMA smoothing (alpha 0.15) - then set weights. FLOW works differently: you post bracket trades (direction, Kelly fraction, stops) with your own collateral on-chain; cleared keys split the pool pro rata, uncleared keys get 2% dust, rest burns.
playbook.minerJobProvide: ["Timely encrypted prediction payloads every sampling window","Statistically salient signals (walk-forward AUC > 0.5)","De-correlated predictions (uniqueness penalties)","FLOW bracket trades with posted collateral"]
playbook.top10Strategy: Genuine out-of-sample edge, not volume: salience is regression-coefficient importance, so de-correlated, unique signals beat clones (Sybil clones split weight; duplicates get zeroed). Concentrate skill on the high-weight challenges (BREAKOUT/FUNDING/LBFGS). FLOW needs real capital and a hard significance gate (t>=1.25 full-history or rolling) - post-sized bets, don't spray. The Model Iteration Tool repo is the sanctioned backtesting path.
playbook.top10Levers: ["True predictive edge on high-weight challenges","Uniqueness/de-correlation vs other miners","Consistent payload cadence (SAMPLE_EVERY=5 blocks)","FLOW capital efficiency + significance gate","Walk-forward validation before submitting"]
playbook.followTopMiners: taostats.io/subnets/123 weights (platform data: ~248/256 earned, broad distribution); MANTIS site settlement console (FLOW books, public recomputation); FLOW_RELEASE.pdf; repo MINER_GUIDE.md and Model Iteration Tool.

playbook.whatItDoes: Swarm is an open arena for drone-pilot AI: miners train control/RL models that fly simulated drones - depth camera and flight state in, flight commands out - across five missions (pursuit, search-and-rescue, autopilot, swarm teamwork). Every 14-day epoch benchmarks 1,000 fresh procedural worlds per mission; king-of-the-hill pays the last five champions per mission.
playbook.hardwareRec: CPU-only for the lightweight miner process (package + upload; digest committed on-chain); training RL policies (SB3/PyTorch/ONNX) realistically wants a GPU (RTX 3090/4090-class) for iteration speed. Local benchmark with --workers 4 runs CPU; rentals fine. One-shot submission per model per mission.
playbook.keyRequirements: ["Model packaged via swarm model package (SB3, PyTorch, or ONNX archive)","One shot per drone per mission - the slot locks once scored","Policy consumes depth camera plus flight state at 50Hz and outputs flight commands","Local benchmark mirrors validator scoring; epoch seeds stay secret until close","Score: 45% success + 45% speed + 10% safety (pursuit missions: half success, half speed)"]
playbook.minerJob: Train a drone pilot (RL/imitation with SB3/PyTorch), package it with the swarm CLI, and submit - the miner process commits the model digest on-chain and uploads the archive to the Swarm backend, then exits. Validators run your model across 1,000 fresh worlds per mission per epoch and rank the average; rewards follow king-of-the-hill, paying the last five champions per mission weighted by how much they raised the record.
playbook.minerJobProvide: ["Trained flight-policy model (SB3/PyTorch/ONNX archive)","High average success/speed/safety across 1,000 unseen worlds","Per-mission champion submissions across five families","On-chain committed model digests"]
playbook.top10Strategy: Generalization beats memorization: epochs use fresh seeds, so train on procedural variety (swarm-worlds maps) and validate locally with the same simulator. Mission reward shares differ (Interceptor 30%, swarm missions 20%, others 15%) - pick a less-contested mission. King-of-the-hill pays the last five champions, so one genuine breakthrough keeps earning. Newcomers: master Autopilot or SAR locally before burning a one-shot submission.
playbook.top10Levers: ["RL generalization across procedural worlds","Choosing lower-competition mission families","Success+speed balance (90% of score) with a safety floor","One-shot submission discipline (locked slots)","KOTH payout persistence for record-setters","Local benchmark parity with the validator scoring path"]
playbook.followTopMiners: Watch the live leaderboard (swarm124.com/benchmark), taostats.io/subnets/124 champion UIDs, swarm-subnet/swarm and swarm-worlds release tags (map/mission changes), and the Swarm Discord.

playbook.whatItDoes: An incentivized ML-research network: miners submit optimizer code; validators train a ~360M Llama-style model with it under a fixed B200 budget (≤20 h, FineWeb-Edu) and score validation loss. Confirmed improvements beyond an adaptive bar (floor 0.03 nats) earn credit with a 14-day half-life. First research target: better gradient descent.
playbook.hardwareRec: No GPU needed merely to serve a submission — the validator's B200 runs scored runs (B200 is the only SKU allowed to score; 180 GB VRAM class). Real research requires your own training compute (A100/H100-class realistic).
playbook.keyRequirements: ["Optimizer code per sn125/miner_template.py interface","Serve source from registered hotkey; commit source hash","Fund evaluation credits (fee ≈ rental cost +10%)","Both initial and confirmation runs must qualify","Linux + Python 3.12 dedicated environment","Improvement must exceed the adaptive bar (≥0.03 nats)","Verify production identity/treasury before paying"]
playbook.minerJob: Implement an optimizer in Python against the template interface, test it against matched controls on your own compute, then serve its source from your miner hotkey and fund evaluation credits for the round. Validators verify the committed source hash, run the scored training contract (360M model, seq 2,048, batch 32, ≤188k steps on one B200), and confirm promising candidates with a second validator-funded run. Credit scales with improvement size and decays with a 14-day half-life; rewards are shared by credit weight and unearned emission burns.
playbook.minerJobProvide: ["Novel optimizer source code","Locally validated loss improvements","Hash-committed, revealable submissions","Evaluation-credit funding per round","Reproducible research evidence"]
playbook.top10Strategy: Pure research competition: study the signed round contract before spending (historical reference numbers are not live targets), and only submit candidates that clear the adaptive improvement bar in your own matched-control tests — failed paid evaluations are pure loss. Compounding wins matter: confirmed optimizers become the frontier others must beat, so iteration speed on the learning-rate-schedule/update-rule search space (including LLM research agents) is the real edge.
playbook.top10Levers: ["Genuinely novel update rules / LR schedules","Local matched-control testing before paying","Compute for rapid candidate iteration","Credit-budget economics (fee vs expected value)","Track signed round announcements + live frontier","Build on confirmed prior winners","LLM research agents to widen the search"]
playbook.followTopMiners: Track the Refinery dashboard/artifact publications, signed round announcements (fee + treasury), the MINING.md economics section, taostats.io/subnet/125 rewards distribution, and Barbariandev/refinery commit cadence.

playbook.whatItDoes: Astrid (subnet 127) runs trading competitions on its Arena platform: miners trade, validators independently replay every trade to compute PnL rankings, and on-chain weights pay the top-3 of each completed competition 60/30/10 of that competition's emission share (the rest burns). This repo is the validator daemon only; miners participate via the Astrid Arena (arena-api.astrid.global).
playbook.hardwareRec: CPU only - the miner is a trader on the Arena platform; the validator does the heavy trade-replay compute. Watch the trade-activity and execution-run correlation eligibility rules, which disqualify sloppy execution.
playbook.keyRequirements: ["Compete in Astrid Arena trading competitions; completed ones enter a delayed-emissions payout window","Top-3 eligible participants by replayed PnL earn 60/30/10 of EMISSIONS_PERCENT per competition","The remainder of each competition's allocation burns (UID 0)","Eligibility: trade activity plus execution-run correlation (disqualified participants filtered)","The validator replays all trades independently - reported PnL must match replayed PnL"]
playbook.minerJob: Miners register on the Astrid Arena platform and compete in periodic trading competitions; all trades and execution runs are recorded via the public Arena API. After a competition completes and enters its payout window, validators fetch every trade, run eligibility checks (activity plus execution correlation), replay them to compute true PnL, and rank the top three - weights go on-chain 60/30/10. Your day-to-day is building a trading edge on the Arena; rewards are strictly competition-outcome-based.
playbook.minerJobProvide: ["Competition trades with matching execution runs","Positive replayed PnL versus other participants","Eligibility compliance (activity + correlation)","Top-3 finishes per competition to earn"]
playbook.top10Strategy: Winner-take-most per competition (60/30/10) means you need podium finishes, not median performance. Study which competitions have thin fields, manage risk so replayed PnL stays clean - disqualification wipes you - and iterate strategy per market. Because validators replay everything, execution integrity matters as much as alpha. Newcomers should paper-trade the Arena first and enter competitions with the fewest strong regulars.
playbook.top10Levers: ["Competition selection (field strength varies)","Clean execution runs passing correlation checks","Risk-managed strategies that avoid disqualification","PnL consistency to reach top-3 repeatedly","Tracking platform and eligibility rule changes"]
playbook.followTopMiners: Track the Arena's completed-competitions endpoint and leaderboards (arena-api.astrid.global), taostats.io/subnet/127 weight flows after each payout window, and astridintelligence/sn-127 commits - emission parameters are hardcoded in src/core/arena/constants.ts.

playbook.whatItDoes: ByteLeap (SN128) is a distributed compute platform whose miner is the resource-aggregation component: miners connect worker machines to the network and earn through active compute leases and computational challenges. Lease revenue is 100% of the score, multiplied by an availability factor based on 169-hour online presence. Validators coordinate, challenge, and set weights.
playbook.hardwareRec: No fixed GPU spec published: score is lease-revenue-driven, so what matters is worker machines that actually rent; the miner process is lightweight (Python 3.8+). Workers deploy separately via the byteleap-Worker repo. Max 100 workers per miner.
playbook.keyRequirements: ["Registered hotkey + miner config (config/miner_config.yaml)","Workers deployed separately via byteleap-Worker repo (WebSocket 1:N)","Max 100 workers per miner; challenges target only unleased workers","Idle workers score zero on the lease-revenue component","169-hour online presence for the availability multiplier"]
playbook.minerJob: Run scripts/run_miner.py (or PM2): the miner connects to SN128 validators, aggregates worker resources over WebSocket, routes compute tasks and cryptographic challenges (Merkle-tree verification protocols), and collects results from workers running system monitoring, challenge execution, VMGW sessions and Libvirt management. Final score sums all worker performance (capped at 100), driven by active compute leases integrated with marketplace APIs; idle capacity earns nothing.
playbook.minerJobProvide: ["Aggregated worker fleet (up to 100 per miner)","Active compute leases — the entire scoring input","Challenge results with Merkle-proof verification","169-hour sustained availability"]
playbook.top10Strategy: Utilization play, not benchmark play: keep workers leased and online — lease revenue is the whole score and availability multiplies it. Newcomers: start with a few worker machines that demonstrably rent, keep them challenged and healthy, then scale toward the 100-worker cap only as utilization holds.
playbook.top10Levers: ["Worker machines that win leases","Uptime (169h availability multiplier)","Worker count scaling toward the 100 cap","Challenge pass reliability","Competitive worker pricing on the marketplace"]
playbook.followTopMiners: Track taostats.io/subnet/128 for weight distribution, the byteleapai org (byteleap-Worker repo) for worker-side changes, and release cadence of byteleap-Miner.
